greenhouse:globalrelay:6103166004.description:
Who we are: 

 For over 25 years, Global Relay has set the standard in enterprise information archiving with industry-leading cloud archiving, surveillance, eDiscovery, and analytics solutions. We securely capture and preserve the communications data of the world’s most highly regulated firms, giving them greater visibility and control over their information and ensuring compliance with stringent regulations.

 Though we offer competitive compensation and benefits and all the other perks one would expect from an established company, we are not your typical technology company. Global Relay is a career-building company. A place for big ideas. New challenges. Groundbreaking innovation. It’s a place where you can genuinely make an impact – and be recognized for it.

 We believe great businesses thrive on diversity, inclusion, and the contributions of all employees. To that end, we recruit candidates from different backgrounds and foster a work environment that encourages employees to collaborate and learn from each other, completely free of barriers.

 Your role: 

 The Senior Manager, Financial Reporting is a critical leadership role within Finance and Accounting, responsible for ensuring the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of financial reporting across all global entities. This role owns the consolidated and statutory financial reporting processes, serves as the primary liaison with external auditors, and maintains a robust control environment that scales with Global Relay’s growth. The Senior Manager, Financial Reporting acts as a bridge between operational finance and strategic leadership, translating complex financial data into actionable insights that inform executive decision-making. You will lead and develop a team of financial reporting professionals while driving improvements to processes and systems. The right candidate brings deep technical expertise, leadership experience, and a practical, solutions-oriented approach to a business that is growing on an international scale.

 Your responsibilities:  

- Financial Close & Reporting

- Lead and oversee the financial month-end close process, ensuring timely and accurate completion of month-end milestones, working cross-functionally with the Financial Reporting, Tax, AP, Billing, and Payroll teams

- Own the timely and accurate preparation and review of monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements and reporting packages for key stakeholders

- Oversee the integrity of transaction processing and general ledger maintenance, ensuring robust internal controls are maintained

- Drive a culture of operational efficiency and reporting accuracy, focused on continually reducing reporting turnaround times

- Champion continual process and system improvement to meaningfully reduce financial close times

- Audits & Statutory Reporting

- Lead the preparation and review of standalone financial statements for all foreign subsidiaries (USA, UK, Sweden, Spain, China, Australia, Netherlands and Singapore)

- Own the consolidated and statutory audit processes for all subsidiaries of Global Relay, acting as the primary liaison for external auditors and accounting service providers

- Lead the compilation and review of ad hoc data extracts and reports in response to various inquiries from management, customers, auditors, regulatory authorities and other government agencies

- Financial Presentation & Analysis

- Develop, monitor, and report on Key Performance Indicators on a timely basis to senior management, ensuring ongoing relevance to reflect changing business needs

- Lead monthly variance analysis between actuals and budget/forecast, providing strategic insights and actionable recommendations to senior management

- Assist other senior Finance & Accounting management in the preparation and maintenance of annual budgets and cash flow forecasts

- Partner with the VP Finance in supervising and reviewing FP&A activities performed by the Business Analysis function within Finance & Accounting

- Technical Accounting & Internal Controls

- Interpret and apply complex accounting standards for new or unusual transactions; provide recommendations and document conclusions

- Champion the accurate and timely review of complex revenue recognition analyses, including multi-element arrangements, subscription models, usage-based billing, and long-term contracts

- Maintain and enhance the company’s accounting policies, ensuring compliance with changes in accounting standards or regulatory requirements

- Prepare and/or review annual or ad hoc accounting memos and analyses as required

- Leadership & Process Improvement

- Scale the financial reporting function and internal controls of Global Relay as its international footprint expands, balancing local reporting and accounting requirements with parent consolidated reporting requirements

- Continually focus on the upskilling and development of other Financial Reporting team members

- Champion data integrity and continuous enhancement of reporting systems, ensuring consistency across global entities

 About you:  

- Qualified professional accountant (CPA) with a strong work ethic and integrity

- A minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance, with at least 3 years in a senior management or equivalent leadership role

- Demonstrated excellence in managing finance teams with a focus on mentoring and developing team members to achieve operational excellence

- Strong knowledge of ASPE and IFRS (or US GAAP) with demonstrated ability to interpret and apply complex accounting standards

- Comprehensive experience in multi-entity and multi-currency consolidation structures

- Familiarity with foreign GAAPs (e.g. USA, UK, Sweden, etc.) is an asset but is not a firm requirement; willingness to learn and master jurisdiction-specific accounting standards as Global Relay grows is essential

- Ability and appetite to navigate a dynamic, high-growth, entrepreneurial environment, while maintaining accuracy and control discipline

- Proven history of excellence and timeliness in external and internal financial reporting

- Comfort working with large data sets, including the ability to validate, reconcile, and analyze data efficiently

- Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities with experience in researching and preparing technical accounting memos

- Advanced level MS Excel proficiency, with advanced knowledge of Word and PowerPoint

- Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to multi-task, prioritize and manage time

- Impeccable accuracy with numbers and attention to detail

- Clear understanding of financial KPIs for SaaS businesses

- Demonstrated discretion and sound judgment in handling confidential information

 Differentiators: 

- Experience in full cycle accounting in a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) environment

- Deep experience with NetSuite ERP, including multi-entity configurations

- Demonstrated track record of process improvement and system optimization that reduced reporting turnaround times

 Working conditions: 

- Able to work hours as necessary to complete job requirements

 Compensation: 

 Global Relay advertises the pay range for this role in compliance with British Columbia’s pay transparency laws. Individual pay rates are determined by evaluating factors such as expertise, skills, education, and professional background. 

 The range below reflects the expected annual base salary, which is only one element of our comprehensive total rewards package designed to reflect our company pay philosophy, culture and values. We aim to foster an inspiring work environment and support employees' work-life rhythms. We provide a comprehensive extended health benefits program, including virtual healthcare and a wellness allowance. Employees also receive annual allotted vacation days, which increase based on tenure. Other benefits include: Paid sick days, maternity/parental enhancement program, bonus, and an RRSP contribution matching program. 

 For Vancouver-based employees, we provide a subsidized meal program, courtesy of our talented in-house culinary team!

 British Columbia - Base salary range
 $120,000 — $165,000 CAD 

 What you can expect: 

 At Global Relay, there’s no ceiling to what you can achieve. It’s the land of opportunity for the energetic, the intelligent, the driven. You’ll receive the mentoring, coaching, and support you need to reach your career goals. You’ll be part of a culture that breeds creativity and rewards perseverance and hard work. And you’ll be working alongside smart, talented individuals from diverse backgrounds, with complementary knowledge and skills.

 Global Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

 We seek to ensure reasonable adjustments, accommodations, and personal time are tailored to meet the unique needs of every individual.

 To learn more about our business, culture, and community involvement, visit www.globalrelay.com .

Location Details: Canada - Ontario

 At GoDaddy the future of work looks different for each team. Some teams work in the office full-time; others have a hybrid arrangement (they work remotely some days and in the office some days) and some work entirely remotely.

 This is a remote position in Ontario Canada, so you’ll be working remotely from your home. You may occasionally visit a GoDaddy office to meet with your team for events or meetings.

 Join our team 

 GoDaddy is on a mission to empower small and medium entrepreneurs to sell anywhere. GoDaddy Payments plays a key role by enabling GoDaddy customers to accept payments across channels with some of the lowest processing fees in the industry.

 As a Principal Product Manager on the GoDaddy Commerce team, you will lead the strategy and development of merchant capital products. You will define the end-to-end experience and platform capabilities that enable GoDaddy customers to qualify for, access, and manage working capital.

 You will have the opportunity to build and scale a GoDaddy-controlled capital offering while balancing merchant experience, credit risk, regulatory requirements, and business performance. Your work will directly affect the growth and profitability of GoDaddy Commerce.

 What you'll get to do... 

- Define the product strategy, business case, and delivery roadmap for Capital on Us, a GoDaddy-controlled merchant capital offering.

 Your experience should include... 

- 7+ years of product management experience building and scaling customer-facing or platform products.

- Experience building credit, lending, merchant capital, or other financial products involving underwriting, decisioning, funding, or portfolio management.

- Solid understanding of how customer experience, credit policy, risk management, operations, and unit economics work together in a lending product.

- Experience partnering with Engineering and Data teams to build technically complex platforms, decisioning capabilities, models, and customer experiences.

- Demonstrated ability to lead across Risk, Credit, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Design, and Go-to-Market teams.

- Strong analytical and communication skills, including the ability to analyze trade-offs, define product economics, make decisions with incomplete information, and explain complex issues to senior leaders.

- Ability to drive clarity, decisions, and execution across globally distributed teams without direct authority.

 You might also have... 

- Experience building financial products for small businesses or entrepreneurs.

- Experience launching products across multiple markets or regulatory environments.

- Experience integrating third-party financial services into a broader product ecosystem.

- Familiarity with data science or machine-learning applications in credit decisioning, fraud prevention, or personalization.

- Experience using JIRA, QuickSight, FullStory, or similar product-development and analytics tools.

 About us... GoDaddy is empowering everyday entrepreneurs around the world by providing the help and tools to succeed online, making opportunity more inclusive for all. Our mission is to give our customers the tools, insights, and people to transform their ideas and personal initiative into success. To learn more about the company, visit About Us .

But we also know that’s not enough to build true equity and belonging in our communities. That’s why we prioritize integrating diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging principles into the core of how we work every day—focusing not only on our employee experience, but also our customer experience and operations. It’s the best way to serve our mission of empowering entrepreneurs everywhere, and making opportunity more inclusive for all. To read more about these commitments, as well as our representation and pay equity data, check out our Diversity and Pay Parity annual report which can be found on our Diversity Careers page .

 We also embrace our diverse culture and offer a range of Employee Resource Groups ( Culture ). Have a side hustle? No problem. We love entrepreneurs! Most importantly, come as you are and make your own way.

 GoDaddy is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. GoDaddy will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with local and federal requirements. Refer to our full EEO policy. 

 Our recruiting team is available to assist you in completing your application. If they could be helpful, please reach out to myrecruiter@godaddy.com.

 GoDaddy doesn’t accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. 
 Compensation & Benefits   

 What We Offer:   

 Working at GoDaddy offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, parental leave, healthcare, retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.   

 This role may be eligible to participate in GoDaddy's equity plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, critical illness, AD&D, health care spending account, employee assistance program, paid sick time, paid personal time, paid parental leave, remote work options, paid holidays, paid Wellness days, employee stock purchase plan; and other benefits in accordance with GoDaddy's benefit plans and applicable law.

- Requires experience with various computer systems to prepare and develop financial reports.

- Perform miscellaneous duties and tasks such as necessary to process joint use agreements or under take special studies of a clerical or technical nature. May perform work of subordinates as necessary to maintain schedules etc.

 Managerial Accountabilities: 
Manage the unit and achieve the approved programs and targeted results through:

- Maintaining a team of subordinates who are capable of producing the outputs required.

- Ensure subordinates are able and willing to produce the desired output, and that subordinate managers continually improve the processes for achieving the outputs.

- Assess staff capability to do the required work, now and in the future.

- Conduct personal effectiveness reviews of subordinates managers/specialists to build relationships and trust, and to improve effectiveness.

- Set an effective framework of policies and procedures for the work of the unit.

- Know and ensure own and subordinates’ compliance with all legal and regulatory requirements, and all corporate policies and procedures, and generally accepted practices relating to the work of the unit.

- Establish a two-way working relationship with subordinates to solicit their views on conditions and potential changes affecting their work, and continuous improvement opportunities.

- Requires a knowledge of customer operations sufficient to lead a staff of mixed trades.

- Requires a knowledge of project management and human relations to negotiate effectively with customers and the public, a knowledge of computer applications related to distribution network systems.

greenhouse:instacart:8146070.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry 

 At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. 

 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

 Instacart is a Flex First team 

 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. 

 Why this role is on the menu

 Most companies are layering AI onto existing processes. This role is about something different: rebuilding those processes from the ground up, so teams can do work that actually matters.

 Instacart's Marketing team has set ambitious AI goals — and this is the person who makes them real. You'll be the first role of this kind in Marketing, embedded in the org with a clear mandate: identify what's slow, manual, or broken across the Marketing organization and rebuild it into something fundamentally better. The benchmark isn't marginal improvement. It's transformation — building solutions that make people wonder how they ever worked without them.

 This is a builder role. Strategy is a means to an end. The end is something shipped, adopted, and measurable. You'll also be the connective tissue for Marketing's AI ambitions — convening the people who own AI goals, unblocking what's stuck, and creating internal momentum that makes the whole org move faster.

 What you'll cook up in your first year

 Building (60%)

- Identify high-impact workflows, systems, and processes across Marketing that are slow, manual, or duct-taped together — and rebuild them AI-natively, from the ground up

- Own the full cycle: understand the current state, design the solution, build it, ship it — then measure what changed. Establish the before, prove the after, and make the case to leadership

- Walk in with work already queued. Early builds include:

- Recurring leadership and planning narratives — transforming how Marketing produces its MBR, quarterly planning summaries, budget variance write-ups, and channel performance narratives; currently manual synthesis across multiple inputs, rebuilt into a faster, more consistent, AI-native output

- Integrated campaign launch process — automating key steps from campaign ideation to launch, reducing the manual handoffs and coordination overhead that slow campaigns down across teams

- Brief quality and standardization — an AI review layer that evaluates briefs before they leave the building, flags what's missing or unclear, and raises input quality across the org before downstream teams absorb the cost of a bad brief

- Build with portability in mind — your solutions should be constructed so others can pick them up, adapt them for their own context, and extend what you've built without starting from scratch; you're not just solving a problem, you're creating infrastructure others can build on

- Develop and maintain an intake framework: gather inputs from across the org, evaluate feasibility and impact, and make a defensible call on what gets built next — including what doesn't; prioritization discipline means saying no to low-value requests as readily as yes to high-value ones

 Driving Adoption (20%) 

- Own the change management side of every build: create the conditions for people to trust what you've built, use it consistently, and not revert to old habits when something feels unfamiliar

- Evangelize internally — write up wins, build case studies, show other teams what's possible; your goal is to generate more demand than you can supply, which means the org needs to see what AI can actually do, not just hear about it

- Create energy around AI across Marketing — not as a cheerleader, but as someone who shows people things they didn't know were possible and makes it easy for them to take the next step

 Orchestration & Thought Partnership (20%) 

- Lead the MarComms AI KR forum: convene AI KR owners across Marketing, create momentum behind shared goals, surface blockers, and hold the operating cadence

- Act as a working partner to AI goal owners — unblocking vendor delays, solving capability gaps, helping people get unstuck

 The secret ingredients we're looking for

 Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications) 

- 7+ years in marketing operations, marketing strategy, or a closely adjacent discipline — you understand how marketing orgs work, where the friction lives, and what it costs to leave it unfixed

- Proven builder with a track record of impact — you have shipped AI-powered workflows and processes that demonstrably changed how teams work; you can name the problem, describe the solution, and quantify the result.  You’re so invested in AI that you’ve applied it beyond the scope of your current role.

- Hands-on daily experience with frontier AI tools such as Claude, GPT-4o, or Gemini, including writing prompts that produce reliable, production-quality output at scale

- Experience building agentic systems where AI components interact with each other, including multi-agent design, orchestration layers, and workflows that run without a human in the loop at every step

- An adoption-minded approach to building: designing for adoption from day one and taking accountability for whether what you built actually gets used

- Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain what you're building, why it matters, and where it stands, for audiences from ICs to CMO-level leadership

- Prioritization discipline — you can evaluate a request and tell someone their problem isn't a good AI candidate right now, or that the cost of building outstrips the benefit; you know what not to build

 Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

- A framework for evaluating AI vendors and tools quickly, including running comparison pilots and making principled decisions about what earns a place in the stack

 The Billing Operations Lead oversees and optimizes the end-to-end billing lifecycle across all Instacart Marketplace retailers, ensuring accurate invoicing, compliance with financial controls, and timely month-end close. This role serves as the operational and strategic anchor for the billing team, partnering closely with Finance, BD, Financial Systems, Legal, Product, and Engineering to drive accuracy, scalability, and continuous improvement. 

 The ideal candidate brings deep billing operations experience, strong analytical ability, and a bias for operational excellence — someone equally comfortable mentoring junior team members as they are collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to scope system enhancements and automation opportunities.

 What you'll cook up in your first year

- Billing portfolios across strategic retail partners and multiple revenue streams are owned and operating accurately, with day-to-day billing operations executed with a focus on revenue recognition inputs and timely month-end close.

- Billing policies, SOPs, and quality standards are developed and maintained, with discrepancies and escalations resolved in close partnership with Finance Systems, BD, and Revenue.

- Dashboards, reporting, and KPIs that track billing health are built in collaboration with Finance Systems, enabling continuous improvement and proactive identification of issues.

- Billing system enhancements, integrations, and automation opportunities are scoped and delivered in partnership with Product and Engineering, reducing manual workload and improving operational scalability.

- Internal controls, audit requirements, and contractual billing terms are enforced, with junior team members mentored and billing operations scaled to support Instacart's growth.

 The secret ingredients we're looking for

 Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications) 

- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 5+ years of experience in Billing Operations, Order-to-Cash, or Accounts Receivable within technology, ecommerce, marketplace, or subscription/SaaS environments.

- 2+ years leading cross-functional billing or quote-to-cash projects as an individual contributor, from requirements through UAT and launch.

- Hands-on experience with Salesforce CPQ and at least one billing platform (e.g., Zuora, Chargebee, Stripe Billing) plus one ERP (e.g., NetSuite, SAP, Oracle).

- Proficiency in Excel (pivot tables, lookups) and basic SQL for reconciliations and data analysis.

- Working knowledge of billing controls, SOX requirements, and revenue considerations (e.g., ASC 606) as they apply to invoicing, credits, and adjustments.

 Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

- Aptitude and demonstrated success leveraging AI solutions to improve billing processes.

 Overview

 Instacart's Enterprise Solutions team partners with Global grocery and retail chains to power their digital commerce through StorefrontPro, Enterprise API (Fulfillment and Ads), CarrotAds, and adjacent Enterprise Solutions  products. We're seeking a Director, Customer Success to lead the  Customer Success organization — accountable for post-live value realization  across the enterprise software portfolio.

 In this highly visible role, you will lead senior managers and Customer Success Managers who serve as the strategic advisor of Instacart to retailer executives. You'll own retailer value realization, measured through adoption velocity, time-to-value, health score coverage, at-risk portfolio management, CSAT, and QBR quality across the portfolio. You'll partner closely with Business Development, who owns NRR, GRR, and expansion, by providing account health, risk signal, and expansion readiness. You'll also partner with Enterprise Solutions Delivery, Technology leadership, and Product on portfolio strategy, retailer signal, and roadmap adoption.

 This is a roll-up-your-sleeves leadership opportunity for someone who has personally led the transformation of CS from reactive enablement toward proactive business advisory, can hire and develop senior consultative talent, and thrives in a fast-paced, BD-led commercial environment with shared standards rather than rigid process. The role reports to the Senior Director, Enterprise Solutions , and is remote across the United States and Canada with a preference for proximity to Toronto for key cross-functional collaboration.

 About the Job

- Lead the Customer Success organization for the Enterprise Solutions  portfolio — owning value realization,  outcomes end to end, and partner closely with BD, who owns NRR, GRR, and expansion, by providing account health, risk signal, and expansion readiness.Build and develop a senior consultative CS bench by hiring, sponsoring, and ramping Customer Success Managers  who engage with retailer executives on ecommerce strategy, merchandising, and operations and who can credibly influence retailer P&L outcomes and roadmap adoption.

- Manage senior managers leading segments, setting standards for what good looks like across the CSM’s  — including QBR quality, growth planning, executive engagement, and renewal execution.

- Operate in a BD-led commercial environment as a true commercial peer to BD — preserving BD's ownership of the primary commercial relationship while owning post-sale accountability and surfacing churn, expansion, and escalation signal early and clearly.

- Partner with the Director of Enterprise Architecture & Engineering on shared-account coordination — ensuring the cross-org account team ( CS + Technical Account Managers (TAM’s) ) functions as one team to the retailer despite the functional ownership, with co-authored protocols and clean escalation paths.

- Define and enforce the CSM/TAM boundary based on segmentation — CSM’s lead retailer-executive engagement, value realization, and growth planning, while TAM’s own technical delivery, configuration, and issue resolution, so that CSM capacity stays focused on strategic advisory, not technical execution.

- Own the consultative transformation roadmap — talent strategy, comp structure, operating cadence, and tooling shifts required to evolve CS from a feature-enablement function into a strategic business advisory function.

- Partner with the Director of Retailer Delivery on the implementation-to-success motion as a managed lifecycle (not a document handoff) — ensuring CS is engaged early, named handoff criteria are met, and accounts transition cleanly into early-lifecycle growth ownership.

- Operationalize the retailer segmented  model in CS — applying high-touch coverage and scaled/digital-first models, with clear exception protocols and capacity guardrails.

- Build a structured retailer-signal feedback loop into Product — using CS engagements to surface durable patterns (not anecdotes), instrument adoption of roadmap items, and hold CS accountable for adoption outcomes.

- Apply AI augmentation to scale CS coverage and quality without linear headcount growth — including health monitoring, account-prep automation, QBR/insight generation, and signal triage — partnering with the Technical org on tooling roadmap and adoption.

- Represent the post-sale narrative for the portfolio to senior leadership — integrating retention, growth, churn risk, executive-account temperature, and pipeline outlook — and serve as the Director-level escalation point for retailer relationships when CSM-led engagement is insufficient.

 About You

 Minimum Qualifications

- 8+ years of enterprise customer success, account management, or post-sale leadership at a B2B SaaS or enterprise technology company.

- Direct, accountable leadership of a customer success organization responsible for adoption velocity, time-to-value, health score, at-risk portfolio, CSAT, QBR quality and support BD with GRR, NRR, and expansion.

- Track record of managing managers with demonstrated ability to set standards and develop senior leaders without micromanagement.

- Ownership of a CS book of business or post-sale P&L of meaningful scale (e.g., $1000M+ ARR) with documented outcomes on Adoption, NRR, GRR, or expansion.

- Proven success operating in a BD- or Sales-led commercial environment — clear instinct for where the CS lane begins and ends, comfort with shared standards rather than rigid RACI/process.

- Demonstrated executive presence with enterprise customer counterparts (VP / SVP / C-level), including the ability to deliver hard news, navigate escalations, and rebuild trust after issues.

- Experience designing and operating segmented  CS coverage models (high-touch for strategic accounts, scaled/digital for the long tail), including capacity planning and exception handling.

- Hands-on experience hiring senior CS  talent — with a clear point of view on profile, comp, and ramp.

- Strong background  having operated in an  end to end post sales service delivery ecosystem with strong CS interaction with Business Development/Sales, Delivery, Technical and Product teams. Preferred Qualifications

- Experience transforming a CS function from reactive enablement into proactive business advisory, including the talent, comp, operating-model, and tooling changes required (not a renaming exercise).

- Track record of building or scaling seasoned strategist roles inside a CS org — including hiring profile, ramp, comp design, and integration with the rest of the account team.

- Experience operating with a separate technical TAM function on shared enterprise accounts — including co-authoring cross-org protocols and managing escalations across an org boundary.

- Background applying AI to CS workflows — health monitoring, account preparation, QBR generation, signal triage — with measurable impact on coverage, throughput, or quality.

- Familiarity with the BD/CS interface in commercially complex enterprise sales motions, including renewals, multi-product expansion, and shared-account operating norms.

- Deep familiarity with enterprise retail, grocery, ecommerce platforms, retail media, or adjacent complex B2B domains — including how large retailers evaluate, adopt, and scale technology solutions.

- Experience instrumenting retailer signal into structured product feedback (not anecdotal) and partnering with Product leaders on adoption accountability.

We're transforming the grocery industry 

 At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. 

 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

 Instacart is a Flex First team 

 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. 

 OVERVIEW 

 Every year, people across the world spend nearly one trillion dollars on groceries. But food is more than sustenance — it's identity, ritual, culture, and care. The way we eat shapes our health, our routines, and our relationships. Yet for most people, translating a desire to eat better or live healthier into actual, lasting habit change remains hard.

 The Instacart Consumer team is at the forefront of reimagining how people relate to food at home. We're building new product experiences around meals, nutrition, and health that go beyond the transaction — helping people discover what to cook, build routines that stick, and feel confident in the choices they make for themselves and their families.

 As a Staff Researcher on the Consumer team, you will shape the foundational understanding of how and why people change (or struggle to change) their food behaviors. You'll lead research that spans the full arc from generative discovery to iterative product testing, partnering closely with product, design, data science, marketing, and engineering to build products grounded in deep human insight. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role for a researcher who is as comfortable in the messiness of early-stage innovation as they are in the rigor of quantitative validation.

 ABOUT THE JOB 

- Independently own and drive the research roadmap for the consumer innovation workstream, partnering across product, design, data science, and engineering leadership to surface where research can shape strategy, unlock new opportunities, and push innovation

- Lead generative, foundational research to understand how people think about food, nutrition, and health — including mental models, motivations, barriers, and behavioral triggers

- Apply behavioral science frameworks (e.g., habit loops, nudge theory, behavior change models) to frame research questions and surface insights that fuel creative problem-solving and unlock new directions for product and design

- Execute and oversee rigorous mixed-methods research: qualitative studies (in-depth interviews, ethnographic observation, diary studies, co-creation) alongside quantitative approaches (surveys, behavioral data analysis, concept testing at scale)

- Translate research into compelling, actionable narratives that move stakeholders to decisions, from early-stage opportunity framing to product launch validation

- Own and evolve the team's understanding of the consumer,  maintaining living knowledge bases, personas, and journey maps that the broader organization draws on

- Mentor junior researchers and contribute to the craft, culture, and standards of the Instacart research organization

- Be a visible advocate for the customer across the organization, influencing roadmap and strategy through the quality and clarity of insights

 ABOUT YOU 

 Minimum Qualifications 

- 8+ years conducting UX or consumer research in a product organization, with meaningful experience in early-stage innovation or new product development

- Background or deep familiarity with behavioral psychology, behavioral economics, or related fields - you understand the science of how habits form, persist, and change, and you bring that lens to your work

- Expertise across a wide range of qualitative methodologies: in-depth interviews, ethnographic and diary studies, usability testing, participatory design, and workshop facilitation

- Equally strong with quantitative methods: survey design and analysis, behavioral data interpretation, experimental design, and synthesis across mixed-methods studies

- Proven ability to lead foundational, generative research — going beyond feature validation to define the opportunity space and shape product strategy

- Exceptional storyteller: you turn nuanced human insight into crisp, compelling narratives that drive alignment and action at all levels of the organization

- Experience working with or alongside data science teams to triangulate behavioral patterns from usage data with qualitative findings

- Track record of influencing product roadmaps, not just informing them — you know how to position research to land with impact

- Fluency using AI tools to accelerate iterative research cycles — from faster synthesis and screener development to rapid concept testing — while maintaining methodological rigor.

- Advanced degree preferred (Psychology, Behavioral Science, Cognitive Science, Human-Computer Interaction, Anthropology, or a related field); Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required

 Preferred Qualifications 

- Experience in marketplaces, e-commerce, grocery, CPG, or subscription products where lifecycle, personalization, and repeat behavior are critical

- Research experience on high-visibility consumer surfaces such as home feeds, personalized browse, and merchandising placements — including how users navigate density, information hierarchy, and above/below-the-fold content

- Background researching and informing onboarding, activation, and retention journeys that build habits, loyalty, and trust

- Familiarity with AI-powered, agentic, or conversational product experiences and the ability to study how users engage with them — including novel methods for researching AI interactions

- Ability to influence outcomes on multi-team initiatives without direct authority — you know how to build the coalitions that make research land

- Familiarity with meal planning, nutrition, health goals, or dietary restriction management and how they intersect with household grocery behavior

QuickBooks Canada is looking for a Senior Staff Designer to reinvent how prospects experience quickbooks.ca — from first visit through trial, plan selection and purchase. This is a senior, hands-on design role for someone who treats the website as a product with a P&L, not a brochure. 
 You will own the design vision for the direct-channel web experience: the ideas, the UI, the prototypes, and the evidence that they work. Web is the primary mandate; you will also flex into campaign, paid media and lifecycle creative when priorities demand it. You will partner day-to-day with our Web Enablement & Ops team, who own the build, release and experimentation infrastructure, to take concepts from Figma into production and into A/B tests. You'll draw on Intuit's brand system and design language, but your mandate is to push beyond templated marketing pages toward experiences that are genuinely new — interactive, personalized, AI-assisted — and measurably better at moving visitors through the funnel. 
 This role operates with independence and clear creative authority. The right candidate is not just a strong maker: they are a strategic partner who can turn business goals, funnel data, customer insight and brand inputs into design that is distinctive, coherent and built to convert. They know how to pitch ideas, take feedback with maturity, build trust with senior stakeholders, and keep work moving through ambiguity. 

 At Intuit, we're intentionally building AI into how we design, prototype and ship. We look for designers who are excited to bring AI into their workflow — to explore more directions faster, prototype in code, and save their energy for the judgment calls only a human can make. 

 Intuit has embraced a hybrid working model and this role will be based out of our Toronto office 3 days per week.

 Responsibilities 
 Own the web experience design vision

- Define and evolve the end-to-end visual and interaction design for quickbooks.ca acquisition journeys: homepage, product and feature pages, pricing and plan selection, trial and buy flows, campaign landing pages and lead-capture experiences.

- Set the bar for UI craft on the site — typography, layout, motion, interaction patterns — and raise it consistently across every page you touch and every page others build.

- Translate Intuit brand and design-system foundations into a web experience that is unmistakably QuickBooks yet tailored to Canadian small businesses and accountants.
 Drive innovation, not just optimization

- Generate and prototype new experience concepts that go beyond incremental page tweaks: interactive product tours, guided plan recommenders, AI-assisted 'which QuickBooks is right for me' flows, dynamic content by segment or intent, and other patterns that don't yet exist on our site.

- Maintain a forward-looking view of best-in-class SaaS and fintech web experiences and bring back what's worth stealing, adapted to our brand and funnel.

- Build reusable patterns, components and templates so innovation scales across the site rather than living on one page.
 Design for the funnel and prove it

- Ground every concept in a hypothesis about visitor behaviour and a target metric (engagement, click-through, trial starts, purchase, SKU mix).

- Partner with Web Enablement & Ops and Analytics to size opportunities, design experiments, define success criteria, and read results. Iterate on what wins; kill what doesn't

- Use behavioural data (analytics, session replay, heatmaps, research) to identify friction and prioritize where design effort will move the numbers most. 
 Ship with the Web Enablement & Ops team

- Deliver production-ready design: annotated Figma files, prototypes, component specs and interaction details that developers can build from without guesswork.

- Work inside the team's sprint and release cadence; participate in QA and design reviews of the live build.

- Ensure work meets accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA / AODA), performance, SEO and localization requirements (English and French) from concept, not as a retrofit.
 Flex into campaign and media creative

- As a secondary responsibility, lead or contribute design for high-priority campaign, paid media and lifecycle creative when the business needs it — bringing the same craft, brand fluency and performance mindset you apply to the web.

- Ensure campaign creative and landing experiences are designed as one journey, not handed off between teams.
 Lead through influence

- Present and defend creative direction to marketing, product, brand and international leadership with clear rationale tied to business outcomes.

- Act as the design voice in Direct Channel Marketing planning, ensuring experience quality is considered alongside media, search and lifecycle decisions.

- Mentor and critique across the broader Canada marketing team and agency partners; raise the standard of design work you don't personally produce.

 Qualifications 
 What you bring:

- Deep experience designing marketing websites and conversion-critical web experiences for SaaS, fintech or consumer subscription businesses, with a portfolio that shows both exceptional UI craft and measurable business results (lift in conversion, engagement or revenue you can speak to).

- Mastery of visual and interaction design fundamentals — typography, layout, hierarchy, colour, motion — applied to responsive web at a large-brand quality bar.

- Advanced Figma skills including component libraries, variables and prototyping; comfort working within and extending an enterprise design system.

- Demonstrated experience in experimentation-led design: framing hypotheses, designing test variants, working with analytics and CRO partners, and iterating from results.

- Ability to prototype interactively — in Figma, and increasingly in code with AI-assisted tools — to test ideas before committing engineering effort.

- Working knowledge of how the web is built (HTML/CSS, component-based front ends, CMS constraints, performance and Core Web Vitals) so your designs are buildable and you can collaborate credibly with developers.

- Demonstrated integration of AI tools into your design workflow to improve speed, exploration or quality.

- Strong storytelling and presentation skills; proven ability to build trust with senior stakeholders through judgment, candour and organization.

- Breadth across marketing design — able to move from web UI to campaign, paid media or lifecycle creative without a drop in quality, and to keep those touchpoints coherent as one journey.

- Ability to operate independently across multiple workstreams while maintaining quality and momentum.

-  
 Nice to have:

- Bilingual English/French, and experience designing for Canadian audiences in both languages.

- Experience with personalization, dynamic content or AI-driven experiences on marketing sites.

- Familiarity with experimentation platforms and behavioural analytics tools.

- Experience in a matrixed global organization where a market team works within a shared brand and platform.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Hi, I’m George Shang https://www.linkedin.com/in/george-shang/ - I lead Jane’s Growth Strategy & Operations team. I’m looking for an experienced, analytical & strategic thinker to help us address some of Jane’s most pressing growth opportunities.

The Senior Manager, Growth Strategy & Insights will work in our growth group to tackle key problems over a wide range of topics, such as growth analysis, revenue forecasting, market sizing, pricing, and more. Day to day, this person will evaluate and model new initiatives, work across senior stakeholders to drive alignment, and lead projects through to completion. This is a highly strategic role, sitting at the heart of how we drive growth for the company.

This role reports into the Growth Strategy & Operations team - we are a lean team, and success in the role depends on strong ownership, comfort operating independently, and effective collaboration across functions.




WHAT IMPACT WE'RE LOOKING FOR YOU TO MAKE: 

 - Build and sustain complex marketing models. Apply structural rigor and inform strategic decisions around how Jane tracks and evaluates marketing influence, spend, and other KPIs.

 - Own the full arc of an analysis, from insight to action. Across some of Jane’s most complex growth initiatives: structure the problem, build the analysis, craft the narrative, present to exec audiences, and follow up to make sure recommendations actually get implemented.

 - Drive Jane’s pricing and packaging strategy. Bring structure to how Jane thinks about pricing: grounding decisions in customer research and financial modeling, aligning stakeholders across the org, and shaping how new offerings get priced and packaged over time. 

 - Track performance and diagnose when something goes wrong. Monitor how the business is doing against plan, and when a number moves unexpectedly, get to the real driver rather than the first explanation that sounds plausible.

 - Act as a thought partner and ‘go-to’ analytical resource for growth leaders; forecast, measure, and make optimization recommendations across channels: e.g., Paid Ads, Direct Mail, Trade Shows, etc.

 - Take on leadership’s most pressing priorities. Serve as a trusted thought partner on high-stakes, often ambiguous problems, working alongside Jane leadership to surface key insights and produce structured executive level perspectives.

 - Build strong working relationships across Jane. Partner effectively with teams across Marketing, Support, General Managers, and beyond, earning trust as someone who can get things done well with anyone in the building.

 - Raise the analytical bar for the team. Build repeatable frameworks and self-serve tools that make the team's recurring work faster and more rigorous over time.




WHAT EXPERIENCE WE NEED

 - Consulting or comparable background. 4+ years in top-tier management consulting (McKinsey, BCG, Bain) with a track record of driving operational improvements & owning strategic initiatives. Candidates from Tech BizOps, corporate strategy, or comparable analytical backgrounds will also be considered.

 - Strong quantitative skills. Proficiency with complex financial models, comfort working with large and imperfect datasets, and the ability to produce a defensible answer. SQL experience, or a willingness to learn it, is a plus.

 - Structured problem solving. A hypothesis-led, answer-first approach, with the ability to take an ambiguous, poorly-defined problem, break it down, and build a clear path to a solution.

 - Slide-building and storytelling. The ability to construct a clear narrative, build the deck to support it, and present it to executive stakeholders.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. Able to make progress without a fully-scoped brief and to prioritize effectively under time constraints.

 - A high bar for quality. Detail-oriented, producing work suitable for an exec level audience.

 - Independence and collaboration. Works autonomously while building trust and collaborating effectively across the organization.

 - Domain interest. Experience in or exposure to SaaS is a plus.

If you don’t meet every single qualification but are excited about this role, we’d still love to hear from you.




MORE ABOUT JANE

Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company with a remote-first team working across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers.

We build the products and tools that thousands of clinics rely on every day to run their businesses, care for their patients, and grow their communities. That level of impact means every person at Jane plays an important role in how we show up for our customers. We're all responsible for being deeply connected to their needs, obsessed with improving their experience, and proud of the difference our work makes in their day-to-day lives.

Jane is growing fast, and that growth brings exciting challenges that call for adaptability, resilience, learning agility, and humility. We're proud of what we've built and quick to admit what we don't know yet. We listen, learn, and adjust as we go. More than 70,000 businesses run on Jane which has 250,000+ practitioners interacting with our product on a daily basis and growth is continuing to accelerate.

Our goal isn't just delivery - it's delight. We move quickly, communicate openly, and solve real problems together. If you're energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and eager to learn with others, you'll thrive at Jane.




COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

At Jane, we’re committed to paying fairly, clearly, and above all, paying for growth. You'll see that our salary ranges are quite large - this is intentional. It reflects the full growth journey someone might take in the role, from developing skills early on to becoming highly proficient and ultimately achieving excellence. Most new hires join at the accomplished stage. A starting salary below this typically indicates a candidate with strong potential who is still developing key skills. Salaries above this usually apply to existing team members who have made a significant impact and bring deep Jane-specific knowledge.

Paying clearly is one of our compensation fundamentals. Watch this https://vimeo.com/880258361 short video to learn how our salary bands are set. You’re also encouraged to ask questions about compensation at any point during the interview process.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Jane is a team that's all about fostering growth, spreading delight, and serving our healthcare community. We're looking for people who are ready to jump in and join us as we simplify the lives of healthcare practitioners and patients every day.


The Web team owns the website end to end: the engineering, the design, the content, and the strategy that connects them. This role owns that last piece. As Web Marketing Manager, you're the person who decides where the website is going and why: the information architecture, the navigation, the page strategy, and the through-line that turns the site into a coherent, high-performing experience. This means connecting the strategy to real growth goals so the site gets found and converts. You'll partner closely with our Product Marketing team (including our Senior PMM, Platform) so that how Jane shows up on the web reflects how we position ourselves as a multi-product, AI-powered platform, but the web strategy itself is yours to own.


This is a senior builder individual contributor role with real influence. Strategy, design, engineering and content work together from the start here; there are no handoffs and you’re leading that work through clarity and judgement.


What impact we're looking for you to make

 - Own the strategy for the Jane marketing website. Translate Jane’s business goals into a concrete roadmap, backed by frameworks and shared language that enables the Web team to make clear decisions on what to build and what to leave behind. On flagship pages like the homepage, you’ll pull in Brand, Content, Design and Product to ensure the story we tell matches the product practitioners are signing up for. You are the decision-maker on how the website is structured and why.

 - Connect strategy to the customer and to performance. Synthesize qualitative and quantitative signals into a clear point of view about what clinics and clinicians need from Jane. Ensure the website earns its keep, grounding strategic decisions in how the site performs after shipping.

 - Direct our organic and answer engine presence. Make sure practitioners find Jane when they’re searching for a solution, whether that search happens on Google or through an AI assistant. Set the strategy, brief subject matter experts effectively and judge whether the work is moving the needle.

 - Bring an experimentation mindset. Think in terms of hypotheses and evidence when you’re making a strategic call - what would tell you this page structure or narrative is working versus not.

 - Partner with the web platform and enablement function. Connect strategic direction to the platform capabilities, tooling, and execution that make it real on the site.



What experience we need

 - Solid experience in web strategy, digital strategy, product/content strategy, or a closely related discipline, including experience owning strategy for a substantial website or digital property. Experience with technology-forward or platform products is a strong asset.

 - Experience treating a website as a genuine growth channel

 - Deep fluency in information architecture and navigation - you can look at a growing, multi-product site and know how it should be structured, and defend why.

 - Strong analytical instincts. You're comfortable with analytics data to inform and validate strategic decisions, and you know the difference between a signal and noise.

 - Real experience running A/B tests and CRO growth experimentation at scale

 - SEO/AEO fluency- close enough to the work to know what’s actually moving the needle

 - Comfort working in a modern CMS (we use WordPress). Experience with CRO tools (Optimizely, Contentful, Webflow, etc.) is a nice-to-have.

 - Understanding of responsive design, accessibility and testing across devices.

 - Excellent communication and storytelling. You can articulate a strategy to various stakeholders and make a case for a strategy as clearly as you can read a dashboard.

 - Genuine curiosity about Jane’s mission and about the healthcare practitioners we build for.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Hi, I'm Dan Davidow https://www.linkedin.com/in/dandavidow/, Chief Marketing Officer at Jane. I joined Jane because I have a real passion for helping small businesses succeed, and our customers run some of the most impactful small businesses there are. When I'm not doing that, you'll usually find me planning my next trip.

Jane has built strong momentum, and our next phase of growth will be driven by deeper relationships, trusted partnerships, and a strong presence in the healthcare community. We have also found success in our demand gen programs, and now is the time to build on what's already working.

That's where you come in. As our Director of SMB & Self Serve Demand Generation, you'll own a core part of how Jane generates demand: our paid media program, our website (including SEO and AEO), and our lifecycle marketing. You'll work alongside the teams who own events, partnerships, and community, so that together it all adds up to one cohesive motion. AI is central to how you'll do this: from how practitioners discover Jane through AI-driven search, to how we use AI to plan, build, and optimize our own programs. You’ll also partner closely with our growth product team who works on onboarding and optimizing user flow.

You'll lead a team of three channel experts today, with room to grow the team as the program scales, and partner closely with our Marketing Analytics & Operations team on measurement and infrastructure.

This is a role for a leader who can balance strategy and execution. Part of this job is hands-on; you're comfortable working directly in the campaigns, data and tools, and building AI-assisted workflows yourself, not just directing from above. Success looks like building trust with our market and driving real business impact.

 


WHAT IMPACT WE’RE LOOKING FOR YOU TO MAKE

 - Own paid media. Lead our paid media budget and team across channels, including paid search, paid social, direct mail, and more - deciding where we invest, how we measure it, and when we shift.

 - Partner with Growth Product. You’ll work directly with designers, developers, and product managers building the future of onboarding and activation at Jane, designing and executing thoughtful tests.

 - Deliver on web experience. Manage the marketing side of jane.com http://jane.com - the front door to Jane for practitioners, patients, and the broader healthcare community. Partner closely with design and engineering, and own site strategy, conversion rate, and our organic presence across both traditional search (SEO) and AI-driven discovery (AEO).

 - Own lifecycle marketing. Design and run the programs that guide practitioners from first touch through trial, signup, and expansion, working closely with product marketing and sales on what happens at each stage.

 - Put AI to work. Make Jane easy to find in an AI-first world, and use AI across the demand program itself - research, creative testing, campaign optimization, reporting - so a small team can operate like a much bigger one.

 - Sharpen our measurement. We have a solid measurement foundation today. You'll define what the demand program needs next - KPIs, attribution, reporting - and partner with our Marketing Analytics & Operations team to build it.

 - Align with Sales and Support. Work deeply with our sales and support teams to design demand programs that support revenue outcomes, not just top-of-page metrics.

 - Build the team. Lead, coach, and grow a team of channel experts, and raise the bar on how we plan, test, and learn together.

 


WHAT EXPERIENCE WE NEED

 - A strong track record in demand gen or growth marketing. 5-7 years driving tangible business impact, ideally with experience managing and scaling multi-million-dollar budgets.

 - Deeply analytical. Exceptional at translating numbers into marketing strategy, and comfortable operating in a constrained, highly data-driven environment. Deep expertise across marketing analytics, web optimization, lifecycle, and paid acquisition.

 - AI-forward. You're already using AI tools in your day-to-day marketing work, you have a point of view on how AI is changing search and discovery, and you're excited to keep experimenting.

 - High-velocity SMB experience. Proven success in high-velocity business models, ideally SMB or consumer. We're not looking for someone whose experience is only account-based marketing or traditional enterprise SaaS.

 - A strong collaborator. You know how to work with design, development, and product teams to drive results.

 - A builder of teams. A track record of hiring and developing high-caliber growth marketing talent.

ashby:jobber:378345d4-0b72-4811-837c-5be.description:
ARE YOU A PERSON THAT WANTS TO EMPOWER SMALL BUSINESSES?



Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for an Account Executive, Full Cycle to be part of our Sales department.



Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want! 



Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ahVf4AjYlh4.



The team: 

Our Sales team gains an understanding of who our customers are, what their businesses do, and how Jobber can help them succeed, to turn leads into advocates.



They all have an incredible passion for sales, our customer, and a connection to our purpose. This team is focused on delivering on the promise to make small businesses more successful, and they celebrate, motivate, and challenge each other daily. They are also focused on growth personally and professionally and are supported through regular 1:1’s which focus on performance, coaching, long-term development, and consistent feedback from peers and leaders. 



The role:

Reporting to the Manager, Sales, this Account Executive, Full Cycle will play a significant role in developing relationships and trust with small businesses in our journey to power the world of mobile services. Our sales process while quick is highly consultative, and helping the customer understand the value and efficiency Jobber could provide their company is paramount.



The Account Executive, Full Cycle will: 

 - Own the full sales process from prospecting to closing 

 - Drive connection with potential customers through phone, email, and sms outreach to create new opportunities

 - Leverage strong communication and active listening skills to build rapport, trust, and a deep understanding of the small businesses we work with. 

 - Be a trusted advisor and product expert and leverage that knowledge to provide recommendations on how to best utilize Jobber, from specific workflows to feature fits.

 - Demonstrate the value of Jobber through conversation, social proof and product demonstrations

 - Track key information in Salesforce for follow-up, knowledge sharing, and analytics
   
   

To be successful, you will need:

 - Demonstrated experience in a sales environment with commission and/or targets. You can speak to them, and can speak to how you were successful. .

 - To drive urgency and excitement. You will be required to sell in a dynamic environment with a fairly short sales cycle. You should be energized by high volume and the prospect of uncapped earning potential!

 - To be driven, tenacious and disciplined. You won’t win over every prospect, and there will be many highs and lows. It’s about how you balance those ups and downs and bring the best of what you have to the job daily.

 - To find solutions. If something isn’t going right, you’ll take care of it. Not every conversation will be the same, and you're quick at thinking on your feet.

 - To be data driven. Being able to source, interpret and create a narrative based on data will be key for your own success as well as the small businesses you’re supporting. 

 - To be coachable and adaptable. The sales team is always changing and evolving, so being flexible and good with change and ambiguity is important.

 - To enjoy technology. We're working hard to empower the world with mobile technology and are looking for someone who wants to share their excitement.

 - To have a clear and confident communication style. You should have the ability to actively listen and consult with our customers and get a true understanding of who they are and what they need. This position involves a good deal of phone time, so these skills are imperative.

 - Previous experience with a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system, preferably SalesForce.

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and supportive of your experience and growth. This opportunity has a fixed compensation structure, meaning all employees come in at the exact same rate.  It includes a base salary of $60,000 and a commission of $40,000, for an On-Target Earnings (OTE) of $100,000. Our commission structure is uncapped and paid out monthly, meaning there is potential to earn beyond the stated OTE. 

This OTE is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. As well, this role has clearly defined growth opportunities to deepen expertise, explore new roles, or step into leadership. You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

If you have any questions about our compensation approach, we encourage open conversations throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. The role:

The Technical Talent Attraction team is dedicated to finding the right people to join us in our mission to help small businesses succeed. Reporting to the Manager, Talent Attraction, you’ll specialize in identifying, engaging, and hiring top-tier technical talent across Product Engineering, Product Design, Product Management, and other technical teams.

In this role, you’ll act as a strategic advisor to hiring managers, gaining deep insight into their teams, aligning on hiring needs, and driving recruitment strategies that deliver exceptional outcomes. You’ll apply your experience with performance-based and competency-driven interviews to ensure we hire candidates who not only have the right skills, but who also align with our values and vision. Throughout, you’ll be committed to delivering a thoughtful, engaging candidate experience that brings Jobber’s story to life and builds lasting connections with every potential Jobberino.

 

The Talent Attraction Partner,  will:

 - Own the full-cycle recruiting process for a variety of technical roles, including pipeline building, screening, interviewing, scheduling, stakeholder coaching, and closing. You'll be accountable for results, efficiency, quality, and equitable outcomes across every stage of the funnel.

 - Builder mindset: Bring an experimental, builder's mindset to the role — research, prototype, and pressure-test new tools, systems, and emerging technologies (including AI) that make the recruitment process faster, smarter, or more insightful, while maintaining a human-centered approach, and share what you learn with the rest of the team.

 - Collaborate with hiring teams to calibrate expectations, improve hiring practices, and up-level talent decisions across our hiring teams — including pushing back constructively when a process, requirement, or assumption no longer makes sense.

This role provides a great balance for someone who wants both the strategy and the execution.

You will build for where Jobber is going, not just where it is. Structures will change, manager expectations will shift, and AI will change what a team can do. With your strong business knowledge, you will bring forward your viewpoint to influence the department's health and success.

The People Business Partner will: 

 - Know your group's strategy, structure, and drivers well enough to build a people agenda that gets ahead of capability, engagement, retention, and succession risk.

 - Advise managers and senior leaders across performance, development, compensation, team structure, and change. Communicate for leaders who do not know People, and persuade where you need to.

 - Coach first-time and early-tenure managers through the hard parts of people leadership. Leaving them more capable and equipped to lead afterward.

 - Identify when the same question keeps returning, and build the guidance once to multiply your impact and allow managers to be self-sufficient.

 - Run performance management end to end: expectations, documentation standards, improvement plans, and the difficult conversations and exits that follow.

 - Bring judgment to talent review and compensation cycles: calibration, leveling, promotions, and succession gaps named before someone resigns.

 - Own the employee lifecycle for your group: leaves, accommodations, return to work, internal moves, and exits, including the administration and coordination with managers, payroll, and providers that keeps it accurate and humane.

 - Manage employee relations independently, including ambiguous and legally sensitive cases, with a firm grip on employment legislation and clear escalation when it is warranted.

 - Assess structures, spans of control, and decision rights when performance or growth raises structural questions. Identify a people problem from a design problem, and support leaders through the changes that follow.

 - Track leading indicators across engagement, performance, and retention, run your group's listening cycles, and turn results into action plans leaders commit to.

 - Drive people initiatives end to end. Adapt an existing program where one fits, build the approach where nothing does.

 - Use AI in the work, not around it. Delegate research and drafting to agents so your time goes to judgment, analyze your group's data to arrive at leadership conversations with a point of view, and pressure test your recommendations before you take them forward.

 - Bring forward the gaps. When a manual process or documentation hole keeps generating the same escalation, propose what should replace it.

 - Partner with Talent Development, Total Rewards, and Talent Attraction so your group gets one answer, not three. Stay current on where People practice and tech are heading, and bring what works back to the PBP team, because the pattern you found almost always exists elsewhere.

To be successful, you should have:

 - A proven track record of advising and influencing senior leaders and executives, including the ones who needed persuading and who did not arrive with the problem framed. Ideally somewhere that was growing while you were there.

 - Performance management and employee relations experience you can speak to specifically, including the cases that did not go the way you planned.

 - Experience running performance and compensation cycles end to end for a multi-team group, not supporting someone else's.

 - A working understanding of employment legislation and how it applies to our business. When we expand into new regions, you get yourself up to speed quickly.

 - Real AI fluency. You can point to work you do differently now than a year ago, and to something you have built or automated yourself.

 - Comfort with the administrative side. Getting the documentation, systems, and detail right matters to the person on the other end.

 - Credibility that comes from following through. You do what you say, which is why leaders trust you with the hard things.

 - Strong written and verbal communication. You can prepare a brief for leadership and deliver content at a department All Hands.

 - The resilience to keep moving when the situation is messy and the answer is not obvious yet.
