The role:

Our Brand Partnerships team manages both short term and long term relationships with online influencers to build awareness of Jobber and recommend Jobber software to their communities, ultimately driving new Jobber customers. It's one of our acquisition channels and we're building it into a best-in-class program.

Reporting to the Senior Manager of Brand Partnerships, the Senior Brand Partnerships Manager is a senior individual contributor role for someone who wants to shape where this channel goes next. Half of your time goes to your own roster of brand partners and the spend behind it, recruiting, coaching, negotiating, and hitting a monthly number. The other half is bigger: you'll build the strategy for how we help our strongest partners grow further, across the entire program, forecast what it's worth, prove it on your own roster, and roll it out to the team.

The ideal candidate has done this before. You've looked across a whole roster and seen where the real headroom was, not just where the gaps were. You've built a strategy, set a number against it, and been held to it. You're comfortable in the data, confident in a negotiation, and good at getting people who don't report to you to change how they work. You have a point of view about where creator marketing is heading and the operating discipline to prove it.

The Senior Brand Partnerships Manager will:

 - Own a roster. You'll recruit, coach, and grow your own roster of brand partners and the spend behind it—full cycle, from first conversation and negotiation through onboarding, ongoing coaching, and renewal.

 - Help great partners 2x their results. With visibility across our whole partner network, you'll work out what our most successful partners do differently, and turn that into something every partner can benefit from. The best partners in this program are still nowhere near their ceiling, and finding what takes them there is the heart of this role.

 - Build the strategy for partner growth. You'll develop the strategy, set the targets and forecast, design what we try, and test across the team. This is work that doesn't exist yet—you'll create it.

 - Implement growth strategies. Working collaboratively across our team, you’ll implement and launch strategies to grow our performing talent into top performers. You’ll set targets, work with other reps to activate their partners, and report on performance regularly to prove what’s working to drive incremental sales.

 - Turn it into plays the team can run. Every improvement you create should become something repeatable. You'll document it, train the team on it, and make sure it sticks, then be honest about what isn't working and change course.

 - Dig deep into the data. You'll analyze channel performance, report on results, and translate what you find into action.

 - Negotiate with judgment. You'll handle complex partnership negotiations and contracts, using strong judgment on brand fit and brand risk, and collaborating with our Public Relations and Legal teams where a partnership carries exposure.

 - Be a brand champion. You'll protect and grow the reach and reputation of our brand through the partners we work with, and contribute ideas for campaigns, events, and resources that make our program one people want to be part of.

 - Raise the level of the team. You'll share insights and learnings, coach and support other Brand Partnership reps, and help set the standard for what great looks like here.



To be successful, you’ll need:

 - Extensive marketing and influencer partnership experience. You’ll have a track record of measurable, social-driven results that contribute to new business (sales) and revenue.

 - A track record of making good performance great. You've taken programs or partners that were already working and found meaningful additional growth in them, helping them reach a level they hadn’t before, and you can explain exactly how.

 - Experience building strategy, not just running campaigns or managing partners. You've formed a thesis about where growth was hiding in a program, forecast it, executed it, and got other people to adopt it so it can compound and scale across a team.

 - Real comfort with data. You can analyze partner-level performance, build a forecast you'll defend, and tell the difference between a trend and noise, without waiting for someone to build you a report.

 - The ability to influence without authority. Much of your impact will come through people who don't report to you. Previous people-leadership experience is a real asset here.

 - Strong commercial instincts. You're confident pitching, handling objections, negotiating, and closing, and you keep a warm pipeline, warm.

 - Excellent judgment. You can assess brand fit and brand risk quickly, and you raise concerns early rather than after the fact.

 - Strong communication and project management skills. You'll coordinate directly with partners and across multiple internal teams to move work forward.

 - Ambition and humility. You don't accept the status quo simply because “it's what we've always done.” You push for better, newer, and more innovative ways to do things, all while staying humble.

 - Comfort wearing multiple hats. This is a hands-on role. Strategy sits alongside building a roster with campaign briefs, backend setup, contract tracking, and content monitoring.

 - The ability to travel. You may get the opportunity to represent Jobber during Ambassador brand trips, trade shows and other customer-related events across North America.

It would be really great (but not a deal-breaker) if you had:

 - Previous people-leadership experience.

 - Sales or business development experience at a SaaS company or tech startup.

 - Experience running paid campaigns on social media and with creators.

 - Experience with affiliate or partner management platforms and attribution tooling.

 - Education in Marketing, Business, Strategy, or related fields. BA, BS, MBA or MS in Marketing, Business or related field is a plus.

 - Investigate operational problems by gathering stakeholder input, reviewing current workflows, and analyzing available data.

 - Separate immediate requests from the underlying problem that needs to be solved, and structure ambiguous problems into testable hypotheses.

 - Build the fact base: pull and analyze operational and performance data, size the impact, and translate findings into clear recommendations with the trade-offs made explicit.

 - Document current-state processes, requirements, owners, handoffs, dependencies, and common failure points.

 - Design practical improvements that make processes clearer, more efficient, and more scalable.


PROJECT & WORKSTREAM DELIVERY

 - Translate business problems into clear requirements, project plans, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, and success measures.

 - Keep projects moving by following up on actions, resolving blockers, and escalating risks when needed.

 - Develop rollout plans that include communication, documentation, training, readiness, and post-launch support, anticipating where resistance may arise and what support will be needed to make the change stick.

Small businesses increasingly rely on vertical SaaS platforms like Jobber not just to run their operations, but to manage their money. Payments is the foundation of everything we do in Fintech, and how we go to market with our Get Paid products (invoicing, payments, instant payouts, etc) is the single biggest lever we have to grow the business.

 - Mapping and rebuilding the end-to-end customer journey for payments, from first touch through activation and ongoing usage, working closely with cross-functional partners. This includes identifying where customer-facing teams (sales, post-sales, support) can change their motions to drive better outcomes.

 - Experimenting with a range of actions (e.g. incentives) to drive payments adoption and usage, rapidly iterating based on results.

 - Defining the metrics that matter for payments GTM and holding yourself (and cross-functional partners) accountable to them.

 - Building deep working relationships across GTM teams, Product, RevOps, Analytics, etc. You are the connective tissue between these teams on payments GTM.

 - Using data and qualitative insights to find opportunities, size them, run experiments, and measure results.

 - Staying close to what other vertical SaaS and embedded payments players are doing. Knowing where Jobber can differentiate.

 - Operating and strategy experience, ideally a mix of both:

   - Strategy experience (valued): you have been a strategic partner to senior leaders, making data-driven recommendations. Examples could be Management Consulting, VC, or Strategy & Operations.

 - Deep understanding of payments and financial services business models, metrics, and growth strategies is desirable, particularly financial services for small businesses.

 - Strong data instincts. You use analytics to measure impact, make decisions, and optimize performance. You are not just comfortable with data, you reach for it first.

 - Experience using languages such as SQL to manipulate large data sets is a plus, but not required.

 - Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to work across GTM teams, Product, Executive Leadership, etc. You translate data into stories and strategies into action plans.

 - Demonstrated ability to design and implement scalable operational processes that enhance efficiency and ultimately drive growth.

 - Passion for helping small businesses succeed through innovative financial solutions.

 - A curious mind and a growth mindset. You are a scrappy learner who can quickly become an expert and build new capabilities.

  • Roadmap Management: Develop the ASO roadmap, balancing default page optimizations with a robust A/B testing schedule of 3–5 tests per month per game.
  • Semantic Optimization: Develop strategy and execution to align with ongoing platform changes driven by AI.
  • AI-Driven Workflows: Utilize generative AI tools to scale high-volume metadata creation, localize for target markets, and perform sentiment analysis on competitor reviews.
  • Storefront Operations: Lead end-to-end execution across iOS, Google Play, Epic, and Steam, including uploading assets and managing storefront asset sheets.
  • Creative & Keyword Optimization: Collaborate with Creative Services (CS) to brief and iterate on high-impact assets like icons, screenshots, and feature graphics.
  • Launch Readiness (New Title): Lead ASO requirements for new game preparation, including soft launch testing roadmaps and post-launch optimization.
  • QA & Compliance: Review all store pages before submission and act as the final sign-off for the PRM release gate.
    Technical & Social Health: Monitor app store trends, competitor strategies, and algorithm changes to maintain visibility rankings.
    • Platform Marketing & Event Cards
  • Strategy Consulting: Advise on platform best practices for App Event Cards across the portfolio to optimize performance, partnering closely with PMM and Creative Services (CS). 
  • Execution: Support Product Marketing in areas that are needed such as (but not limited to) execution, including copywriting, creative ideation/project management, etc. 
  • Cross-Functional: If necessary, coordinate with PMM, PRM, CS, and BD to align ASO efforts with game calendars and platforms featuring opportunities.
  • Maintenance: Maintain the Platform Event Card Mastersheet and track performance metrics.
    • Analysis, Reporting & Synergy
  • Holistic Reporting: Monitor ASO KPIs (Impressions, Page Views, Downloads, CVR) and provide weekly/quarterly recaps.
  • Stakeholder Reporting: Deliver weekly, monthly, and quarterly performance recaps to cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Market Intelligence: Conduct thorough keyword research and competitor analysis to identify high-impact optimization opportunities.
  • Growth Modeling: Partner with Data Science to build forecasting models and evaluate the business impact of storefront optimizations.
  • Behavioral Analysis: Track post-install engagement and retention signals, as the 2026 algorithm increasingly rewards sustained user value over simple download velocity.
  • Industry trends: Share ongoing trend updates that are impacting our organic installs and store presence to major stakeholders. Ensure to provide up to date information in real time and insights on how this can impact Kabam’s business.
    • To be successful in this role, your background includes::
  • Experience: 2+ years in Growth Marketing and ASO within the mobile gaming industry.
  • Platform Expertise: Deep knowledge of modern app store algorithms, including Apple's NLP intent matching and Google’s AI-organized "Guided Search".
  • AI Tooling: Proficiency in AI-specific ASO tools (e.g., AppTweak) and LLMs for workflow efficiency.
  • Analytical Skills: Strong data-driven mindset with the ability to build growth models and forecast install impact.
  • Project Management: Ability to manage high-volume storefront setups (iOS, Google Play, Epic, Steam) and track all changes meticulously.

Our teams are made up of a fusion of personalities and interests bound together by a collaborative nature, fun-loving culture, and a drive to do what it takes to make great games. And this is where you come in…   As a Senior Publishing Product Manager, you will work across a broad range of projects, supporting the full product lifecycle from early opportunity discovery through development and launch. For internal projects, you will support the new product discovery process through market trends and research, identifying comparable titles for both product and marketing purposes, and assessing market-product fit to help teams make informed product decisions. For external projects, you will provide data, market research, and competitive insights to help the Principal Publishing Product Manager and the team to identify and evaluate new opportunities. This includes creating reports on the business potential and marketability of each product, supporting the creation of financial and revenue forecasts, and contributing to the execution of product, publishing, and marketing strategy. Working closely with the Principal Product Manager, you will help shape the strategic direction of projects, from opportunity assessment and product positioning through go-to-market planning. You will work cross-functionally to align teams around priorities, strategy, and key objectives. Importantly, this role is not limited to assessing opportunities and developing strategy. You will also work directly with the team to execute against the strategy and see projects through the full development and launch cycle, using market insights and performance data to inform decisions and optimize outcomes along the way. The role ultimately sits at the intersection of market intelligence, product strategy, commercial assessment, marketing, and execution, with the goal of identifying the right opportunities and turning them into successful products for both players and the business.   This role is a full-time, on-site position based 5 days a week at our Downtown Vancouver studio. In this role, you can expect to::
Key Accountabilities:

New Product Discovery

  • Conduct market analysis, competitive research, and business analysis to identify trends and potential new product opportunities, within the strategic areas the team has defined.
  • Partner with the Research & Insights team to gather and apply user research that informs product direction.
  • Work with cross-functional stakeholders (Design, Finance, Marketing, Product, Player Insights) to assess feasibility of new product concepts.
  • Build business cases for specific product opportunities, including market sizing, value proposition, and financial projections, for review by leadership.
  • Track progress of assigned discovery initiatives against established success metrics.
  • Prepare and hand off prioritized opportunities and supporting documentation to dedicated product teams.
    • Publishing Execution
  • Develop go-to-market strategy and plans by analyzing successful comparable titles and marketing strategies, working closely with the Principal Publishing Product Manager to translate market insights into actionable plans.
  • Maintain ongoing competitive intelligence by continuously tracking new and emerging comparable titles across external publishing projects, providing regular updates and analysis to inform product and marketing decisions.
  • Support creation of the product roadmap by developing a deep understanding of development milestones, assessing product, development, and market risks and recommending mitigation strategies where needed.
  • Conduct milestone-based product reviews with the broader Publishing team, evaluating product progress against market comparables and providing insights and recommendations to strengthen the product.
  • Coordinate cross-functional execution across publishing partners to track milestones, budgets, product goals, and key deliverables, ensuring projects remain aligned with strategic objectives.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with external studios, working closely with development teams to establish effective communication, resolve pain points, and support a smooth publishing and development process.
  • Partner with Business Development to identify and develop platform partnership opportunities that can support the product's growth, visibility, and commercial performance.
  • Ensure cross-functional readiness and alignment by communicating product updates, roadmap changes, launch milestones, and marketing beats across BD, Legal, Finance, Marketing, PRM, QA, and other relevant teams.
  • Monitor post-launch performance and proactively identify risks, performance gaps, and opportunities for improvement, escalating key insights and recommendations to the publishing team.

ashby:klue:4cd5cf92-2263-4b2c-960c-f86d3.description:
AT KLUE https://klue.com/, WE’RE BUILDING THE FUTURE OF COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE




👋 AND OUR SDR TEAM IS HIRING: ONE DREAM TEAM, TWO AVENUES 

(P.s. We call our SDRs "Account Specialists" if you're having trouble finding them on LinkedIn)


CHECK OUT WHAT A DAY IN THE LIFE OF AN SDR IS LIKE HERE https://www.instagram.com/kluein/reel/C8s6tWhxMqF/?hl=en!



We're hiring for two roles on Klue's SDR team. 

 - Account Specialist, New Business. You'll go after new business through true outbound prospecting. You've got proven sales experience.

 - Account Specialist, Win-Loss-Programs. You'll recruit and schedule the buyer interviews behind our win-loss research programs. No sales experience needed. Drive, EQ, and a hunger to learn are.

Both are a real start in tech, with a focus on outbound, real training, and plenty of room to grow.




OUR FOUNDATIONAL SDR PROGRAM

Regardless of your focus, this is a learning culture. Your growth matters here. Starting with our 2-week foundational SDR onboarding program where you'll build strong prospecting skills with continued training throughout your 3-month ramp. Our team will help you advance, and in time, you'll mentor newer SDRs. Our commitment is clear: prepare you to be an expert prospector and a well-rounded sales professional. 




WE'RE LOOKING FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE: 

 - Relentless, and have a history of achieving. You don’t stop when you face adversity and have a proven record of growing and developing whatever you dedicate yourself to.

 - Self driven. No one has to tell you to be hungry to achieve. We’ll help point you in the right direction but it’s on you to push to get there and that comes naturally.

 - Curious and keen to learn. You’ll keep digging until you find the answer and when you do you’ll question it in case you can improve what you dig up.

 - Tech-savvy early adopter. You’re willing to get uncomfortable testing new things in the pursuit of maximizing your outcomes. You’re also the first to share what’s working because you know it’ll elevate the team

 - Organized and detail-oriented. You stay meticulous on repeatable work.

 - High EQ and have good business acumen. You communicate well, read people, and understand why the work matters to the client



Now let's break down the roles and their focuses ⤵




ACCOUNT SPECIALIST, NEW BUSINESS

Your job is new business. Outbound is the whole game.

You have proven sales experience. It doesn’t have to be in SaaS, but you’ve consistently met and exceeded targets in your industry, demonstrating steady growth and leadership in your sales career.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Generate Leads. You’ll build prospect lists, learn how to research accounts, cold call and warm call, craft personalized email outreach, leverage LinkedIn, and use AI to prospect at scale. You'll generate leads through: 
   
   - Highly targeted outbound prospecting 
   
   - Nurturing and converting inbound leads. 

 - Lead introductory calls and master the art of discovery. You'll learn to identify prospect pain points and articulate Klue's value in real conversations, building this crucial sales skill through hands-on experience.

 - Have the autonomy to work on projects beyond your role. From evaluating leading edge sales technology, to improving existing processes, or learning how to interview other SDRs your impact goes beyond just prospecting.




ACCOUNT SPECIALIST, WIN-LOSS PROGRAMS

Break into tech by powering the research our clients use to win more deals.

You are looking to grow a career in tech sales. Maybe you're the hostess or bartender ready to break into tech. Maybe you're a few years into your career and making a pivot. Maybe you're a recent grad and high achiever with internships behind you. 




WHAT'S WIN-LOSS?

Our team of experienced analysts designs and delivers research programs for B2B technology companies. We use a structured, scalable process to help clients improve their win rates by making smarter, more impactful decisions.



We acquired Goldpan.ai http://Goldpan.ai in 2025, which strengthens our product and adds even more win-loss data for our growing client base. We're excited about what's ahead.



In this role, you'll sit at the intersection of win-loss research, B2B technology programs, and qualitative research recruitment. You'll use HubSpot, Nooks, LinkedIn, and AI-assisted workflows to build outreach campaigns that turn contact data and stale CRM data into completed, high-quality research interviews.




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Recruit interviewees. You'll run high-volume, multi-channel outreach by email, phone (parallel dialing in Nooks), and LinkedIn. You'll juggle ~30 active customer programs at once and keep recruitment statuses in HubSpot accurate and on time. When a program stalls, you'll dig into why and propose a fix. You'll also test new tactics to lift interview conversion across the team.

 - Qualify and hand off. You'll make sure interview data is clean, structured, and qualified before research calls. That means filling in missing details on HubSpot interview cards and telling researchers about anything that could affect interview quality or scope, so they never walk into a call underprepared.

 - Be a real part of the account team. You'll work alongside the CSM and Researcher on each program. You'll share status, challenges, and proposed solutions so nobody gets caught off guard, flag risks to program momentum or renewal, and join customer calls when needed.

 - Become the recruitment expert. You'll build fluency in our outreach approaches (Sales First, Leadership First, Klue Direct) and learn when each works best. You'll advise AEs, CSMs, and Researchers on recruitment strategy, lean on AI tools and automations to work faster, and propose better processes and workflows.




WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?

We'll be honest about the day-to-day: it's detailed, high-volume work. The people who love it stay meticulous because they can see where it leads. If you excel, you'll be promoted onto the New Business SDR team. 



Not sure which focus is right for you? No worries. When you apply, you'll be considered for both roles and we'll discuss it with you throughout the interview process.




⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️

Not ticking every box? That’s okay. We take potential into consideration. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be accepted in lieu of the specifics listed above.  - Upsell and cross-sell opportunities are identified, qualified, and closed at or above target. Win-loss cross-sell pipeline exists and is actively moving for eligible accounts.

 - Every account has at least one documented ROI moment per quarter, tied to a specific Klue outcome.

 - Every account has at least two active contacts at different levels. No single-threaded accounts in your book.

 - Customers are activated on new product capabilities within one quarter of release.

 - Risk is flagged and acted on early, not discovered at renewal.

MUST HAVES:

 - The experience. track record in a CSM or commercial role with direct revenue accountability. You've owned renewals and expansion targets and hit them.

 - Ownership. ability to lead and coordinate a cross-functional account team without direct authority.

 - Customer facing. Proven success building trust and credibility across a customer organization, from day-to-day champions to executive buyers.

 - Commercial fluency. comfortable with upsell conversations, business-case development, and navigating contract dynamics with confidence.

 - Strong discovery skills. can diagnose a customer's business goals, connect them to Klue's platform outcomes, and make the link explicit and repeatable.

 - Change management instinct. knows how to build internal Champions, navigate complex stakeholder dynamics, and drive adoption against organizational friction.

 - Multi-threading instinct. you build relationships across levels by default, not as a recovery strategy.

 - Signal awareness and speed. proactively identifies risk and opportunity in customer behavior, usage data, and relationship health, and acts fast.

 - Technical curiosity. comfortable learning integrations and AI capabilities, and explaining them clearly to non-technical audiences.

 - AI-fluency. actively uses AI tools in day-to-day work and can model that behavior with customers.




NICE-TO-HAVES:

 - Experience in competitive intelligence, product marketing, sales enablement, or B2B SaaS.

 - Familiarity with technical integrations (MCP, CRM, Slack, or similar) and comfort guiding customers through deployment.

 - Knowledge of competitive enablement best practices and how revenue teams operationalize competitive programs.

 - Hands-on experience with AI tools beyond basic usage: prompt design, workflow automation, or AI-assisted customer work.

Knak is a mission-driven company 

 Why? Because our time is limited, our competition is fierce, and our margin for error is small. To have the biggest impact on the world, we stay focused on our core mission, which is...

 Empowering marketers to be creative . 

 That’s why Knak exists.

 In a world where AI has made everyone a creator, Knak helps marketers turn ideas into on-brand, high-performing campaigns at scale. The world's most AI-forward companies, including Meta, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Vercel, Notion and Stripe, use Knak as their agentic marketing production layer.

 Here's what they and our investor Insight Partners figured out: creation got easy, but that’s making production harder. Every new idea and brief still has to be built, versioned, checked, approved, and shipped across every channel, and that work runs on handoffs, review cycles, and a lot of copy-paste. That middle stretch of the marketing stack has no system, no standard, and no owner.

 Knak is the flexible factory for that work. Our customers set the brand rules, choose the tools that feed in and the platforms that send, and decide where AI does the work and where people do. We handle the repeatable parts, so marketers get their time back for the parts that aren't.

 We're built by marketers, for marketers. We started with email because it's the hardest channel to get right and where many campaigns win or lose. Now we're bringing that same production discipline to every channel our customers use.

 The Role 

 As an Account Executive at Knak, you will be responsible for driving new business revenue by identifying, developing, and closing opportunities across mid-market and enterprise accounts. You will own the sales process from initial engagement through close, balancing proactive outbound prospecting with the effective conversion of inbound opportunities.

 Reporting to the Director of Sales, you will develop a strong understanding of each prospect's business challenges, build relationships with key stakeholders, and use a consultative approach to demonstrate how Knak can deliver meaningful business value. You'll work closely with Sales Development, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, and Sales Leadership throughout the sales process.

 Roles & Responsibilities 

- Build and manage a high-quality sales pipeline through strategic outbound prospecting and effective qualification and conversion of inbound opportunities.

- Partner with Marketing and Sales Development to identify priority accounts, personas, and opportunities.

- Develop a strong understanding of Knak's product, customers, market, and the challenges our buyers face.

- Conduct thoughtful discovery and deliver relevant product demonstrations that connect customer needs to Knak's capabilities and business value.

- Own assigned opportunities from qualification through close, developing and executing a clear strategy for each deal.

- Manage stakeholder engagement, next steps, business case development, demonstrations, commercial conversations, negotiation, procurement, and contracting.

- Identify and build relationships with multiple stakeholders within prospective accounts, including senior decision-makers and executive sponsors.

- Understand customer decision criteria, buying processes, organizational priorities, procurement requirements, and potential barriers to purchase.

- Tailor messaging, demonstrations, and business cases to customer priorities, clearly articulating Knak's differentiation, expected business impact, and return on investment.

- Maintain accurate and current CRM data, establish clear next steps and close plans, and regularly assess deal health and risk.

- Provide timely, evidence-based pipeline forecasts to Sales Leadership.

- Make informed decisions about opportunity prioritization, stakeholder engagement, deal strategy, and resource allocation.

- Collaborate with Sales Development, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, and Sales Leadership to create a coordinated customer experience.

- Share customer and market insights with internal teams and engage the appropriate cross-functional resources throughout the sales process.

- Continuously improve sales effectiveness by seeking feedback, reviewing performance, learning from wins and losses, and deepening product and industry knowledge.

- Refine prospecting, discovery, demonstration, negotiation, and closing skills to take on increasingly complex opportunities.

- Achieve assigned new business revenue targets while maintaining appropriate pipeline coverage.

- Represent Knak professionally with prospective customers, from day-to-day practitioners to senior executives.

 Skills & Experience 

- Proven experience in B2B SaaS sales, ideally selling into mid-market and/or enterprise organizations.

- Demonstrated track record of meeting or exceeding revenue targets.

- Experience owning a full sales cycle, from discovery and qualification through negotiation and close.

- Strong consultative selling and discovery skills, with the ability to uncover business challenges and underlying customer needs.

- Ability to navigate multi-stakeholder sales processes and engage confidently with senior decision-makers.

- Strong presentation, demonstration, negotiation, and written and verbal communication skills.

- Ability to articulate business value and translate product capabilities into relevant customer outcomes.

- Strong pipeline management, forecasting, organization, and time-management skills.

- Comfort using CRM and sales technology to manage opportunities and make data-informed decisions.

- A curious, proactive, and coachable approach, with a focus on continuous improvement.

- Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across teams.

 Base Salary: The anticipated base salary range for this position is $90,000-110,000. Final compensation will be determined based on factors including relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity. This range reflects base salary only and does not include other forms of compensation that may be available as part of the total rewards package. 
 What We Offer 

 At Knak we have four foundational pillars. Culture, customers, product and growth. Culture is our number one pillar because we know that is at the core of building a strong company that can build amazing products and delight our customers. We do this with a laser focus on hiring the right people who are smart, positive and who want more than the typical nine-to-five offers. 

 We offer an extremely rewarding, second to none work environment as acknowledged by Ottawa’s Best Places to Work 2025 ! We show our investment in our people through our competitive salaries, equity in the company, great benefits, paid vacation, Life leave days (because life happens), team lunches and off-sites, and most importantly our commitment to YOUR career growth.

 If this sounds like something you’re looking for, then we’d love to hear from you! 

 If you don’t see yourself fully reflected in every job requirement listed on the posting above, we still encourage you to reach out and apply. Research has shown that women and underrepresented groups often only apply when they feel 100% qualified. We strongly encourage applicants of all genders, ages, ethnicities, cultures, abilities, sexual orientations, and life experiences to apply. Knak believes in creating an inclusive, barrier-free working environment. If you require ANY accommodation to the interview process please contact culture@knak.com. 

 At Knak, our recruitment process includes AI screening for keywords and minimum qualifications as well as video interviews which are transcribed with AI. Humans are still at the core of our decision making! Please note that this job post is for an existing vacancy.

Knak is a mission-driven company 

 Why? Because our time is limited, our competition is fierce, and our margin for error is small. To have the biggest impact on the world, we stay focused on our core mission, which is...

 Empowering marketers to be creative . 

 That’s why Knak exists.

 In a world where AI has made everyone a creator, Knak helps marketers turn ideas into on-brand, high-performing campaigns at scale. The world's most AI-forward companies, including Meta, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Vercel, Notion and Stripe, use Knak as their agentic marketing production layer.

 Here's what they and our investor Insight Partners figured out: creation got easy, but that’s making production harder. Every new idea and brief still has to be built, versioned, checked, approved, and shipped across every channel, and that work runs on handoffs, review cycles, and a lot of copy-paste. That middle stretch of the marketing stack has no system, no standard, and no owner.

 Knak is the flexible factory for that work. Our customers set the brand rules, choose the tools that feed in and the platforms that send, and decide where AI does the work and where people do. We handle the repeatable parts, so marketers get their time back for the parts that aren't.

 We're built by marketers, for marketers. We started with email because it's the hardest channel to get right and where many campaigns win or lose. Now we're bringing that same production discipline to every channel our customers use.

 AI made everyone a creator. It didn't make anyone a producer. 

 Every enterprise marketing team on the planet just got faster at making things. AI drafts the copy, generates the image, spins up ten variants before lunch.

 Then it all stops in the same place.

 Someone still has to actually build the thing. Keep it on brand. Localize it into nine languages. QA it across forty email clients. Get legal to sign off. Push it into Marketo or Eloqua without breaking the template. That work didn't get faster. It got busier.

 That's the production layer. That's where Knak lives.

 Uber, Stripe, Meta, AWS and Nvidia use Knak to produce the campaigns their customers actually see. We started with email. We added landing pages. Mobile messaging — SMS and RCS — ships this September, and more channels are on the roadmap. Underneath all of it, we're putting AI agents to work inside the production process.

 So: the product is expanding, the buyer set is expanding, and the category we're building doesn't have a name yet in most marketers' heads.

 That's our job! 

 The role 

 This is the first hire into a product marketing function we're rebuilding from the ground up. Reporting to the VP of Product Marketing, you'll drive product marketing for the entire portfolio, not a slice of it. 

 The three most important things we need someone to drive at the moment: 

- Messaging and the product marketing content that sells it. Build the narrative for what Product is shipping, and the decks, pages, and stories for the people who need to hear it.

- Launches. Run them end to end, across Product, Sales, Enablement, and Marketing, to drive pipeline, adoption and revenue. 

- Customer marketing. Drive marketing to the enterprises we’ve already won, so they adopt more, buy more, and stay. 

 We're hiring at either the Product Marketing Manager or Senior Product Marketing Manager level. Show us what you've done and we'll size the role to it.

 What you'll own 

 Build the narrative and the content that carries it 

 You'll sit close enough to the PMs across email, landing pages, mobile messaging, integrations, and AI to shape the story early. 

- Develop messaging across the portfolio that resonates with target buyers, and that a competitor couldn’t paste onto their own website. 

- Create content that carries the messaging: pitch decks, one-pagers, battlecards, demo narratives, web copy, product videos, customer stories

- Talk to customers regularly. Steal their words. Use them.

- Keep a working point of view on the competitive set and where the market is heading

 Run launches that change what people do 

 A launch that generates a blog post and a Slack message isn't a launch. You'll own the whole arc, from the brief to the number.

- Own go-to-market for new products and features, end to end

- Set launch tiers so a template tweak and a new channel don't get the same treatment

- Get Sales, CSMs, and Enablement genuinely ready — training, plays, objection handling, discovery questions

- Report on what happened: adoption, attach rate, pipeline, win rate. Then fix what didn't work.

 Grow the accounts we already won 

 Large enterprises are our sweet spot, and most of them use a slice of what we can do for them. You'll build the customer marketing motion that changes that.

- Build campaigns to our installed base that drive adoption, expansion, and retention

- Arm CSMs and Sales with the plays, proof, and content to run expansion conversations without waiting on you

- Introduce Knak to the marketers a new channel brings with it — mobile messaging and landing pages pull in people who've never touched our email builder

- Turn customer wins into proof: stories, benchmarks, and stats a champion can carry into their own business case

 What year one looks like 

 First 90 days. You know the product, the buyers, and the top ten accounts cold. You've talked to at least fifteen customers. You've shipped messaging for one product area that Sales is already using in live deals.

 By six months. You've run a full launch end to end and can point to what it moved. Enablement for your product areas is something Sales asks for rather than something you push.

 By twelve months. Customer marketing is a running motion, not a project. Expansion pipeline from the installed base is measurably up, and you own a number you're proud to report.

 Who you are 

- 4+ years in B2B product marketing , ideally in SaaS sold to enterprise buyers. (Senior level: 6+, with launches you led rather than supported.)

- You write well. Clearly, specifically, in the customer's words. You've turned a complicated product into a sentence a seller can repeat without a cheat sheet.

- You've launched things that worked — and you can tell us what the result was, not just what the plan was.

- You get cross-functional teams moving without owning them. PMs, AEs, CSMs, designers, campaign managers. Influence over authority.

- You finish. Details, deadlines, and follow-through. This function is small and there's no one behind you catching things.

- You're a self-starter with a competitive streak. You'd rather bring a recommendation than ask what to do next.

- You're comfortable with ambiguity, because the category we're in is still being defined and some of the answers don't exist yet.

 Bonus points for: 

- Experience with enterprise marketing automation — Marketo, Eloqua, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Pardot — or having been a marketing ops or campaign practitioner yourself

- Customer marketing, lifecycle, or expansion-focused product marketing experience

- Multi-product or platform portfolios, especially where new channels brought new personas

- Marketing AI-native capabilities to buyers who are rightly skeptical of AI claims

 What this role is not 

 Being straight with you saves us both time.

- This isn't a demand gen role. You'll partner closely with campaigns, but you're not running paid media.

- This isn't a content mill. We need strategy and judgment, not volume.

- There's no team under you today. Lead through influence now; build later as we grow.

- If you want tightly defined scope and a clear playbook handed to you, this will frustrate you. If you want to write the playbook, keep reading.

 Base Salary: The anticipated base salary range for this position is $120,000 to $160,000. Final compensation will be determined based on factors including relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity. This range reflects base salary only and does not include other forms of compensation that may be available as part of the total rewards package. 
 What We Offer 

 At Knak we have four foundational pillars. Culture, customers, product and growth. Culture is our number one pillar because we know that is at the core of building a strong company that can build amazing products and delight our customers. We do this with a laser focus on hiring the right people who are smart, positive and who want more than the typical nine-to-five offers. 

 We offer an extremely rewarding, second to none work environment as acknowledged by Ottawa’s Best Places to Work 2025 ! We show our investment in our people through our competitive salaries, equity in the company, great benefits, paid vacation, Life leave days (because life happens), team lunches and off-sites, and most importantly our commitment to YOUR career growth.

 If this sounds like something you’re looking for, then we’d love to hear from you! 

 If you don’t see yourself fully reflected in every job requirement listed on the posting above, we still encourage you to reach out and apply. Research has shown that women and underrepresented groups often only apply when they feel 100% qualified. We strongly encourage applicants of all genders, ages, ethnicities, cultures, abilities, sexual orientations, and life experiences to apply. Knak believes in creating an inclusive, barrier-free working environment. If you require ANY accommodation to the interview process please contact culture@knak.com. 

 At Knak, our recruitment process includes AI screening for keywords and minimum qualifications as well as video interviews which are transcribed with AI. Humans are still at the core of our decision making! Please note that this job post is for an existing vacancy.

lever:knix:54dc67f5-9adb-4a76-98f2-80ce8.title: Director, Brand & Growth - Mntd
lever:knix:54dc67f5-9adb-4a76-98f2-80ce8.description:
Knix is an award-winning intimate apparel and activewear brand that is re-inventing intimates for real life. Through our innovative products and our engaged community, we are empowering people everywhere to be unapologetically free.  Launched in 2013, we are one of the fastest-growing intimate apparel brands in North America and are globally recognized as an innovator within the apparel space.  We reach over 3 million customers through our online stores, Knix retail locations across North America and channels such as wholesale and Amazon.  We are revolutionizing the apparel industry with our best-in-class customer experience, innovative products and brands Knix, Kt by Knix, and Mntd.  Come join us if you are looking for a purpose-driven and authentic career! MNTD is looking for a highly entrepreneurial, commercially minded brand leader to help build the next stage of the business. This is a broad, hands-on leadership role for someone who knows how to build a brand and grow a business at the same time. You will own the day-to-day performance of MNTD while shaping how the brand shows up in the market, from growth strategy and digital marketing to campaigns, retail, partnerships, storytelling, customer experience and commercial planning. You will operate with the speed and resourcefulness of an early-stage business, while having access to the capabilities, infrastructure and expertise of the broader Knix organization. The right person is equally comfortable developing the strategy, reviewing a P&L, briefing a creative campaign, managing an agency, evaluating paid media performance, building a retail or brand partnership and jumping in to solve an executional problem when needed. This role requires someone who creates momentum rather than waits for direction. You should be excited by ambiguity, motivated by growth and comfortable moving between big-picture thinking and detailed execution. What You'll Own:

Build the MNTD Brand

  • Develop and execute the annual brand and marketing strategy for MNTD, translating business goals into clear consumer-facing plans.

  • Build integrated campaigns that create awareness, conversation and demand across paid, owned, earned and retail channels.

  • Shape the stories MNTD tells around its products, consumer, innovation and brand point of view.

  • Identify cultural moments, partnerships, collaborations, creators and brand opportunities that can introduce MNTD to new audiences.

  • Build a consistent marketing calendar across product launches, campaigns, partnerships, promotions, retail moments and key brand milestones.

  • Partner with creative teams, agencies and external talent to bring ideas to market quickly while maintaining a clear and differentiated brand identity.

  • Develop a strong understanding of the MNTD customer and use consumer insights, performance data and cultural signals to guide decisions.

    • Drive Growth

    • Build an integrated growth plan that connects brand marketing, digital acquisition, retention, retail and partnerships.

    • Understand the full customer journey from awareness through acquisition, conversion, retail engagement, retention and repeat purchase.

    • Partner with internal eCommerce experts to continually improve site experience, merchandising, landing pages and conversion.

    • Oversee email and SMS strategy, including campaigns, lifecycle marketing, segmentation and retention.

    • Identify and test new channels, audiences, partnerships and growth opportunities while building a disciplined approach to measurement and learning.

    • Balance short-term revenue opportunities with the longer-term work required to build brand awareness, customer demand and market presence.

    • Use retail as a meaningful growth and brand-building channel, connecting physical experiences with digital marketing and broader commercial goals.

      • Own the Business

      • Own the MNTD P&L and understand the levers driving revenue, gross margin, marketing investment and profitability.

      • Build annual and quarterly commercial plans and regularly evaluate performance against them.

      • Track the metrics that matter, including revenue, traffic, conversion, AOV, CAC, LTV, retention, retail performance, margin and marketing efficiency.

      • Lead weekly and monthly business reviews, identifying what is working, where performance is off track and what actions need to happen next.

      • Partner with finance, inventory, operations, retail and eCommerce teams on forecasting, demand planning, inventory and promotional decisions.

      • Make thoughtful tradeoffs across brand investment, customer acquisition, retail growth, margin and near-term revenue.

      • Build processes and operating rhythms that allow the business to move quickly without creating unnecessary complexity.

        • Lead and Execute

        • Own the growth strategy across paid media, CRM, organic, retail, partnerships, creators and emerging acquisition channels.

        • Act as the day-to-day leader for MNTD, connecting the work happening across marketing, eCommerce, retail, creative, growth, merchandising, operations and finance.

        • Set clear priorities and keep teams focused on the initiatives with the greatest impact.

        • Lead agency partners across media, creative, PR, partnerships and other external disciplines, including setting expectations, managing budgets and holding partners accountable for results.

        • Manage internal team members as well as agencies, freelancers and external partners.

        • Work closely with retail teams to develop launches, in-store moments, activations and customer experiences that build awareness and drive revenue.

        • Identify when to leverage Knix shared capabilities and when MNTD needs a different or more entrepreneurial approach.

        • Build the team and external partner network thoughtfully as the business grows.

        • Stay close enough to the work to step in and execute when necessary. No task is too strategic or too tactical when it moves the business forward.

What We're Looking For:

  • 8+ years of experience across brand, growth, digital marketing, retail, eCommerce or general management, ideally within a consumer brand.

  • A track record of building brands and driving commercial growth, not simply managing one marketing function.

  • Deep understanding of digital marketing, including paid social, paid search, CRM, creators, content and customer acquisition.

  • Meaningful retail experience, including understanding how physical retail contributes to brand building, customer acquisition, conversion and omnichannel growth.

  • Experience developing integrated campaigns and brand stories that generate consumer excitement and translate into business results.

  • Strong commercial instincts and experience owning or meaningfully managing a P&L, budget, revenue target or profitability goal.

  • Experience managing agencies and external partners across media, creative, PR, partnerships or related disciplines.

  • Strong understanding of eCommerce and the digital customer journey. You do not need to be a technical eCommerce specialist, but you should know how digital businesses work and what drives conversion and retention.

  • Comfortable using data to make decisions while understanding that not every important brand decision can be reduced to a single performance metric.

  • Experience operating in a fast-moving environment with limited resources, changing priorities and high expectations.

  • A builder mentality. You see what needs to happen, create a plan and move.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to prioritize when everything feels important.

  • Comfortable moving between strategy, management and hands-on execution.

  • Strong written, verbal and presentation skills.

    • Nice to Have

    • Experience in apparel, intimates, fashion, lifestyle or another consumer category.

    • Experience helping scale an early-stage or emerging brand.

    • Experience building teams or functions from the ground up.

    • Experience with collaborations, creators, PR or experiential marketing.

    • Experience working within a smaller brand that is supported by a larger parent organization.

Salary::
  • Annual salary starting at $135,000 CAD

About You::

  • Culturally Curious & Consumer-Obsessed: Genuine curiosity about Gen Alpha, parents, youth culture, and the changing conversation around periods and growing up, with exceptional instincts for identifying human tensions.

  • Creatively Ambitious & Solution-Oriented: Asking "what problem are we actually solving?" and using a strong creative mind to turn one powerful insight into compelling brand stories.

  • Commercially Minded & Data-Informed: A mindset that balances long-term brand building with commercial performance, comfortable using data and insights to challenge assumptions and drive business results.

  • Collaborative & Adaptive Leadership: Highly cross-functional leader capable of aligning multiple teams around a single clear idea while navigating ambiguity in a fast-paced DTC environment.

    • The Opportunity::

    Brand Strategy & Positioning

  • Define and evolve Kt.’s brand positioning, messaging and consumer value proposition.

  • Develop a deep understanding of our two key audiences: the tween wearing the product and the parent often purchasing it.

  • Translate consumer insights into clear, differentiated brand stories that drive both relevance and conversion.

  • Identify the problems Kt. can uniquely solve; from first-period anxiety and unpredictable cycles to swimming, sports, school and sleepovers.

  • Ensure our brand voice and positioning remain consistent while adapting appropriately by channel and audience.

    • Campaigns & Go-to-Market

  • Lead integrated campaign strategy for key brand moments, product launches and seasonal initiatives.

  • Develop briefs rooted in a clear consumer insight, business objective and desired behavior.

  • Own the marketing calendar and ensure Knixteen has a compelling year-round reason to be in the market.

  • Partner with Creative to turn strategic insights into breakthrough concepts and content.

  • Connect campaigns across paid media, owned channels, site, social, PR, influencers and partnerships rather than treating each channel independently.

  • Build launch strategies that move beyond product features to clearly communicate why the product needs to exist in a tween’s life.

    • Social, Influencer & Culture

  • Define how Kt. participates in tween, teen, and parent culture.

  • Partner with Social and Influencer teams to build a creator strategy that generates authentic, useful and highly shareable content.

  • Identify emerging conversations, behaviors and cultural moments where Kt. has permission to participate.

  • Develop programs that make Kt. a trusted resource for first periods and growing up, not simply a brand selling period underwear.

  • Identify partnerships, communities and voices that can meaningfully expand brand awareness and credibility.

  • Regularly bring the voice of tweens and parents into business decisions through research, social listening, reviews, customer feedback, search behavior and performance data.

  • Identify unmet needs, anxieties and behaviors that can become new marketing territories.

  • Turn insights into actionable opportunities for Marketing, Product, Merchandising and E-commerce.

    • Brand Growth & Performance

  • Partner closely with Growth and E-commerce to ensure brand strategy translates into measurable business results.

  • Understand campaign performance across awareness, traffic, acquisition, conversion and repeat purchase.

  • Use performance data to identify which messages, products and consumer problems are resonating and evolve the strategy accordingly.

  • Balance long-term brand building with the commercial realities of a fast-growing DTC business.

    • Qualifications::

  • 6–8+ years of experience in brand marketing, consumer marketing or integrated marketing, ideally within DTC, apparel, beauty, wellness or another consumer-led category.

  • Experience owning campaigns from consumer insight through creative development, launch and performance analysis.

  • Strong understanding of modern brand building across paid, owned, social, influencer, PR and e-commerce.

  • Exceptional consumer instincts and an ability to uncover the human tension behind a business problem.

  • Strong creative judgment and experience writing briefs that lead to great work.

  • Commercial mindset; you care about the brand and whether the work actually drives the business.

  • Comfortable using data to challenge assumptions and improve marketing strategy.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership skills and the ability to bring multiple teams around one clear idea.

  • Ability to operate with ambiguity, move quickly and build rather than wait for a perfect process.

  • Genuine curiosity about Gen Alpha, parents, youth culture and the changing conversation around periods and growing up.

lever:knix:9a46a21d-1c81-4544-8d3c-d7629.title: Sr. UX/UI Designer
lever:knix:9a46a21d-1c81-4544-8d3c-d7629.description:
Knix is an award-winning intimate apparel and activewear brand that is re-inventing intimates for real life. Through our innovative products and our engaged community, we are empowering people everywhere to be unapologetically free.  Launched in 2013, we are one of the fastest-growing intimate apparel brands in North America and are globally recognized as an innovator within the apparel space.  We reach over 3 million customers through our online stores, Knix retail locations across North America and channels such as wholesale and Amazon.  We are revolutionizing the apparel industry with our best-in-class customer experience, innovative products and brands Knix, Kt by Knix, and Mntd.  Come join us if you are looking for a purpose-driven and authentic career! We're looking for a Senior UX/UI Designer to own and elevate the end-to-end design quality of our eCommerce experience. This is a high-impact, highly visible role, you'll be the single owner of our site's visual and interaction language, setting the standard for how the Knix brand comes to life across every digital touchpoint as we scale and a chance to work on a world-class brand to showcase your UX thinking and design skills. If you are a deeply skilled, execution-focused designer who takes pride in shipping beautiful, high-performing interfaces, this role was built for you. About You::

  • You are a craftsperson first,  you produce design work that is precise, considered, and visually distinctive.

  • You have a commercially focused design aptitude,  and know how to strike a good balance between high conversion and premium brand presentation in a fast moving environment. You understand key engagement and DTC KPIs that drive funnel optimization 

  • You have strong opinions about UI quality and can articulate and defend design decisions to stakeholders at all levels.

  • You move fluidly between big-picture thinking and pixel-level execution without losing momentum.

  • You are familiar with and utilize AI tools in order to ideate and optimize your workflow

  • You are proactive about identifying friction in the current experience and come armed with solutions, not just observations.

  • You are deeply familiar with eCommerce UX patterns and know what drives conversion, clarity, and brand trust on the web.

  • You thrive as a strong individual contributor and are energized by owning a design system end-to-end rather than working within one someone else built.

  • You communicate clearly, collaborate constructively, and manage your own workload without needing heavy oversight.

  • Above all, you're energized by Knix's mission and excited by the scale of the opportunity in front of us.

    • The Opportunity:

  • Own the UX/UI direction for our Knix, KT, and MNTD from homepage to checkout, ensuring every surface reflects a cohesive, elevated, and on-brand experience.

  • Lead the upcoming redesign and ongoing optimization of key eCommerce templates, including the PDP, PLP, homepage, cart, and checkout flows.

  • Establish and maintain a living design system that scales across web and mobile web, serving as the source of truth for all UI components, tokens, and interaction patterns.

  • Partner closely with eCommerce, Product, and Engineering to translate business requirements into clear, buildable design solutions delivered on time.

  • Drive iterative UI improvements grounded in performance data, heuristic review, and competitive benchmarking,  not just aesthetic preference.

  • Develop motion and interaction design specs for key micro-interactions, transitions, and animated elements where they enhance the customer experience. (A strong plus.)

  • Contribute to and review creative executions, ensuring campaign landing pages, editorial features, and seasonal moments stay on-system.

  • Present design work to cross-functional stakeholders and leadership, providing clear rationale and context for design decisions.

  • Actively champion design quality across the organization — raising the bar, educating partners, and pushing back thoughtfully when standards slip.

  • Own research strategy, not just execution: Translate our product roadmap into a clear, actionable research plan. Identify knowledge gaps, define hypotheses, and lead customer research initiatives (qualitative and quantitative) to inform product direction.

    • Qualifications::

  • 6+ years of UX/UI design experience, with a significant portion focused on direct-to-consumer eCommerce or digital retail.

  • An exceptional portfolio demonstrating sophisticated visual design skill, strong interaction thinking, and measurable eCommerce outcomes.

  • Expert-level proficiency in Figma (or similar), including component libraries, auto-layout, variables, and prototyping.

  • Working knowledge of gen AI/LLM tools as it relates to UX/UI workflows

  • Solid working knowledge of HTML/CSS fundamentals,  enough to communicate with developers fluently and understand implementation constraints.

  • Experience owning or significantly contributing to a design system in a production environment.

  • Familiarity with CRO principles and the ability to design with conversion metrics in mind.

  • Experience with or strong interest in motion and interaction design — familiarity with tools such as Principle, Rive, or After Effects is a plus.

  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to sell a design vision clearly to non-designers.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and a high standard for visual quality.

    • Salary Expectations:
  • Annual salary starting $115,000.00 CAD

ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.




ABOUT THE ROLE

At KOHO, Product Design is key to our brand identity and product differentiation. As a Senior Product Designer, you will be involved in every aspect of the product development process. You will be using your skills in UI and UX design, product design, interaction design, visual / audio / motion design and prototyping to create product experiences that wow and deliver measurable value.

We’re looking for someone who embraces innovation, including the use of Generative AI and other AI-powered tools to speed up workflows, explore creative solutions, and enhance design decision-making. Our dream candidate has a passion for understanding users and enjoys working closely with other designers, engineers, data analysts, and product managers to build the best banking experience for Canadians.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a seasoned Director - Privacy Office (Deputy Chief Privacy Officer); Head of Advisory and RCM to lead the advisory heart of KOHO’s Compliance function and to own our Privacy Office end to end. Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, you will be the trusted advisor to our business partners, such as product (lending, core banking, growth & onboarding), marketing, and user success, and before they build — translating a dense regulatory landscape into clear and useful guidance. You will also own KOHO’s privacy program, from Privacy Impact Assessments and consent design through to breach response.

 

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is energized by ambiguity, comfortable being the decision-maker in the room, and motivated by building durable programs rather than inheriting them. If you believe compliance should make good products possible rather than merely permissible, you’ll do your best work here.

 


WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING


COMPLIANCE ADVISORY

 - Act as the primary compliance advisor to business partners such as Product (lending, core banking, growth & onboarding), Marketing, Technology, Payments, Partnerships, and User Success, providing timely, practical, risk-based guidance on new products, features, campaigns, and business arrangements.

 - Own the regulatory advisory and interpretation function, resolving novel questions with clear written positions and a defensible rationale that stands up to regulatory and audit scrutiny.

 - Lead compliance review and sign-off of marketing materials, disclosures, and customer communications, and embed obligations into product development early.

 - Own the Whistleblower and Ethics programs, including intake, investigation oversight, non-retaliation, and ethics reporting to the Board.


REGULATORY COMPLIANCE MANAGEMENT

 - In collaboration with Legal, own the regulatory compliance management program: horizon scanning, impact assessment, and coordinated implementation of new and amended regulatory requirements.

 - Maintain KOHO’s regulatory obligations inventory and the mapping of obligations to responsible business owners, policies, and controls.

 - Lead the development, refresh, and governance of compliance policies, standards, and procedures, including annual approval cycles.


PRIVACY OFFICE (DEPUTY CHIEF PRIVACY OFFICER)

 - Own and mature KOHO’s enterprise privacy program, aligned to privacy legislation, and act as KOHO’s designated privacy lead.

 - Establish and run the Privacy Impact Assessment process for new products, vendors, data uses, and technology changes, and govern consent, collection, use, disclosure, retention, and cross-border transfer of personal information on a privacy-by-design basis.

 - Lead privacy incident and breach response, including containment coordination, real-risk-of-significant-harm assessments, regulatory and individual notification, and root cause remediation.

 - Own privacy complaints and access and correction requests, the data inventory and privacy notices, and privacy training and awareness across the organization.


TEAM LEADERSHIP AND INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT

 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of compliance and privacy professionals, setting clear priorities and raising the technical bar of the function.

 - Partner closely with Financial Crime, Compliance Testing, Operational Risk, Internal Audit, Legal, and Tech/Cyber to ensure integrated coverage and no gaps between mandates.

 - Represent KOHO externally with industry associations, peer forums, and regulator outreach, staying ahead of emerging compliance, privacy, and conduct risk trends.

 - Prepare and present clear, decision-ready materials for senior management and applicable Board-level committees.


AI, AUTOMATION AND INNOVATION

 - Apply AI, automation, and data analytics to advisory intake, regulatory horizon scanning, marketing review, and privacy assessments.

 - Advise the business on the responsible use of AI, including model transparency, fairness, explainability, and personal information use.

 - Evaluate and implement RegTech and privacy technology that improves speed and consistency without diluting rigour.


WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 10+ years of progressive compliance, privacy, or regulatory legal experience in financial services, with meaningful time spent in an advisory capacity.

 - You have deep working knowledge of Canadian consumer protection, retail banking or payments, and privacy legislation.

 - You have built or substantially matured a privacy program or regulatory change program, not just operated one someone else designed.

 - You are a strong people leader and a clear writer — you can give a straight answer to a hard question and explain the reasoning behind it.

 - You’ve worked in regulated fintech, neobank, or direct-to-consumer financial institutions, you’re passionate about empowering financial wellness, and a relevant designation (CIPP/C, CAMS, CRCM, LL.B/JD, or equivalent) is an asset.

The budgeted salary range for this role is $190,000-230,000 CAD / year.  

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.




DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS


À PROPOS DU POSTE

Nous sommes à la recherche d’une personne chevronnée pour diriger les services-conseils — le cœur de la fonction Conformité de KOHO — et prendre en charge l’ensemble de notre Bureau de la protection des renseignements personnels. Relevant de la cheffe ou du chef de la conformité, vous serez la personne-ressource de confiance de nos partenaires d’affaires, notamment les équipes Produits (prêts, services bancaires de base, croissance et intégration), Marketing et Expérience utilisateur. Votre rôle consistera à traduire un environnement réglementaire complexe en conseils clairs et utiles, en amont de la conception de leurs produits et initiatives.

Vous serez également responsable du programme de protection des renseignements personnels de KOHO, de bout en bout : évaluations des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée, conception des mécanismes de consentement, gestion des incidents et intervention en cas d’atteinte à la protection des renseignements personnels.

Il s’agit d’un rôle de leadership très concret, pour une personne qui aime évoluer dans l’ambiguïté, qui est à l’aise de prendre des décisions et qui souhaite bâtir des programmes durables plutôt que de simplement assurer le maintien de programmes existants. Si vous croyez que la conformité doit rendre possibles de bons produits — et pas seulement les rendre permis —, vous pourrez vous épanouir pleinement dans ce rôle.


CE QUE VOUS FEREZ


SERVICES-CONSEILS EN CONFORMITÉ

 - Agir comme principale personne-conseil en conformité auprès des partenaires d’affaires, notamment les équipes Produits (prêts, services bancaires de base, croissance et intégration), Marketing, Technologie, Paiements, Partenariats et Expérience utilisateur, en fournissant des conseils rapides, pratiques et fondés sur les risques pour les nouveaux produits, les fonctionnalités, les campagnes et les ententes commerciales.

 - Diriger la fonction de conseil et d’interprétation réglementaires, résoudre les questions inédites et formuler des positions claires, écrites et appuyées par une analyse défendable qui résiste à l’examen des organismes de réglementation et de l’audit.

 - Diriger l’examen et l’approbation de conformité des documents marketing, des communications aux clients et des informations à fournir, et intégrer les exigences réglementaires dès les premières étapes du développement des produits.

 - Être responsable des programmes de dénonciation et d’éthique, notamment la réception des signalements, la supervision des enquêtes, la protection contre les représailles et la présentation de rapports sur l’éthique au conseil d’administration.


GESTION DE LA CONFORMITÉ RÉGLEMENTAIRE

 - En collaboration avec le service juridique, être responsable du programme de gestion de la conformité réglementaire : veille réglementaire, évaluation des répercussions et mise en œuvre coordonnée des exigences nouvelles ou modifiées.

 - Tenir à jour l’inventaire des obligations réglementaires de KOHO et établir la correspondance entre ces obligations, les responsables d’affaires, les politiques et les contrôles en place.

 - Diriger l’élaboration, la mise à jour et la gouvernance des politiques, normes et procédures de conformité, y compris les cycles annuels d’approbation.


BUREAU DE LA PROTECTION DES RENSEIGNEMENTS PERSONNELS

 - Prendre en charge et faire évoluer le programme d’entreprise de protection des renseignements personnels de KOHO, conformément aux lois applicables, et agir à titre de personne responsable de la protection des renseignements personnels désignée par KOHO.

 - Mettre en place et administrer le processus d’évaluation des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée (EFVP) pour les nouveaux produits, les fournisseurs, les utilisations de données et les changements technologiques. Encadrer le consentement ainsi que la collecte, l’utilisation, la communication, la conservation et le transfert transfrontalier de renseignements personnels selon une approche de protection de la vie privée dès la conception.

 - Diriger la réponse aux incidents et aux atteintes à la protection des renseignements personnels, notamment la coordination du confinement, l’évaluation du risque de préjudice sérieux, les avis aux organismes de réglementation et aux personnes concernées, ainsi que la mise en œuvre des mesures correctives visant à éliminer les causes profondes.

 - Être responsable des plaintes en matière de protection des renseignements personnels, des demandes d’accès et de rectification, de l’inventaire des données, des avis de confidentialité ainsi que de la formation et de la sensibilisation à l’échelle de l’organisation.


LEADERSHIP D’ÉQUIPE ET RAYONNEMENT DANS LE SECTEUR

 - Diriger, accompagner et faire progresser une équipe de spécialistes de la conformité et de la protection des renseignements personnels, en établissant des priorités claires et en rehaussant le niveau d’expertise technique de la fonction.

 - Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Crimes financiers, Tests de conformité, Risques opérationnels, Audit interne, Affaires juridiques et Technologie/Cybersécurité afin d’assurer une couverture intégrée et d’éviter les angles morts entre les différents mandats.

 - Représenter KOHO auprès d’associations sectorielles, de groupes de pairs et d’organismes de réglementation, et demeurer au fait des tendances émergentes en matière de conformité, de protection des renseignements personnels et de risques liés aux pratiques commerciales.

 - Préparer et présenter des documents clairs, axés sur la prise de décision, à la haute direction et aux comités pertinents du conseil d’administration.


INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE, AUTOMATISATION ET INNOVATION

 - Utiliser l’intelligence artificielle, l’automatisation et l’analytique des données pour améliorer la gestion des demandes de conseil, la veille réglementaire, l’examen du matériel marketing et les évaluations des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée.

 - Conseiller l’entreprise sur l’utilisation responsable de l’intelligence artificielle, notamment en matière de transparence des modèles, d’équité, d’explicabilité et d’utilisation des renseignements personnels.

 - Évaluer et mettre en œuvre des solutions de technologie réglementaire et de protection des renseignements personnels qui améliorent la rapidité et la cohérence des processus sans en réduire la rigueur.


PROFIL RECHERCHÉ

 - Vous possédez au moins 10 ans d’expérience progressive en conformité, en protection des renseignements personnels ou en droit réglementaire dans le secteur des services financiers, dont une expérience substantielle en services-conseils.

 - Vous avez une connaissance approfondie de la protection des consommateurs au Canada, des services bancaires de détail ou des paiements, ainsi que des lois relatives à la protection des renseignements personnels.

 - Vous avez bâti ou fait évoluer de façon importante un programme de protection des renseignements personnels ou de gestion des changements réglementaires — vous n’avez pas uniquement assuré l’exploitation d’un programme conçu par quelqu’un d’autre.

 - Vous êtes une personne gestionnaire solide et une excellente rédactrice ou un excellent rédacteur : vous savez donner une réponse claire à une question difficile et en expliquer le raisonnement.

 - Vous avez travaillé dans une entreprise de technologie financière réglementée, une néobanque ou une institution financière s’adressant directement aux consommateurs. Vous avez à cœur de favoriser la santé financière et une certification pertinente — CIPP/C, CAMS, CRCM, LL. B./J.D. ou équivalent — constitue un atout.
