Data Platform Account Executive – Eastern Canada (Multi-Cloud) 

 Drive Business Transformation Through Data, AI, and Multi-Cloud Innovation

 Oracle is seeking a bilingual (French and English), high-performing Data Platform Account Executive to drive growth across strategic Enterprise and Commercial customers throughout Eastern Canada.

 This individual contributor role spans all major industry verticals, helping organizations modernize how they leverage data, analytics, AI, database, and cloud technologies. You will own and develop strategic customer relationships, identify new opportunities, and help customers modernize their data architectures, accelerate AI adoption, and drive business transformation through Oracle's industry-leading Data Platform and multi-cloud portfolio.

 If you thrive in complex enterprise sales, enjoy building relationships with senior executives, and are passionate about helping customers solve their most important technology and business challenges, we'd love to meet you.

 What You'll Do

- Own, develop, and grow a portfolio of strategic Enterprise and Commercial accounts across Eastern Canada, spanning multiple industries and customer segments. 

- Build trusted relationships with C-level executives and senior business and technology stakeholders, including CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, CISOs, CFOs, and business leaders. 

- Drive sales of Oracle's AI Data Platform, Database, Analytics, AI, and Cloud solutions, developing new opportunities and expanding Oracle's footprint within existing customers. 

- Lead strategic customer conversations around data modernization, AI adoption, analytics transformation, cloud modernization, operational efficiency, and digital innovation. 

- Position Oracle as a strategic partner for multi-cloud and hybrid cloud transformation, helping customers leverage Oracle technology across Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud. 

- Develop and execute comprehensive account and territory strategies that align Oracle's technology portfolio with customers' business priorities and transformation initiatives. 

- Generate, develop, manage, and close complex enterprise opportunities while maintaining a strong pipeline, disciplined sales process, and accurate forecast. 

- Identify and develop net-new business opportunities while expanding relationships and technology adoption within Oracle's existing customer base. 

- Partner closely with Sales Engineering, OCI, AI, Applications, Consulting, Customer Success, Industry, Marketing, and Alliances to bring the full value of Oracle to customers. 

- Build relationships with Global Systems Integrators (GSIs), cloud partners, Independent Software Vendors (ISVs), and other ecosystem partners to identify opportunities and accelerate customer transformation. 

- Orchestrate cross-functional teams throughout complex sales cycles, from initial customer engagement and solution development through commercial negotiations and successful close. 

- Represent Oracle in executive customer meetings, industry events, partner engagements, and other strategic forums across Eastern Canada. 

 Market & Customer Focus

 This role provides the opportunity to work across all major industries in Eastern Canada, including Financial Services, Telecommunications, Media, Technology, Retail, Manufacturing, Energy, Transportation, Utilities, Professional Services, and other strategic Enterprise and Commercial segments.

 You will work with customers to unlock greater value from their enterprise data through secure, scalable, AI-ready, and multi-cloud architectures while helping them address some of their most important technology and business priorities.

 As organizations increasingly look to AI to improve productivity, automate processes, enhance customer experiences, and create new sources of competitive advantage, you will help executives understand how a modern data foundation can accelerate their AI strategy.

 Oracle's AI Data Platform, Database, Analytics, AI, OCI, and multi-cloud capabilities provide the foundation for customers to bring AI to their enterprise data while maintaining the performance, security, resiliency, and governance required for their most critical workloads.

 What We're Looking For

- 8+ years of successful enterprise technology sales experience, with a demonstrated ability to develop and close complex, strategic opportunities. 

- Bilingual proficiency in French and English, with the ability to engage business and technology executives in both languages. 

- Experience selling Data Platforms, Databases, Analytics, AI, Cloud Infrastructure, SaaS, PaaS, or related enterprise technology solutions. 

- Demonstrated success building relationships and selling to CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, CISOs, CFOs, and other senior executive stakeholders. 

- Proven track record of achieving or exceeding quota, developing new business, expanding strategic accounts, and closing complex enterprise opportunities. 

- Strong understanding of modern data architectures, AI/ML, analytics, databases, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise technology transformation. 

- Familiarity with multi-cloud strategies and technologies spanning OCI, Microsoft Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud. 

- Strong prospecting and business-development capabilities with the ability to create new opportunities within both existing and prospective customers. 

- Exceptional account planning, communication, presentation, negotiation, and executive engagement skills. 

- Ability to navigate complex organizations, manage long and sophisticated sales cycles, and orchestrate cross-functional teams to deliver successful customer outcomes. 

- Self-motivated, accountable, and comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy across a large geographic territory. 

 Why Oracle

 Oracle delivers one of the industry's most comprehensive portfolios across Data, AI, Analytics, Database, Applications, and Cloud Infrastructure. Our differentiated multi-cloud strategy enables customers to modernize their most important workloads while leveraging the cloud platforms that best fit their business and technology strategies.

 As a Data Platform Account Executive for Eastern Canada, you will have the opportunity to work with some of Canada's most important organizations and executive leaders as they navigate the next generation of AI, data, cloud, and multi-cloud transformation.

 You'll have the opportunity to build a significant business, develop long-term executive relationships, create new opportunities, and help customers unlock the value of their enterprise data through Oracle's AI Data Platform.

 Join a team that is shaping the future of AI, data, and cloud transformation across Canada.

 Apply today and help organizations across Eastern Canada redefine what's possible with Data, AI, and Multi-Cloud innovation.

- Develop and execute account plans that drive renewals, mitigate churn risk, and uncover expansion opportunities.

- Experience using Salesforce (SFDC) and analytics tools such as Gainsight, Tableau, or Looker.

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Prior enterprise sales expertise leveraging MEDDPICC & Value Selling.

- Experience working with enterprise software customers or in a DevOps environment.

- Strong understanding of AI-powered tools and how they can be leveraged to drive efficiency and insight.

- Proven history of achieving revenue and retention goals through consultative account management.

 About the Role

 PagerDuty is seeking a Principal Product Manager, Platform Security to own the strategy and execution of how we secure, harden, and defend our Operations Cloud platform. This role sits within our Product Development organization and reports to the Sr Director of Product, Platform & Partners.

 This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll bring the same rigor to security that a great PM brings to a product: deep customer empathy, structured threat modeling, clear risk tiering frameworks, and a bias toward measurable outcomes. You'll also be the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, IT, and Legal, ensuring security strategy translates into engineering execution and customer trust. This role owns the full lifecycle from recommendation to implementation to operations. You'll be the decision-maker on risk acceptance, control exceptions, and incident escalation in real-time.

 The ideal candidate has operated at the intersection of product management and security engineering in a later-stage B2B SaaS environment. You've owned security architecture decisions end-to-end, built security infrastructure, and have the credibility to influence both product roadmaps and engineering practices without formal authority.

 What You'll Own

 Product & Platform Security

- Define and evolve PagerDuty's platform identity and security architecture — trust boundaries, authentication and authorization models, and secrets management frameworks

- Admin experience and admin console for enterprise and security administrators

- Build and maintain a security review process so product teams bring security into roadmap decisions early, not as an afterthought

- Own the security platform roadmap 

- Provide security and secure-design leadership to other product teams across the portfolio

 What You'll Build

 This role owns a portfolio of platform security surfaces that includes:

- Identity & Permissions platform — the authentication and authorization foundation for both human users and AI agents, spanning roles, scopes, and delegated access as agentic workflows become first-class actors on the platform

- Security products — customer-facing capabilities such as IP Allow list and SCIM, extending the set of controls enterprise customers need to adopt PagerDuty at scale

- Admin experience — the tooling administrators use to configure, audit, and govern their PagerDuty environment, with opportunity to improve clarity and self-service

- Partner security and governance — the shared services, primitives, and audit surfaces that every partner team builds on

- Partner with executive leadership to align security strategy with company-level trust and resilience targets

 The opportunity is to bring these surfaces together into a coherent platform so security decisions and actions happen faster, customers can govern their own environments with confidence, and product teams have primitives they trust and actively build on.

 Basic Qualifications

- 10+ years in B2B SaaS in roles spanning product management, security engineering, and/or platform security

- Demonstrated experience owning security architecture and risk tiering decisions — not just supporting them

- Track record of running security programs and measuring risk reduction impact

- Strong cross-functional credibility with Engineering, Legal, Product, and Go-To-Market leadership

- Experience managing security change in the field — migrations, re-architecture, new authentication and authorization models — with the communication skills to bring stakeholders along

- Ability to mentor other product managers and raise the security bar across a product organization without direct reports

 Preferred Qualifications

- Experience at a company during transition to zero-trust or hardened multi-tenant isolation architecture

- Familiarity with security infrastructure (IAM, secrets management, vulnerability and posture tooling)

- Familiarity with B2B SaaS compliance frameworks, customer security review processes, and audit considerations

dayforce:paymentscanada:6363.location: Payments Canada, 800-350 Albert Street, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada; Payments Canada, Toronto, Ontario, Canada
dayforce:paymentscanada:6363.description:
| What we are looking for
Reporting to the Director, Legal Affairs & Senior Legal Counsel, the Legal Counsel functions as part of a collegial team and provides strategic and business focused legal analysis and advice to Payments Canada relating to its statutory mandate, legal and regulatory framework (including the development and interpretation of Payments Canada’s enabling legislation, by-laws and rules), strategic goals, and general business affairs. As a trusted team player and peer mentor, the Legal Counsel readily shares their specialized knowledge and works to develop both their own expertise and skills and those of others. 
Legal Advice and Support Services

Support Payments Canada in its business operations and in achieving its strategic plan by proactively advising on a wide range of legal risks and issues, responding to internal and external legal inquiries, providing legal support on projects, and giving both strategic and operational legal advice on matters such as: 

the Canadian Payments Act, and Payments Canada’s by-laws, rules, and standards;
Banking and payments law;
Governance, regulatory oversight, and regulatory practices and requirements;
General corporate and commercial law;
Intellectual property; and
Information technology, Fintech, and emerging policy and legal issues.

Seek out opportunities and establish methods to share knowledge with legal and business partner colleagues to promote collaboration and the transfer of knowledge.
Participate in Legal team planning to help foster an environment of continuous improvement in the provision of efficient and effective legal support to Payments Canada.
Seek out, promote, and implement process and practice management improvements on an ongoing basis. 
Protect Payments Canada’s solicitor-client privilege and treat all matters involving the provision of legal advice in strictest confidence, as required by the duties of confidentiality and loyalty set out in the rules of professional conduct applicable to practicing lawyers.
Provide mentorship and guidance to colleagues across Payments Canada with respect to specific subject matter expertise.

Professional Development

The incumbent should expect to spend a minimum of 5-10 days annually on professional development in fulfillment of Law Society CPD requirements, and to maintain the skills required in the performance of the duties associated with this position.
Develop and maintain legal skills and expertise by seeking out peer learning opportunities and attending continuing legal education offerings tailored to develop professional and subject matter expertise.

Technical Competencies

Excellent legal research and drafting skills
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
Ability to identify risks and potential solutions when providing legal advice
Business acumen with an ability to balance legal risks and business objectives, influence business leaders, and deal effectively with conflict
Ability to work independently and as part of a team to produce high-quality work
Ability to devise innovative approaches to problems
Ability to provide concise guidance and advice

Personal Competencies

Critical reasoning and analytical thinking
Displays of social and self-awareness
High attention to detail and accuracy
Develops and apply innovative solutions as appropriate
Ability to quickly establish and maintain credibility and respect among colleagues and peers within and beyond Payments Canada
Exercises a high degree of initiative and flexibility
Recognizes the importance of strong communication and interpersonal skills
Excellent organizational and time management skills
Demonstrates commitment to continuous learning and skills development for self, and provides support to others via mentorship and knowledge sharing
Acts decisively and assertively as needed
Demonstrates excellent judgment and discretion
Strong interpersonal skills; the incumbent must maintain professional interactions and be able to respond to all employees, members and external contacts in a diplomatic manner

| What you need to be successful

Baccalaureate of Laws (LL. B) or Juris Doctor (J.D.);
Lawyer in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario;
Minimum of three (3) years of post-call corporate law experience in a law firm or in-house/corporate counsel position;
Experience in drafting and interpreting legislation, by-laws, rules and standards, and organizational policies;
Experience in reviewing, drafting, and negotiating contracts;
Experience in establishing and maintaining effective relationships with business partners, clients or stakeholders;
Experience in financial services and with federally regulated entities is considered an asset; 
Valid criminal records check or eligibility to obtain;
Ability to accommodate occasional travel, as required;
Must be able to work out of our Toronto or Ottawa offices;
Post-call corporate law experience in a law firm or in-house/corporate counsel position in Ontario is considered an asset; 
Experience or background in employment and labor law is considered an asset; and
Bilingualism (English and French) is considered an asset.

| Salary range
Our target starting rate for this role is $119,850 with flexibility based on your experience and qualifications. The full salary range and benefits package are detailed below.
Please submit your application by October 23, 2026.

dayforce:paymentscanada:6299.location: Payments Canada, 800-350 Albert Street, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada; Payments Canada, Toronto, Ontario, Canada
dayforce:paymentscanada:6299.description:
| What we are looking for
Reporting to the Manager, Security Compliance, this position carries out the day-to-day work of the Security Compliance function. Working from direction set by the Manager, the incumbent performs control assessments, gathers and documents evidence, keeps compliance trackers and registers current and prepares compliance reporting against internal mandates and external regulations. As a representative of the organization's security function, the incumbent helps promote a culture of security compliance among all employees and works day to day with colleagues across other Payments Canada divisions and with members and user groups as required. 

Duties and Responsibilities of the Security Compliance Analyst will include but is not limited to: 
Security Compliance 

Support the development of information security controls by drafting and documenting control statements against existing policies, standards, procedures, regulatory guidelines and security frameworks and routing them to stakeholders for feedback and approval.
Carry out assessments and validation of security controls across Payments Canada, following the approach and scope set by the Manager, Security Compliance.
Process and review Security Exception Requests, checking submissions for completeness, documenting the control gap and any compensating controls, and referring risk acceptance decisions to the Manager, Security Compliance.
Promote day-to-day compliance with internal policies, standards and procedures, and with external regulatory requirements.
Support security related audits (for example, ISO/IEC 27001 and the SWIFT CSP) by gathering evidence, preparing the requested documentation and responding to auditor questions within agreed timelines.
Respond promptly to routine security compliance questions, and escalate those that call for a decision to the Manager, Security Compliance.
Work with the other lines of defense= to support improvements in compliance maturity.
Support Third-Party Risk Management by reviewing the security clauses, schedules and assurance evidence for third- and fourth-party engagements, working in support of and facilitated through Procurement, Vendor Management and the TPRM function; the vendor relationship and any direct engagement with the vendor are led by those functions. 
Prepare reports and slide decks covering control assessment results, key control indicators and key risk indicators, for the Manager's review ahead of management reporting. 

Security Governance

Support the Technology Governance function on information security policies and standards, checking that they line up with the security control framework and flagging any discrepancies.
Provide supporting input to the Cyber Resiliency Framework where Security Compliance is asked to contribute, in line with the review cadence.
From a compliance-review perspective, flag opportunities to improve the clarity of security policies and standards and route them to the Technology Governance owner for action.

Security Architecture and Support 

Take part in security assessments and reviews for the Security Architecture and Engineering Work Groups, checking new solutions and designs against the applicable security controls.
Apply Secure by Design principles in the reviews completed, so that adequate security controls are considered during the design and architecture phases.

Security Information Improvement

Suggest improvements to internal processes, reporting and documentation that support compliance. 
Track security assessment findings and improvement actions through to closure, following up with internal stakeholders and escalating delays.
Provide support in the closure of security related audit findings, engaging with Internal Audit and the control owners to develop and document action plans, and tracking progress.
Other tasks as assigned by the manager. 

Technical Competencies

Working understanding of information security principles, practices, technologies and procedures.
Working understanding of information risk management methods and techniques for assessing risks, threats and vulnerabilities.
Ability to weigh security controls against the risks they address, including the use of compensating controls.
Knowledge of security control frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST CSF, and how they apply to the security governance and compliance practice.
Awareness of industry security standards, laws and regulations (for example, ISO/IEC 27001, SWIFT CSP, PIPEDA and Bank of Canada oversight expectations).
Security audit and findings management — tracking findings to closure with documented action plans and evidence, and supporting second- and third-line assessments and internal audits.

Energetic, self-motivated, quick to learn, and comfortable taking responsibility for assigned work.
High degree of initiative and flexibility.
Strong communication and organizational skills.
Strong relationship management skills.
Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills.
Ability to work with colleagues in Procurement, Legal, GRC/TPRM, Privacy, TPRM and project teams, explaining security requirements clearly and following up to a workable outcome.
Care and accuracy in preparing the material that supports responses to regulators (for example, the Bank of Canada), where inquiries and attestations carry firm external deadlines. 
Persistence in carrying contractual security requirements through successive review rounds, with support from the Manager where a position needs to be negotiated.
Ability to stay organized and composed when demand is deadline-driven and unpredictable, managing a queue of competing commitments.
Strong attention to detail when documenting exceptions, control gaps and the supporting evidence.
Ownership of assigned work and the ability to deliver it reliably in a small team, adapting as responsibilities and priorities shift.
Discretion and integrity in handling sensitive vendor, audit and regulatory information. 

| What you need to be successful

Post-secondary degree or diploma in computer science or other field related to information systems and technology or information security management or equivalent work experience.
A minimum of three (3) years of combined relevant work experience in an information security, IT audit or information risk management capacity. Regular activities will have included control assessment, evidence gathering and compliance reporting.
 Sound organizational and time management skills, with the ability to deliver assigned work to agreed timelines.
Ability to work with stakeholders across teams, take ownership of assigned work and follow it through to completion.
Working knowledge of security frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27002 and NIST, with general awareness of other industry security frameworks, regulations and standards.
Practical exposure to cybersecurity compliance, audit support and risk management.
Industry certifications, or demonstrated progress towards them, are considered an asset (CISA, CRISC, CISSP, CISM, etc.).

Clear written and verbal communication, with solid report writing skills.

| You will really stand out with
The following are considered an asset, and can be developed in the role:

Third-party assurance analysis: reviewing SOC 1 and SOC 2 (Type II) reports, exceptions and bridge letters, and validating Complementary User Entity Controls (CUECs) for critical service providers.
Working knowledge of the SWIFT Customer Security Programme (CSP) and Customer Security Controls Framework (CSCF) — architecture types, mandatory and advisory controls, independent assessment and annual attestation.
Familiarity with financial market infrastructure oversight, including the Bank of Canada's PFMI (Annex F) self-attestation reviews and cyber-resilience expectations for designated systems.
Control-framework mapping and controls-library maintenance across ISO/IEC 27001, 27002, 27017/27018 (cloud), 27701 (privacy) and 42001 (AI), NIST CSF, CIS, COBIT and SOC 2.
Working knowledge of privacy and data-protection obligations (PIPEDA), personal-information handling and cross-border data-flow considerations in vendor

jazzhr:paystone:job_20261016004913_07XKR.description:
About Paystone 
 At Paystone, we're building the future of customer-driven growth for small businesses. Our products help business owners build stronger customer relationships and grow their businesses. 
 We're a team that puts people first, solves impactful problems, and believes there's always a better way to do things. We move quickly, challenge the status quo, and aren't afraid to roll up our sleeves to get things done. 
 Our People Experience function plays a big part in making Paystone a great place to work, and we're looking for someone who wants to help make it even better. 
 About the Role 
 We're looking for a Senior People Partner to support our Revenue and Operations teams as we continue to grow. You'll work closely with leaders to build strong teams, plan for future talent needs, strengthen employee engagement, and help create an environment where people can do their best work. 
 This role combines business partnership with hands-on ownership of our people programs. You'll bring ideas to the table, help leaders navigate people challenges, and find practical ways to improve how we work, including using AI and automation to make our processes more efficient. 
 We're a small People Experience function, so we're looking for someone who can work independently while staying closely aligned with our broader people strategy and the way we support employees and leaders across Paystone. Reporting to the Director of People Experience, you'll have room to take ownership, make recommendations, and turn good ideas into meaningful improvements. 
 What You'll Do 

- Partner with leaders across Revenue and Operations to understand their goals, strengthen their teams, plan for talent needs, and navigate organizational and people challenges. 

- Coach managers on team effectiveness, employee development, engagement, performance, and employee relations, helping them make thoughtful, informed decisions. 

- Own the delivery of key people programs, including onboarding, performance management, engagement, recognition, career development, and compensation, working with the Director of People Experience to bring our priorities to life. 

- Look for opportunities to improve our programs and processes, using feedback, people data, and practical recommendations to make the employee and manager experience better. 

- Use AI, automation, and technology to streamline workflows, reduce manual work, and find smarter ways to deliver People Experience programs. 

- Support our globally distributed workforce, working with employees, managers, and Employer of Record (EOR) partners across different locations and employment arrangements. 
 What You'll Bring 

- 5+ years of progressive HR experience, including experience in a People Partner or HR Business Partner role. 

- Experience partnering with leaders on business and people priorities, with a strong understanding of how to build effective teams and support employee growth. 

- The ability to think beyond individual issues and connect your recommendations to broader people strategies, philosophies, and established practices. 

- A track record of taking ownership, improving processes, and turning ideas into action. 

- Experience using AI, automation, data, or technology to improve how work gets done, along with curiosity about what else is possible. 

- Strong judgment, attention to detail, and organizational skills. You work independently, manage competing priorities, and follow through on your commitments. 

- Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to coach managers, challenge thinking when needed, and build trust. 

- Working knowledge of Canadian employment legislation and HR best practices. 

- A degree, diploma, or equivalent experience in Human Resources or a related field. 
 Bonus points if you have: 

- Experience supporting Revenue, Sales, Customer Success, or Operations teams. 

- Experience supporting remote, globally distributed teams or working with EOR providers. 

- Experience with Leapsome, JazzHR, Asana, or similar HR and workflow platforms. 

- Experience working in a growing organization where you've had to be resourceful, adaptable, and comfortable figuring things out. 
 What Success Looks Like 
 You'll be a trusted partner to leaders, helping them build strong teams and make better people decisions. You'll take ownership of your work, bring forward ideas that improve how we operate, and ensure your approach aligns with the broader People Experience function. Our programs will become more effective, our workflows more efficient, and our employees and managers will have a consistent, positive experience across Paystone. 
 Why Paystone? 
 You'll have the opportunity to make a real impact in a growing business, work closely with leaders, and help shape how we support our people as we evolve. 
 If you enjoy building relationships, solving problems, taking ownership, and finding better ways to work, we'd love to meet you. 
 Additional Information 
 Compensation 
 The expected annual salary for this position is CAD $80,000.00 -$100,000.00 
 Position Availability 
 This position represents an existing vacancy at Paystone, and we are actively recruiting candidates to join our team. 
 Our Recruitment Process 
 At Paystone, our recruitment and selection decisions are made by our hiring team. We do not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess, or select applicants for this position. 
  Perks & Benefits 

- Compensation tied to market data 

- We reward for contribution 

- Flexible Time-off 

- We’re committed to career development 

- Work from home 
 Our Mission 
 By joining Paystone, you are joining a team that is future-focused and driven by our mission of creating Customer Driven Growth. 
 By helping our clients create better experiences for their customers, and in turn, motivating their happy customers to share their experiences with others, our platform creates the momentum for our clients to gain more happy customers. In other words, we win when our customers do. 
 Curious? 
 Good! We want all the curiosity we can muster. Innovation stems from observation and questioning, so be eager, be innovative, and be ready to raise the bar. 
 Come check us out!! 
 paystone.com

 get.nicejob.com 
 About Us 
 Paystone is a leading North American payment and software company redefining the way merchants engage their customers and grow their businesses. The company's seamlessly integrated suite of automated payment processing, customer loyalty, gift card solutions, and now reputation marketing, is used by brands such as Irving Oil, The Source, Global Pet Foods, Kernels Popcorn, and many of the MTY Food Group's restaurant brands. Paystone's solutions are used at over 30,000 locations across Canada and the United States which collectively process over 10 billion dollars a year in bankcard volume. We employ over 200 employees and serve as the technology partner of choice for hundreds of partners across North America.

About Plotly

Plotly builds the tools millions of developers use to work with data. Our open-source libraries are downloaded millions of times per day, Dash is one of the most popular ways to build data applications in Python, and we are building AI features up and down the stack.

About the role

This role is responsible for the company's website content, blog, social media presence, and marketing/sales collateral. It is a hands-on, execution-focused position that involves writing and publishing content, maintaining a strong SEO site architecture, and applying modern web design trends, without needing to create visual designs from scratch. This individual will work closely with Marketing Operations, Front-End Web Development, and Product to ensure all content is well-crafted, strategically structured, and high-performing.

Key Responsibilities (Primary Ownership)

Web Content & Structure

 - Own end-to-end website copy, including homepages, product pages, solution pages, landing pages, blog posts, and supporting site content in collaboration with Marketing Operations and with input from Product.

 - Manage site-wide heading architecture, applying best practices consistently across new and existing pages to optimize SEO performance.

 - Maintain alignment between website content and evolving Product and GTM priorities.

Content Production

 - Manage the blog program: editorial calendar, briefing, writing/editing, and publishing, coordinating with Product for subject-matter input.

 - Own daily social media content and posting cadence (planning, writing, and creation), using established templates and visual systems, and track what's performing.

 - Create design assets with templates (graphics, slide decks, video, and other creative collateral) to support marketing and sales needs, using templates and existing brand systems where possible to keep production efficient.

lever:pointclickcare:c9e4c36c-27f6-48ae-.description:
Job Title: Director, People Strategy and HR Portfolio (Project) Management 
Location: Mississauga, ON - Hybrid
 
**Travel to Office expectations**
For Hybrid Roles: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.
 
At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare.
 
With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work. 
 
At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.
 
Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
 
About the Team
The People Strategy & Transformation (PST) is PointClickCare's HR strategy, organizational design, and portfolio management pillar. The team includes HR Business Partners, Organizational Design & Effectiveness, People Experience, and the HR Strategy & Enablement function, with a dotted-line partnership to Internal Communications. PST is responsible for ensuring HR's work across every Center of Excellence is planned, resourced, sequenced, and tracked against business outcomes — spanning a portfolio of Pillar Initiatives, Cross-Pillar Projects, and Program Roll-Ups delivered across all four HR solution groups.
 
Position Summary:
The Director, People Strategy and HR Portfolio (Project) Management s is the VP, People Strategy & Transformation's strategic thought partner in building and running PointClickCare's HR Portfolio Management Office (HR PMO) — co-designing the strategy, governance model, capacity methodology, and dashboard reporting that let HR plan, resource, and track its work against business outcomes. This is a net-new function: no HR PMO currently exists at PointClickCare, and this role will design these mechanics in partnership with the VP rather than operate a system someone else has already built.

Operating with significant design authority but without direct reports or final decision rights on cross-functional trade-offs, this role earns influence through the credibility of the mechanics it builds and runs. It operates across all four HR solution groups without formal authority over any of them, serves as the VP's thought partner on HR strategy and the HR SLT prioritization process, and convenes HR initiative stakeholders and Internal Communications to coordinate how HR's work reaches the business.
 
Key Responsibilities:
Design and run the HR Portfolio Management Office’s core operating mechanics
Design and maintain the capacity management methodology, including the heat map model and the oversubscription thresholds used to flag resourcing conflicts across HR COEs
Own and run the Portfolio Council governance cadence end to end — intake, capacity check, tier assignment, publish, mid-quarter check, and close-out
Build and maintain the integrated HR initiative dashboard, ensuring data currency and accuracy across every active Pillar Initiative, Cross-Pillar Project, and Program Roll-Up
Example deliverable: a quarterly Portfolio Council capacity heat map showing every HR COE’s current initiative load, used to approve or defer new initiative intake
Serve as strategic thought partner to the VP, People Strategy & Transformation
Co-design the HR SLT prioritization process and criteria used to evaluate and sequence HR initiatives each planning cycle
Co-design the OKR and scorecard measurement architecture — what gets measured, how it rolls up, and the cadence it runs on
Co-author and stress-test the HR Strategy on a Page, contributing independent analysis before it is finalized by the VP
Example deliverable: a documented HR SLT prioritization framework — criteria, weighting, and process — adopted for the FY28 planning cycle
Own capacity management and project plan oversight across the full HR initiative portfolio
Track progress against committed business outcomes, not activity completion alone, across every active HR initiative
Maintain consistent project plan structure, milestone tracking, and dependency mapping in partnership with each initiative’s named Delivery Lead
Proactively surface cross-COE capacity collisions and resourcing conflicts before they reach Portfolio Council
Example deliverable: a consolidated project plan view across all active Program Roll-Ups, flagging dependency risk before it affects a committed milestone
Convene HR initiative stakeholders and Internal Communications on a recurring cadence
Establish and run a recurring go-to-market coordination cadence bringing together initiative Delivery Leads and Internal Communications
Sequence the timing and stakeholder readiness of HR initiative rollouts to the business, avoiding duplicate or conflicting messages landing in the same window
Maintain a shared go-to-market calendar visible to HR SLT, showing what is launching, when, and to whom
Example deliverable: a quarterly HR go-to-market calendar sequencing every planned initiative rollout to the business, reviewed and approved by HR SLT before the quarter begins
Represent HR in enterprise planning and governance forums
Serve as the primary operational liaison to the Strategic Delivery Office, aligning HR’s initiative classification and intake practices to enterprise taxonomy
Represent HR’s initiative portfolio and capacity picture in the Corporate Strategy Group’s quarterly planning cadence
Flag enterprise-level dependencies or conflicts affecting HR’s ability to deliver against committed priorities
Example deliverable: HR’s consolidated initiative and capacity submission into the Corporate Strategy Group’s quarterly planning sprint, reflecting current Portfolio Council status
 
Required Skills & Qualifications:
10–15 years of experience in program/portfolio management, management consulting, or a PMO leadership capacity, including demonstrated experience designing — not only operating — portfolio governance, capacity management, or OKR measurement systems
A track record serving as a strategic thought partner to a senior leader, with evidence of shaping that leader's thinking rather than only executing direction
Demonstrated experience operating in matrixed, cross-functional environments without formal authority over the teams being coordinated
Strong data and dashboard fluency — comfortable architecting reporting tools and the metrics model behind them, not just maintaining an existing build
Executive-level communication skills — this role prepares materials for and interacts directly with VP-level stakeholders across every HR pillar
Experience convening cross-functional stakeholder groups to coordinate sequencing and alignment on complex, multi-team initiatives
 
Preferred Experience:
Experience building a PMO or governance function from scratch, in a design capacity, rather than operating within an already-mature one
HR domain experience, including familiarity with COE structures and business-outcome-linked workforce initiatives
Experience partnering with internal communications or marketing functions on coordinated, multi-stakeholder rollouts

Our salary ranges are determined by job and level. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the target for new hire salaries for the position across all Canada locations. Within the range, individual compensation is determined by job-related skills and knowledge, relevant experience including professional and lived experience, and/or work location. Position Summary: The Market Insights Manager is an individual contributor responsible for executing the market research and competitive intelligence that informs PointClickCare’s product, marketing, and go-to-market decisions. This role maintains continuous competitive monitoring, builds competitor profiles and market trend analyses, and produces the reports, dashboards, and presentation materials that carry findings to cross-functional partners and contribute to leadership readouts. This role also independently designs and runs standard qualitative studies — in-depth interviews — and supports the design and analysis of quantitative studies such as surveys, MaxDiff, and pricing research. Success in this role requires analytical rigor, methodological curiosity, clear written and verbal communication, and the organization to manage several concurrent projects.  Key Responsibilities::
  • Foster a Customer-Centric Culture: Advocate for a customer-focused approach throughout the organization by promoting the voice of the customer and enhancing primary research capabilities.
  • Execute Research Projects: Assist in designing, implementing, and managing market research studies utilizing qualitative and quantitative methods, such as surveys and focus groups, to gather insights on customer needs, market trends, and competitive activity.
  • Methodology Development: Contribute to the development and refinement of research methodologies and best practices to enhance the quality and effectiveness of research efforts.
  • Data Collection and Analysis: Gather, organize, and analyze data from various sources, including qualitative interviews, discussions, surveys, and industry publications, using both basic and advanced tools like Excel, SPSS, or AI-based solutions.
  • Reporting and Insights: Create reports, dashboards, and presentations that clearly communicate findings and actionable insights to internal teams and stakeholders, aiding in marketing and product strategy decisions.
  • Presentation Skills: Deliver findings and recommendations to senior leadership and stakeholders through engaging presentations.
  • Quality Assurance: Maintain data accuracy and integrity by overseeing research administration, paying close attention to detail, and properly managing confidential or regulated information.
  • Support Senior Staff: Provide logistical and analytical assistance to senior research or insights managers by conducting background research, drafting survey and discussion guides, and more.
  • Project Management: Oversee project timelines, document research processes, assist with scheduling, and maintain organized research files.
  • Innovation and Trends: Stay updated on emerging research technologies and methodologies to innovate research practices and enhance the quality of insights.
    • Required Skills & Qualifications::
  • 5 years hands-on experience within the market research industry, collecting and analyzing data, reporting and presenting findings within the healthcare industry
  • Advanced analytical skills, including experience with statistical modeling and ability to integrate disparate data sources
  • Advanced storytelling and presentation skills; ability to translate complex concepts and methodologies into easily understood language
  • Expertise with Excel, PowerPoint, PowerBI, and AI solutions
  • Highly motivated, results-driven person, who works effectively in a collaborative, fast-paced environment
  • Bachelors or advanced degree in business, mathematics, or the sciences
  • Should have understanding of conjoint, Max Diff, price elasticity, concept testing, and other such research types. 
  • Should have experience managing complex market research studies such as brand health and brand equity trackers
    • Preferred Experience::
  • Has a deep understanding of the healthcare industry/sector including experience with LTPAC, Acute and/or Payer audiences.
  • Previous experience working successfully in a SaaS organization
  • Experience with a wide array of new product, brand, advertising and customer segmentation research methodologies

Position Summary: The Strategic Finance Analytics Manager is a newly created role that builds and leads the financial modelling and analytics capability at the core of PointClickCare’s strategic finance function. The role delivers the models, tools, and decision support that enable leadership to drive profitability, optimize commercial strategy, and allocate resources with precision — with work that is highly visible to executive leadership, the Board, and investors. Positioned at the intersection of Finance, Strategy, and Go-to-Market, the near-term focus is Pricing & Monetization Analytics, while the broader mandate is to build scalable analytical frameworks applicable across any strategic finance domain the business identifies. A defining attribute of the role is the hands-on application of AI/ML to modernize and accelerate modelling, scenario generation, and reporting. Key Responsibilities: :
  • Financial Modelling & Scenario Analysis. Build and maintain in-house financial and profitability models that evaluate the revenue and margin implications of strategic decisions, beginning with pricing and commercial strategy and expanding to other strategic finance domains. Run scenario and sensitivity analyses on packaging, pricing changes, GTM strategies, and investment trade-offs, measured against NRR, ARR, and contribution margin.
  • AI-Led Modernization of the Analytics Toolkit. Apply AI/ML tools, including LLMs and predictive modelling, to accelerate modelling, scenario generation, and reporting, raising the speed and sophistication of decision support across the function. Build scalable, self-serve analytics tools that give Finance, Pricing, Sales Ops, and business unit leaders consistent, decision-ready intelligence.
  • Pricing & Monetization Analytics. Evaluate pricing changes through quantitative modelling of customer, revenue, and margin impact across segments and geographies. Track pricing and monetization KPIs (discount compliance, revenue realization, contribution margin) against targets, and quantify the financial impact of commercial governance decisions including pricing policies, discount frameworks, and packaging structures.
  • Executive & Profitability Reporting. Deliver regular profitability and commercial performance reporting to ELT and GTM leadership, including a measurement framework that tracks strategic initiative effectiveness, monetization outcomes, and contribution margin across products, segments, and geographies. Partner with FP&A and Sales Ops to integrate pricing and profitability analytics into the forecast and planning cycle, and with Revenue Assurance and Finance Ops to remediate pricing-related revenue risks.
  • Stakeholder Engagement & Decision Support. Act as the primary analytical partner to Pricing, Sales Enablement, and business unit leaders on profitability decisions, translating complex analysis into clear, actionable recommendations. Present findings, models, and recommendations to senior leadership in executive-ready format, and contribute to Board and investor materials covering pricing strategy, monetization performance, and platform progress.
    • Required Skills & Qualifications::
  • University degree in Finance, Business, Economics, or a related quantitative field
  • 5–7 years in financial analysis, FP&A, or quantitative/strategic finance in a SaaS or technology environment.
  • Exceptional financial modelling and scenario-analysis skills, with a demonstrated track record building revenue, profitability, or pricing models and translating them into decision support (the core qualification for the role).
  • Hands-on experience applying AI/ML tools (including LLMs and predictive modelling) to accelerate and modernize modelling and reporting workflows — a defining attribute of the role, not a nice-to-have.
    • Preferred Skills & Qualifications::
  • Pricing or monetization experience (an asset, not a requirement)
  • Experience with BI tools (Power BI preferred) and executive-grade data visualization.
  • Exposure to Salesforce (SFDC), including Revenue Cloud Advanced (RCA).

jibe:flyporter:5429.description: Job Summary The Senior Analyst, Financial Reporting will be a key member of the finance team, reporting to the Manager, Financial Reporting. This role supports the preparation of accurate and timely financial statements, management discussion and analysis, and ensuring compliance with IFRS and other relevant regulations. The Senior Analyst will assist in preparing internal and external financial reports, contribute to regulatory filings, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure financial data accurately reflects the Company’s operations. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical skills, keen attention to detail, deep technical IFRS knowledge, including the ability to apply it to complex and non-routine transactions, and a proactive mindset to support continuous improvements in financial reporting processes. Duties & Responsibilities Assist in the preparation of accurate and timely quarterly financial reporting documents, including consolidated financial statements, management’s discussion and analysis, and materials for the disclosure and audit committees. Support the Finance team in producing accurate monthly, quarterly, annual, and ad-hoc financial reports for both internal and external stakeholders. Provide accounting insights and ensure financial data is aligned with IFRS and internal policies. Perform technical accounting research and analyze complex agreements and transactions (i.e., revenue arrangements, leases, financial instruments, and business combinations) to determine and document appropriate accounting treatments under IFRS. Prepare technical and complex accounting journal entries as required. Draft technical accounting memoranda documenting the Company’s accounting conclusions on significant or judgmental transactions. Stay informed on new and evolving accounting standards, supporting the team in ensuring compliance and implementing changes. Collaborate with external auditors and assist in managing the annual audit process to ensure timely and efficient completion. Contribute to improving the accuracy, quality, and timeliness of financial information prepared for leadership and the Audit Committee. Support the development and implementation of new financial policies, processes, and systems to enhance operational efficiency. Assist in maintaining and strengthening internal controls over financial reporting, including documentation and updates to key processes and controls. Participate in finance transformation initiatives, ensuring accounting processes are accurately implemented. Provide mentorship and guidance to junior team members, promoting growth and continuous learning. Collaborate with the broader finance team and other corporate and operational departments to ensure accurate, complete, and compliant financial reporting. Actively engage in the Company’s Safety Management System (SMS), reporting hazards and incidents encountered in daily operations while promoting and adhering to the Company Safety Policy. Behavioural Competencies Concern for Safety: Identifying hazardous or potentially hazardous situations and taking appropriate action to maintain a safe environment for self and others. Teamwork: Working collaboratively with others to achieve organizational goals. Passenger/Customer Service: Providing service excellence to internal and/or external customers (passengers). Initiative: Dealing with situations and issues proactively and persistently, seizing opportunities that arise. Results Focus: Focusing efforts on achieving high quality results consistent with the organization’s standards. Fostering Communication: Listening and communicating openly, honestly, and respectfully with different audiences, promoting dialogue and building consensus. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in finance, business, or a related discipline, complemented by a CPA accreditation. 4-5 years of direct financial reporting experience. Prior experience with a major public accounting firm. Deep technical accounting expertise in IFRS, with demonstrated ability to apply IFRS to complex and judgmental transactions, and strong working knowledge of consolidations. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, with strong fundamental and analytical skills. Highly organized, with a strong focus on accuracy, timeliness, and attention to detail. Excellent analytical skills, with a strong aptitude for reviewing financial information for accuracy and completeness. Proactive and solution-oriented mindset, with the ability to identify and implement process improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness. Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial data effectively to stakeholders at all organizational levels. Team-oriented professional, capable of influencing and collaborating across multiple functions. Experience in the airline or transportation industry is considered an asset. Procurify is the AI-enhanced procurement and AP automation platform for the mid-market. We make it easy for organizations to take control of spend and save money. We’re looking for a talented and team-driven Business Development Representative to join us on our journey.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

 

As a Business Development Representative, you will be responsible for all top of funnel activities that create qualified opportunities for our sales team. This is a high-impact role where you’ll join a team of high performers dedicated to building relationships, achieving quotas, and delivering exceptional results.

 - Engage in networking, face-to-face meetings, and other activities to generate and close leads.

 - Conduct initial discovery calls to educate prospects about our offerings.

 - Stay up-to-date on trends and news from the industry, competitors, and target market.

 - Collaborate with the sales team to develop and execute strategies to meet revenue targets.

 - Build and nurture relationships with prospects, guiding them through the sales funnel.

 - Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of prospect interactions and sales activities in the CRM system.

 

Tech Stack:

 - Salesforce

 - Nooks

 - Zoominfo

 - Gong/ Gong Engage

 - LinkedIn Sales Navigator
   




WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - At least 1 year of any sales or quota-carrying experience.

 - Highly driven and goal-oriented, willing to work as hard as necessary to achieve success.

 - Committed to continuous learning and self-improvement.

 - Has strong communication, negotiation, and persuasion skills.

 - Self-motivated with a target-driven mindset.

 - Thrives in a fast-paced environment and works well both independently and as part of a team.

 - Technically inclined and eager to learn new tools or software.

 - Conversion ratios

We’re committed to helping mission-driven organizations spend smarter

Procurify is a remote-first company with a big heart and a strong ambition to modernize the way organizations manage business spend. We’re looking for talented and team-driven individuals to join us on our journey to build a place where the best people want to work – a place where every team member is empowered to apply their best thinking, push boundaries thoughtfully, and drive high performance together.

 

You’re empowered to do your best work

Location:
Canada (100% Remote)


Procurify is the agentic procurement platform that helps mid-market organizations get complete control over their spend.


We’re trusted by hundreds of companies around the world, across industries like biotechnology, education, health care, manufacturing, and software, to manage over $100B in spend.


About the Role



Procurify is seeking a Director of Performance Marketing to lead our paid acquisition and digital experience strategy, driving qualified pipeline growth as AI reshapes how B2B buyers discover, evaluate and purchase software.



This is a hands-on leadership role combining deep paid media expertise, commercial acumen and a strategic approach to digital experience. You'll optimize established acquisition channels, identify emerging growth opportunities and evolve our digital presence to better engage and convert today's buyers.



We're looking for a strategic thinker and strong executor who brings analytical rigor, curiosity and sound commercial judgment. Someone who can translate complex performance data into clear decisions, challenge conventional approaches and deliver measurable business outcomes.



Reporting to the CMO, you'll directly manage our Senior Wordpress Developer and collaborate closely with Demand Generation, Content & Brand, Product Marketing, Revenue Operations and Sales.



Key Responsibilities



Paid Media Strategy & Performance

 - Own the strategy, execution, forecasting and performance of paid acquisition channels, including Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising, paid social, review platforms and emerging digital channels.

 - Lead paid media optimization across campaign strategy, audience targeting, bidding, creative experimentation and budget allocation to maximize qualified pipeline and return on investment.

 - Identify, test and scale new acquisition opportunities, evolving our channel mix to reach and convert buyers across an increasingly diverse digital landscape.

 - Leverage CRM data, offline conversion tracking and advanced bidding strategies to continuously improve acquisition quality and campaign effectiveness.

 - Own paid media budgets, performance forecasting and external agency relationships, ensuring disciplined investment and measurable commercial outcomes.

 

Digital Experience & Conversion Optimization

 - Lead Procurify's digital experience strategy, evolving how we engage and convert buyers as AI transforms research, discovery and purchasing behaviours.

 - Own website conversion strategy across key digital journeys, landing pages and conversion experiences, with a focus on generating qualified demand.

 - Manage and develop the WebOps Manager, establishing a prioritized roadmap for website performance, user experience and conversion optimization.

 - Lead a structured experimentation program to continuously improve website effectiveness, using data, buyer insights and testing to inform priorities.

 - Partner with Content & Brand and Product Marketing to align digital experiences with buyer intent, positioning, content strategy and emerging discovery channels.
   
   

Analytics, Measurement & Commercial Performance

 - Own performance analysis and reporting across paid acquisition and digital conversion, connecting investment and engagement to qualified pipeline and revenue outcomes.

 - Partner with Revenue Operations to ensure accurate attribution, conversion tracking and measurement across the digital buyer journey.

 - Apply advanced analytics, attribution and incrementality testing to evaluate channel effectiveness and inform investment decisions.

 - Translate performance insights into clear executive recommendations, forecasts and actionable optimization strategies.
   
   

Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

 - Provide strategic and operational leadership across paid acquisition and digital experience, balancing hands-on execution with longer-term growth opportunities.

 - Partner closely with Demand Generation on integrated campaigns, audience strategies and conversion experiences to maximize pipeline contribution.

 - Collaborate with Content & Brand on SEO, GEO and organic acquisition initiatives, contributing website, conversion and performance expertise to shared priorities.

 - Build strong partnerships with Product Marketing, Sales and Revenue Operations to improve buyer engagement, lead quality and revenue outcomes.

 - Champion the application of AI across performance marketing, using emerging capabilities to accelerate analysis, experimentation, operational efficiency and execution.

 - Communicate priorities, performance and strategic recommendations effectively to marketing and executive leadership.
   
   

How Success Will Be Measured

 - Growth and efficiency of qualified pipeline generated through paid acquisition.

 - Improvement in website conversion performance and the generation of qualified demand.

 - Demonstrated contribution from new acquisition opportunities and effective investment allocation.

 - Strong performance measurement, actionable insights and strategic decision-making.

 - Effective leadership, execution and cross-functional collaboration.

 
 

What You'll Bring



 - 7-10 years of experience in B2B SaaS performance marketing, with demonstrated ownership of significant paid media budgets and measurable pipeline outcomes.

 - Deep, hands-on expertise in Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising and other paid media channels including campaign strategy, bidding, optimization and performance analysis.

 - Proven success driving paid acquisition and qualified pipeline in B2B SaaS environments with complex buying journeys and multi-stakeholder purchase decisions.

 - Strong understanding of advanced paid media measurement and optimization, including offline conversions, CRM-based performance data and automated bidding strategies.
   

 - Demonstrated experience leading website conversion strategy, CRO programs and digital experience improvements that drive measurable business results.

 - Advanced analytical and experimentation skills, including attribution, performance forecasting, incremental measurement and investment optimization.

 - Hands-on experience with Salesforce, Google Analytics 4 and Google Ads, with familiarity in marketing automation and attribution platforms such as Marketo and Marketo Measure.

 - Strong commercial judgment and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate insights into clear priorities and effective execution.

 - Demonstrated ability to leverage AI tools to improve marketing performance, generate insights and accelerate workflows.

 - Experience managing team members, collaborating with agencies and influencing cross-functional stakeholders.

 - Strong executive communication skills and the ability to present clear, data-driven recommendations to senior leadership.

 - Strong knowledge of SEO, GEO and organic acquisition, with an understanding of how these disciplines intersect with digital experience and conversion optimization.

We’re building a product that matters.




Procurify is redefining how organizations manage spend - transforming a historically manual, reactive process into a strategic advantage. Today, hundreds of companies trust us to manage billions in spend, and we’re just getting started.

lever:quandri:a181f86b-baee-4c20-9358-2b.description:
Who we are
Our mission at Quandri is to transform insurance into a trusted and delightful experience using AI. We are building the AI operating system for North America’s best insurance agencies and brokerages. 

For the first time ever, we have the technology to fundamentally change how insurance operates, and the stakes are human. Better insurance means families protected from harm, businesses able to take risks, and communities more resilient when the worst happens. For insurance practitioners, the ability to deliver this level of service finally becomes possible.
What we do
Quandri brings deeply specific, vertically-focused AI to the industry’s most critical stakeholders:insurance agencies and brokerages. 
Agents are the lifeblood of the industry, the place where most property and casualty insurance is sold and serviced. Yet operating an agency is harder than ever. Peak product complexity, accelerating consolidation, a deepening talent crisis, and the AI revolution are all reshaping how agencies work.
Quandri sits at the cutting edge of this shift, rebuilding how agencies operate one workflow at a time. We pair a deep understanding of insurance processes, systems, and data with serious technical capability and proprietary models, so the transformation is tangible and operational rather than aspirational.
We’re making insurance better for policyholders, while helping insurance brokerages deliver a better client service, grow faster, and harness AI so that they control the future of insurance distribution.
Why join us?
You'll join a fast-moving team with real ownership, direct access to leadership, and a genuine hand in shaping the company's next chapter.
We are headquartered in beautiful Vancouver, BC, backed by leading US and Canadian investors, and the recognition has followed:
LinkedIn’s Top Canadian Startups in 2024 & 2025
Deloitte’s Fast 50
CB Insights’ Insurtech 50 and Fintech 100 
The Globe and Mail’s Top Growing Companies in Canada.
About the role
As Director of Field Marketing at Quandri reporting to the CMO, you’ll establish the strategy, operating rhythms, and measurement needed to generate demand for Quandri’s software in our first priority regions. As the program grows, you’ll hire and lead marketers dedicated to individual regions.
You’ll work closely with regional Sales teams to understand their markets, target accounts, and pipeline goals. You’ll turn those priorities into a focused mix of hosted events, sponsored conferences, executive dinners, meetups, local digital programs, and other tactics you think are relevant and meaningful. The industry is insurance, and the events are fun: think golf tournaments, baseball games, community get-togethers and more. This is a hands-on role: you’ll set the direction and personally deliver programs while building the team.
You will:
Build the field marketing plan for Quandri’s first defined regions, deciding where to invest and developing repeatable programs that can scale.
Manage field events from start to finish, including venues, vendors, staffing, on-site materials, and execution.
For each major event, agree with Sales on the accounts to reach, meetings to book, and opportunities to advance. Plan outreach before the event, secure clear next steps during it, and ensure timely, personalized follow-up is recorded in HubSpot.
Set goals for meetings, qualified opportunities, and sourced and influenced pipeline. Report results and use them to refine the plan.
Own the field marketing budget and assess programs against their cost and contribution to pipeline.
Hire, coach, and lead region-specific field marketers as the function expands.
Requirements
5+ years of field marketing or regionally focused marketing experience in a SaaS company.
Experience building field marketing programs from scratch and creating repeatable processes.
Experience supporting multiple regions or distributed Sales teams and adapting programs to local needs.
A record of delivering field programs that generate demand and measurable sales opportunities.
Experience owning event or field marketing budgets and making investment decisions based on results.
Experience hiring, coaching, or managing marketers as a team grows.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage several programs, events, and stakeholders at once.
A collaborative, hands-on approach: you’re willing to execute programs yourself as well as set the strategy.
Familiarity with HubSpot for tracking, measuring, and reporting on field and event activity.
Willingness to travel up to approximately 40% for events and customer engagements while the regional team is being built. Once marketers are staffed in their regions, travel is expected to decrease to approximately 20%.
Our guiding principles:
Customers at the core. We put the customer at the center of all we do. At a basic level, we believe business success comes down to talking to customers and building something they want. We don’t listen to customers and just take what they say blindly, but we think critically about it and build what they need. Customers are the core of everything we do, and our business exists to serve them. We prioritize their needs over all else within the company.
Move with urgency. There are times when we need to move slowly and deliberately, but we default to acting fast and with urgency. We slow down when necessary, but this should be a deliberate choice. Businesses become more lethargic as they grow, this principle is designed to fight this fact.
Be curious. We understand the world by being curious and asking why. We aren’t satisfied with surface level understanding, and seek a deeper understanding of why things are the way they are. Don’t take someone’s word for it or the answer “because that’s how we do it.” Understand why and dig deep.
Excellence in execution. We know that what separates good from great is a high level of execution. We commit ourselves to excellence in everything that we do, from delivering an amazing product to writing a great email.
Act like an owner.  We’re all owners of the business and act like it. We follow through on commitments, own our results and think long-term.
Fight for simplicity. The law of increasing functional information states that systems evolve to become more complex over time. At Quandri, we believe there is sophistication in simplicity; as such, we intentionally fight for streamlined solutions and are committed to the uncomplicated.
AI-first. We believe AI is a fundamental shift in how work gets done, not just a tool we occasionally reach for. At Quandri, we lead with AI, in how we build our product, how we run our operations, and how we think about every process and workflow. This isn't about replacing people; it's about unlocking them to do higher-value work.
Compensation and Benefits:
The range for base pay is $150,000 - $190,000, most hires land around the midpoint of the range, while candidates with standout experience may land closer to the top.
Employee stock options, granted based off experience level upon hire and subject to a standard vesting schedule
Employee stock options based on experience level
Comprehensive health benefits, including $500 Lifestyle Spending Account
Four weeks of paid vacation per year
Work anywhere in the world for 60 calendar days of the year
Parental leave top-ups: 6 months for birthing parents, 8 weeks for non-birthing parents (up to $100,000 annual salary)
Quandri is dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. As an equal opportunity employer, Quandri adheres to Canadian labour laws and does not engage in discrimination based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or any other status protected under Canadian law.
Don’t let imposter syndrome stop you from applying. Great people sometimes don’t have the “right” experience. If you think that you’ll be amazing at this role then we encourage you to apply.
