English version to follow.

Pourquoi joindre QFG ? 
En tant qu'employé chez QFG, vous bénéficierez de nombreux avantages:

Programmes et ressources dédiés à la santé et au mieux-être.

Vacances rémunérées, journées personnelles et congés maladie pour favoriser un équilibre sain entre travail et vie personnelle.

Rémunération globale et gamme d’avantages sociaux concurrentiels.

Possibilités de croissance et de perfectionnement professionnel.

Occasions de contribuer à des causes communautaires.

Environnement collaboratif et inclusif où vous côtoierez des collègues issus de la diversité.

Ce poste est à combler pour une vacance actuelle.

Nous sommes à la recherche de notre prochain Spécialiste, assurance qualité du crédit (bilingue). Est-ce vous ?
Relevant du superviseur, Gestion des courtiers, le ou la spécialiste bilingue de l'intégration des courtiers joue un rôle essentiel dans la croissance de l'entreprise en supervisant l'ensemble du processus d'intégration, d'inscription et de vérification de la conformité pour tous les agents et cabinets de courtage.
Travaillant avec aisance en anglais et en français, ce ou cette professionnel(le) axé(e) sur les résultats agit à titre de liaison principale auprès des partenaires à travers l'ensemble des marchés canadiens. Ce poste équilibre le développement proactif de relations et le soutien aux partenaires avec le respect rigoureux de la conformité réglementaire — incluant les contrôles de lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent (LBA) et la vérification des permis d'exercice.
Le candidat idéal ou la candidate idéale allie un dynamisme énergique pour atteindre les objectifs de performance du service, une capacité exceptionnelle à résoudre les problèmes ainsi qu'un solide esprit d'équipe.

Vous voulez en savoir plus ? Continuez votre lecture...
Dans ce rôle, vos responsabilités incluront, sans s'y limiter:
1. Intégration des courtiers et gestion des relations

Exécuter la procédure d'intégration des courtiers de CTC afin d'assurer une inscription fluide, rapide et de haute qualité pour tous les nouveaux agents et cabinets de courtage, tant en anglais qu'en français.

Gérer de façon proactive le volume d'appels et les communications afin de soutenir la croissance du service et d'atteindre les objectifs du plan d'affaires.

Identifier les relations à fort potentiel avec les courtiers et les partenaires en offrant un soutien à l'intégration sur mesure pour renforcer l'engagement et la rétention.

Travailler en partenariat avec l'équipe des opérations des prêts résidentiels pour desservir et soutenir les partenaires dans les territoires régionaux assignés.

Collaborer avec l'équipe du marketing et de la gestion de la marque pour réviser, mettre à jour et créer des communications bilingues destinées aux courtiers, y compris des courriels promotionnels, du matériel éducatif et des documents de présentation.

Animer des présentations professionnelles et représenter l'organisation lors de visites dans les bureaux de courtiers, d'événements et de salons professionnels de l'industrie, au besoin.

2. Conformité, permis d'exercice et gestion des risques

Appliquer des normes de conformité strictes pour toutes les nouvelles inscriptions d'agents et de cabinets de courtage.

Surveiller, mettre à jour et vérifier de façon continue les détails des permis d'exercice des agents et des cabinets de courtage afin d'assurer la tenue de dossiers précis, conformément aux exigences annuelles et bisannuelles.

Respecter rigoureusement les procédures de lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent (LBA), en mettant un accent particulier sur les règles de « connaissance du client » (KYC).

Détecter, examiner et signaler de façon proactive les situations de risque réelles ou potentielles liées à la LBA/FAT (lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent et le financement des activités terroristes), à la non-conformité réglementaire ou aux violations des politiques internes ; mettre en œuvre des mesures correctives en temps opportun.

Respecter l'ensemble des contrôles internes liés aux risques opérationnels, des directives sur la confidentialité et des politiques de l'entreprise.

3. Analyse du marché et amélioration continue

Analyser les indicateurs issus des rapports et les données de performance des partenaires pour déceler des occasions de croissance.

Maintenir à jour ses connaissances sur les tendances du secteur, les conditions du marché et les activités de la concurrence dans le domaine des prêts résidentiels.

Identifier les goulots d'étranglement opérationnels et mettre en œuvre des initiatives d'amélioration continuous afin de simplifier et d'optimiser les flux de travail d'intégration.

Conserver des dossiers électroniques et physiques complets, précis et organisés, conformément aux politiques de conservation des documents de l'entreprise.

Alors, serez-vous notre prochain Spécialiste, assurance qualité du crédit (bilingue)? Vous l'êtes si vous possédez ces qualifications...
Exigences linguistiques

Bilinguisme (anglais et français) : Une maîtrise de l'anglais et du français de niveau langue maternelle ou professionnel, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit, est requise pour soutenir efficacement les partenaires à travers le Canada.

Formation et expérience

Études postsecondaires (diplôme ou baccalauréat) en administration des affaires, finance, communications ou dans un domaine connexe (de préférence).

Plus de 2 ans d'expérience en intégration de courtiers, en soutien aux partenaires, en opérations de prêt ou en conformité des services financiers (de préférence).

La connaissance des types de prêts résidentiels, de leurs caractéristiques, des facteurs de risque et des écosystèmes de courtiers hypothécaires constitue un atout majeur.

Compétences techniques et fonctionnelles

Maîtrise des applications de Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive) et des outils de recherche en ligne avancés.

Solides compétences en tenue de dossiers, en gestion de données et en production de rapports opérationnels.

Compréhension démontrée de la conformité en matière de LBA/FAT (lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent et le financement des activités terroristes) et des protocoles KYC (« connaissance du client »).

Qualités interpersonnelles et comportementales

Communication et influence : Excellentes aptitudes en communication d'affaires orale et écrite, avec une capacité à effectuer des présentations avec assurance auprès de partenaires externes.

Résolution de problèmes et jugement : Fortes capacités d'analyse et de prise de décision ; grande habileté à répondre aux demandes complexes des partenaires tout en respectant les normes de conformité.

Motivation et résilience : Personne axée sur les résultats, très disciplinée et faisant preuve d'une persévérance courtoise, animée par la volonté d'atteindre les objectifs dans des délais serrés.

Adaptabilité et intégrité : Fait preuve du plus haut niveau d'intégrité, d'une attitude positive et proactive (« can-do ») ainsi que d'une capacité à travailler aussi bien de manière autonome qu'en équipe.

Conditions de travail et exigences physiques

Déplacements : Déplacements intermittents requis pour des visites dans les bureaux de courtiers, des événements de partenaires, des présentations et des salons professionnels.

Gestion du stress : Stress modéré lié à un rythme de travail rapide, à la gestion de délais serrés, au traitement simultané de priorités concurrentes et à la prise en charge d'un volume élevé de demandes provenant des courtiers.

Exigences physiques : Périodes prolongées en position assise et debout ; dextérité manuelle requise pour l'utilisation du clavier et du matériel informatique ; soulèvement occasionnel de charges modérées pour le matériel événementiel et publicitaire.

Informations sur la rémunération:

Échelle de salaire de base: $50,000 - $60,000

La rémunération finale sera établie en fonction de l'expérience, des compétences et du lieu de travail (Canada) du candidat retenu. Elle comprend un régime d'avantages sociaux complet et un programme de primes concurrentiel pour les postes permanents à temps plein.

We're looking for our next Key Account Manager. Could It Be You?

Flexiti sits at the intersection of fintech, retail, and consumer lending — a $1.6B+ platform serving hundreds of thousands of Canadian consumers through major merchant partnerships. We've spent the last year investing in the foundations: Braze for lifecycle orchestration, Databricks for analytics and segmentation, and a consumer mobile app that's now live. Now we're accelerating, expanding into new verticals, scaling high-velocity partnerships, and building the team and operating model to match our ambitions.

As a Key Account Manager, you will drive the growth and overall success of some of Flexiti's high-value national key merchants. As a core member of our Account Management team, you will take a holistic, big-picture approach: you will oversee the high-level operational success of your accounts, but your primary focus will be commercial.

You are sales-focused, and you understand that the best partnerships are mutually beneficial. You will work to find the sweet spot between optimizing cost-efficiency for the merchant and maximizing profitability for Flexiti. You are comfortable presenting data to C-suite executives, with the analytical ability to look past raw numbers and read between the lines to find actionable trends. You are highly proficient in Excel and comfortable leveraging modern AI tools to gather data, but your real strength lies in interpreting what that data means for the client's business.

Need more details? Keep reading…

In this role, responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Enterprise relationship management: Serving as the primary strategic and commercial contact for national corporate brands, managing account health to flag risk early, and building strong, trusted relationships with executive stakeholders.

Internal merchant advocacy: Representing the merchant's needs back into product to shape the offering, and representing Flexiti to ensure the merchant's priorities align with ours.

Commercial growth and profitability: Identifying and executing growth opportunities within your portfolio to increase financing volume and drive revenue, balancing merchant cost-efficiency with Flexiti's revenue goals.

ashby:ramp:3f94674f-6af8-4e10-9631-77b1b.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

As an Account Executive focused on high-velocity sales in Canada, you will drive Ramp’s growth by closing a large volume of small, repeatable deals with speed and consistency. This role is designed for sellers who thrive in fast sales cycles, high activity, and a process-drive environment. You’ll primarily sell to small businesses and early-stage companies, running a transactional sales motion that emphasizes quick qualification, clear ROI, and rapid decision-making. You’ll work closely with SDRs, efficiently move deals forward, and help Ramp scale its presence across Canada.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Close a high volume of deals by managing opportunities from first contact to signature in short, efficient sales cycles.

 - Quickly qualify prospects based on firmographics, use case, and urgency, advancing strong-fit deals and disqualifying others early.

 - Run concise, repeatable demos and sales conversations focused on immediate value, ease of adoption, and clear next steps.

 - Manage a large pipeline of simultaneous opportunities, maintaining responsiveness and momentum across all accounts.

 - Hit weekly and monthly activity, pipeline, and revenue targets in a metrics-driven sales environment.

 - Maintain clean CRM hygiene, accurate forecasting, and disciplined follow-up in Salesforce.

 - Provide ongoing feedback on SMB objections, competitive trends, and process improvements to help optimize Ramp’s velocity sales motion.




WHAT YOU NEED

 - 1-2 years of quota-carrying SaaS sales experience in an SMB, transactional, or high-velocity closing role.

 - Proven ability to consistently close a high number of small deals per month (20–30+ deals/month)

 - Experience selling to founders, owners, and operators at small businesses with straightforward, value-focused messaging.

 - Ability to stay highly organized while managing dozens of active deals at once.

 - Comfort working off clear metrics and operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills.

 - This is an in-office role in Toronto, 5 days per week. This is not a remote role.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience selling into very small businesses or early-stage startups.

 - Fintech, payments, or financial operations sales experience.

 - Familiarity with Canadian SMBs and local business requirements.









BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

jazzhr:ratehubinc:job_20261015194222_DHA.description:
WHO IS RATEHUB? 
 We’re a company on a mission. We are a unique Canadian Fintech that is the one-stop shop for all financial needs of the consumer: Save, Spend, Borrow, Invest, and Protect. Every single team member — from Product & Engineering to Sales & Marketing, Finance, Operations, and everything in between — is obsessed with one thing: helping Canadians make better financial choices. And we’re pretty great at it, too. Via our digital application technology and our award-winning in-house brokerages, we help over 2M Canadians per month make a positive impact on their finances. We have many unique businesses: a mortgage brokerage, a life insurance brokerage, a home and auto insurance brokerage, a mortgage originations and servicing business, a Financial Services Marketplace, and a content business across Ratehub and MoneySense. 365 days a year, we deliver our users the best online mortgage experience, personalized credit card and loan options, and cheaper auto and home insurance policies than they typically get from their existing financial adviser. 
  Changing how people make financial choices isn’t easy, though. We know that achieving our mission is full of challenges — challenges that can be complex and often unexpected but that are always interesting, rewarding, and fun to solve as a team. This is where you come in. We are on the hunt for the right candidate to join us and help lead us forward to continued growth. 
  About the role 
 We’re looking for a Content Strategist to help grow and reach more Canadians through high-quality, data-driven sponsored content.  
  This is a mid-level individual contributor role reporting to the Senior Organic Growth Manager. You’ll work closely with the Senior Director of Everyday Banking and Partnerships, the Partnerships Team, our partners, the Content Team, and other cross-functional stakeholders. The role sits at the intersection of content strategy, SEO, GEO, analytics, content creation, and distribution. You’ll use performance data, search trends, audience insights, and emerging AI search data to identify opportunities, make recommendations, and execute content initiatives that drive organic growth. 
  As the Content Strategist dedicated to sponsored content, you’ll work with the Partnerships Team and our partners to come up with content ideas and handle writing, distributing, and optimizing content across personal finance topics, including credit cards, banking, credit monitoring, and investing. You don’t need to be an expert in every product area when you join, but you’ll be expected to develop a strong working knowledge of our partners’ products and the Canadian personal finance space over time, so you can create content that’s accurate, relevant, and useful to consumers while meeting partner goals. You’ll also support firmwide SEO and GEO initiatives. 
  Your goal is simple: use content, search, data, and distribution to bring more qualified traffic to Ratehub.ca and deliver strong results for our partners. You’ll work across blogs, landing pages, sponsored emails, social content, short-form video, forums, and emerging search channels, with a focus on measurable organic growth. 
 What you’ll do 
 Develop a data-driven content and SEO/GEO strategy 

- Develop a strong understanding of Search Engine Optimization (SEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and use SEO and AI Search Analytics platforms to monitor how Ratehub's sponsored content is appearing in traditional rankings and AI-generated answers. 

- Use analytics, search data, audience insights, and content performance across both traditional and AI-powered search to identify opportunities. 

- Analyze organic traffic, rankings, on-page engagement, conversions, and AI-search visibility (mentions and citations across LLMs and generative search platforms) to understand what's working and where there are opportunities to improve. 

- Identify content gaps, high-value topics, and emerging search trends, including which topics, sources, and formats are being surfaced by AI search engines. 

- Work with the Senior Organic Growth Manager and other stakeholders to turn analysis and recommendations into actionable content initiatives and help inform the broader SEO and GEO strategy. 

- Support firmwide SEO and GEO initiatives alongside the Senior Organic Growth Manager. 

- Stay up to date on changes in search, AI discovery, GEO best practices, and emerging search behaviours. 
 Create and optimize content 

- Work with the Partnerships Team and our partners to come up with sponsored content ideas that meet partner goals and are genuinely useful to consumers. 

- Develop and maintain a sponsored content calendar 

- Write and produce unique, useful, and engaging content across multiple formats, including blog posts, sponsored emails, social content, forum posts, and short-form video scripts. 

- Use content analysis, search data, and performance insights to create copy that addresses what consumers are actually searching for and helps them make informed financial decisions. 

- Develop an understanding of our partners’ products and the broader Canadian personal finance landscape, and manage partner review and approval rounds to make sure content is accurate and approved before it’s published. 

- Translate partner product information, key messaging, and expert input into clear, accessible, consumer-friendly content that’s educational rather than salesy, bringing your own perspective on structure, messaging, search intent, format, and audience engagement. 

- Refresh and rewrite existing sponsored content and landing pages to keep them accurate, relevant, competitive, and aligned with SEO and GEO best practices, using performance data to guide improvements. 

- Use AI tools to assist with research, ideation, analysis, and content generation, and test and implement emerging AI content practices, while maintaining strong editorial standards, originality, accuracy, and Ratehub's brand voice. 
 Manage sponsored content distribution and reporting 

- Write and build dedicated sponsored content emails, working with the Partnerships Team and partners to incorporate their messaging and goals. 

- Support organic growth for sponsored content across Google Search, AI search, Reddit and other forums, social media, email, and short-form video, and develop recommendations for how content can be distributed to bring more qualified traffic to Ratehub.ca. 

- Develop channel-specific distribution recommendations for sponsored content based on audience behaviour, search performance, AI citation patterns, and partner objectives, prioritizing the platforms and formats most likely to improve discoverability, engagement, and qualified traffic. 

- Create and support timely social content across platforms, including Meta, TikTok, and LinkedIn, and participate in community engagement where appropriate, to support sponsored campaigns, organic content, and PR initiatives. 

- Run paid social campaigns for sponsored content, including Meta ads and boosted Instagram posts for the purpose of driving traffic. 

- Track sponsored content performance and prepare performance reports for partners as requested.

About Ratehub & the Role 
 WHO IS RATEHUB? 
 We’re a company on a mission. We are a unique Canadian Fintech that is the one-stop shop for all financial needs of the consumer: Save, Spend, Borrow, Invest, and Protect. Every single team member — from Product & Engineering to Sales & Marketing, Finance, Operations, and everything in between — is obsessed with one thing: helping Canadians make better financial choices. And we’re pretty great at it, too. Via our digital application technology and our award-winning in-house brokerages, we help over 2M Canadians per month make a positive impact on their finances. We have many unique businesses: a mortgage brokerage, a life insurance brokerage, a home and auto insurance brokerage, a mortgage originations and servicing business, a Financial Services Marketplace, and a content business across Ratehub and MoneySense. 365 days a year, we deliver our users the best online mortgage experience, personalized credit card and loan options, and cheaper auto and home insurance policies than they typically get from their existing financial adviser. 
 Changing how people make financial choices isn’t easy, though. We know that achieving our mission is full of challenges — challenges that can be complex and often unexpected but that are always interesting, rewarding, and fun to solve as a team. This is where you come in. We are on the hunt for the right candidate to join us and help lead us forward to continued growth.

 About the role 
 We’re looking for a Content Strategist to help grow Ratehub’s organic presence and reach more Canadians through high-quality, data-driven content. 
 This is a mid-level individual contributor role reporting to the Senior Organic Growth Manager. You’ll work closely with the Sr. Mortgage Editor, VP of Mortgages, Content Team, PR Team, Email, Partnerships Team, and other cross-functional stakeholders. The role sits at the intersection of content strategy, SEO, GEO, analytics, content creation, and distribution. You’ll use performance data, search trends, audience insights, and emerging AI search data to identify opportunities, make recommendations, and execute content initiatives that drive organic growth. 
 As the Content Strategist dedicated to our Mortgage business unit, you’ll work closely with the Sr. Mortgage Editor who will provide the majority of the mortgage insights, analysis, and subject-matter expertise. You don’t need to be a mortgage expert when you join, but you’ll be expected to develop a strong working knowledge of the Canadian mortgage market over time, so you can confidently translate expert insights into effective content and ensure what we produce is accurate, relevant, and useful to consumers. 
 Your goal is simple: use content, search, data, and distribution to bring more qualified traffic to Ratehub.ca. You’ll work across blogs, landing pages, newsletters, eblasts, social content, short-form video, forums, and emerging search channels, with a focus on measurable organic growth. 
 What you’ll do 
 Develop a data-driven content and SEO/GEO strategy 

- Develop a strong understanding of SEO and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and use SEO and AI Search Analytics platforms to monitor how Ratehub's content is appearing in traditional rankings and AI-generated answers. 

- Use analytics, search data, audience insights, and content performance across both traditional and AI-powered search to identify opportunities and recommend what content to create, update, optimize, or retire. 

- Analyze organic traffic, rankings, on-page engagement, conversions, and AI-search visibility (mentions and citations across LLMs and generative search platforms) to understand what's working and where there are opportunities to improve. 

- Identify content gaps, high-value topics, and emerging search trends, including which topics, sources, and formats are being surfaced by AI search engines 

- Recommend the right format and channel for each opportunity (blog post, landing page, newsletter, eblast, Reel, social post, forum contribution) and changes to improve content's ability to be discovered, referenced, and cited by search engines and generative AI platforms. 

- Work with the Senior Organic Growth Manager and other stakeholders to turn analysis and recommendations into actionable content initiatives and help inform the broader SEO and GEO strategy. 

- Stay up to date on changes in search, AI discovery, GEO best practices, and emerging search behaviours. 
 Create and optimize content 

- Develop and maintain a mortgage content calendar and prioritized content backlog, balancing evergreen content with timely opportunities. 

- Write and produce unique, useful, and engaging content across multiple formats, including blog posts, landing pages, mortgage rate pages, social content, forum posts, and short-form video scripts. 

- Use content analysis, search data, and performance insights to create copy that addresses what consumers are actually searching for and helps them make informed financial decisions. 

- Develop an understanding of the factors affecting Canadian borrowers, including Bank of Canada rate announcements, Government of Canada bond yields, CPI releases, CREA housing data, lender activity, and broader economic trends, and work with the Sr. Mortgage Editor to validate that content accurately reflects the latest market developments. 

- Translate mortgage insights, market analysis, and expert commentary into clear, accessible, consumer-friendly content, using expert input as the foundation while bringing your own perspective on structure, messaging, search intent, format, and audience engagement. 

- Learn to recognize the questions, concerns, and search behaviours of Canadian mortgage consumers, and stay curious about the industry, proactively building your knowledge over time.

- Own the building and management of Mortgage weekly eblasts and promotional emails, working with the Sr. Mortgage Editor and other stakeholders to incorporate their content and insights. 

- Use performance data and audience insights to determine which topics and content should be featured and how they should be positioned, and identify the right channel and format for each piece of content rather than relying solely on traditional search. 

- Support organic growth across Google Search, AI search, Reddit and other forums, social media, email, and short-form video, and develop recommendations for how content can be distributed to bring more qualified traffic to Ratehub.ca. 

- Create and support timely social content across platforms, including Meta, TikTok, and LinkedIn, and participate in community engagement where appropriate, to support organic content, paid marketing, and PR initiatives. 
 Publish and manage website content

- Collaborate with internal stakeholders on the prioritization and implementation of relevant CMS components, website functionality, and content updates.

- A demonstrated ability to take complex information from subject matter experts and turn it into clear, compelling, consumer-friendly content. 

- A strong interest in the Canadian mortgage and broader personal finance space, with the curiosity and drive to develop deep mortgage expertise over time. 

- Previous experience with WordPress or another CMS.

 What is the opportunity? 
 Lead the Chief Control Office as a 2nd line of defense assurance team reporting to the CFO Group. You'll elevate RBC's financial reporting control environment and strengthen operational risk stewardship across the CFO Group. In this role, you'll drive strategic implementation of operational risk and regulatory compliance programs, partnering with 1st line teams across Enterprise Controllership, Tax, platforms, and COO. You'll combine subject matter expertise with people leadership, directing a team of specialists to embed systematic, disciplined risk management practices that enhance the effectiveness of controls and governance across CFO Group operations.

 What will you do? 

- Lead CFO Group through Operational Risk program transformation as launched by GRM, including development of implementation frameworks, project plans, guidance, training delivery, and design of systems and tools as required.

- Provide strategic advice on control and risk trends through ongoing reviews; identify improvements and solutions to key control issues impacting CFO Group risks and processes.

- Guide CFO Group teams on risk and control identification, digital risk register and control register documentation, enterprise issue management, and annual RCSA processes; ensure adherence to GRM policies and frameworks.

- Design and oversee an enhanced regulatory compliance monitoring and reporting program for senior executives; manage quality assurance of documentation and testing standards aligned to RBC expectations.

- Conduct regulatory horizon scanning for CFO risk themes; support change management activities and quality assurance reviews in partnership with compliance teams.

- Lead, motivate, and inspire a diverse team of subject matter experts; communicate Chief Control Office vision and direction while clarifying priorities to drive efficiency and engagement.

- Deep experience in risk management, internal controls, banking processes, and industry best practices

- Proven track record as a valued advisor with ability to provide constructive challenge and communicate with senior stakeholders; strong relationship management skills

phenom:RBCAA0088:R-0000188123.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 RBC Home Equity Financing is one of Canada’s most significant and strategically vital lending businesses — and we’re looking for a Senior Marketing Manager to be part of the next chapter of growth for this exciting portfolio.
 The Canadian mortgage space is a dynamic space that continues to evolve. A single decision represents the largest financial commitment most Canadians will ever make, so emotion, trust, and life's biggest milestones meet hard numbers and real competition. It calls for marketers who can balance brand storytelling with performance rigor, who can move potential home buyers from a dream to a decision. 
 As the Senior Marketing Manager, Home Equity Financing, you will shape and drive integrated marketing strategies across mass advertising, digital and programmatic.
 If you are a bold, results-oriented marketer who thrives on turning complex challenges into breakthrough campaigns — and you have a track record of delivering integrated, multi-channel programs at scale that move the needle on acquisition — this is your opportunity to shape how millions of Canadians experience one of the most pivotal moments of their financial lives.

 What will you do?
 Integrated Campaign Planning and Execution 

- Build a strong working relationship with an extensive network of internal partners and leverage your ability to impact and influence partnerships across the Bank.

- Own and lead best-in-class mass integrated campaign planning and go-to-market execution across owned and paid channels.

- Develop and deliver creative and media briefs, tactical plans and collaborate with agency partners and external vendors to deliver high-quality creative and media executions on time and on budget.

- Proactively seek out new growth opportunities, campaign innovation and test initiatives to drive continuous improvement and learning.

- Partner closely with the performance marketing team to drive year-round acquisition initiatives, ensuring we are efficiently scaling acquisition growth and maximizing ROI, and translating data into clear, actionable recommendations.

- Lead targeted acquisition campaigns that activate field sales and owned digital channels, building a seamless journey from first impression to funded mortgage.

- Keep a keen eye to process to drive efficiencies and excellence across all stages.

- Manage marketing budget efficiently, focusing on transparency, efficiency, and flexibility to make the most of market opportunities.

 Measurement & Performance Reporting 

- Monitor, report and present marketing results to line-of-business stakeholders providing data-driven recommendations to optimize campaigns to drive growth.

- Translate marketing performance metrics into clear business outcomes, articulating the “so what” for the line of business and recommending where to double down or course-correct.

- Lead the cross-functional development of Spring campaign lead reporting collaborating with Digital Marketing Partners

- Oversee the development and communication of monthly lead results.

 Team Leadership & People Development 

- Lead, mentor, and develop two marketing managers, setting clear direction, maintaining high standards, and creating conditions for sustained excellence

- Provide strong people management, including coaching, performance development, career planning, and recognition

- Model inclusive leadership behaviours consistent with RBC’s values and Purpose

 What do you need to succeed?
 Must-have: 

- 7+ years marketing experience, with demonstrated ability to think strategically.

- Experience planning, managing, and optimizing multi-million dollar marketing budget with rigorous measurement and accountability

- Strong analytical capabilities; comfort with data, performance metrics, and a fact-based approach to decision-making and executive communication

- Proven project management and organizational skills. Ability to multi-task, as well as confidently and effectively lead a project team through timelines, prioritization, budget management and collaboration.

- Ability to influence peers and partners through collaborative, transparent socialization, to secure alignment on our vision and recommendations.

- Ability to think strategically and execute with excellence; must be an enthusiastic, well-organized self-starter, able to use initiative and adapt to change within a fast-paced environment.

- Strong attention to detail and ability to lead multi-stakeholder groups to develop and execute targeted marketing campaigns.

- A growth mindset and a strong track record of insight-led marketing in a culture that values a collaborative approach.

- 3+ years of people management experience, with a demonstrated track record of building and leading high-performing teams

 Nice-to-have: 

- FI experience an asset and/or experience in large matrix organizations.

- University degree - undergraduate and/or MBA - in marketing or other related field

- Mass marketing experience.

- Direct experience marketing mortgage, HELOC, or secured lending products

- Experience in a large financial institution or similarly regulated, complex matrix environment

 What’s in it for you? 
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

- A high-impact, highly visible role at the heart of one of RBC’s most strategically important consumer lending businesses

- The opportunity to lead an exceptional team and own end-to-end marketing accountability across a major portfolio

- A competitive total compensation package including base salary, performance-based incentive, and comprehensive benefits

- Opportunities to take on progressively greater accountabilities and grow your career at Canada’s largest bank

- Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team

- Access to a wide range of learning and development resources, including mentorship, skills development, and leadership programs

- Flexible work arrangements and modern work environments designed to support your best work

With a strong foundation in Canada and a dynamic international presence, our team combines deep industry knowledge with innovative technology to drive client success. At RBC Investor Services, we are committed to fostering a collaborative, forward-thinking culture where professionals thrive in a fast-paced, client-centric environment. Joining our team means contributing to a legacy of excellence within one of the world’s most respected financial institutions, where your growth is supported, and your impact matters.

 What is the opportunity? 
 In this role, you will be responsible for the identification, development, implementation of new Asset Servicing sales opportunities.  You will participate in the definition of strategy to take RBC Investor Services (IS) products to market to drive new sales through client acquisition and revenue generation.

 What will you do? 

- Articulate a clear vision for sales growth across your defined territory that primarily focuses on the acquisition of new client names.

- Point of contact for strategic discussions with CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, and COOs looking to drive digital transformation, innovation journeys, and operational efficiency exercises. Be conversant and comfortable having strategic conversations on asset servicing capabilities, operational process improvements, managed services, outsourcing and modern technologies including Front – Mid and Back Office Fintechs, Cloud, APIs, AI, Web Technologies, Security, etc.

- Identify opportunities in the market for expanding RBCIS footprint by enhancing the use of people, process, and technology to deliver new products and services to the market.  This will include liaising and collaborate with product, technology and strategy owners at RBCIS to build and deliver new innovative product offerings and construct enterprise solutions.

- Ensure sales pipeline opportunities are well documented to create executive visibility into revenue targets and pipeline.

- Ultimate ownership and oversight of the delivery of RFI/RFP and proposal management processes for opportunity portfolio

- Consultant engagement as required in support of complex long sales cycle deals.

- Travel outside of the office, typically to Canadian cities including overnight stays may be required.

 What do you need to succeed? 

- 10+ years of relevant experience within the financial services and/or asset servicing industry

Job Description 

 What is the Opportunity? 
 As part of the Chief Data Office, collaborating closely with Chief Financial Office and Group Risk Management teams, the Associate Director is the first line of defense for data management risk and is responsible for building and maintaining a comprehensive inventory of data management practice components for Finance and Risk domains.

The ideal candidate will provide expertise and support to senior management in identification, documentation and maintenance of data risk management requirements, enhancing their ability to anticipate and manage data management risks effectively.
 ​
 What will you do? 

- Act as a centre of excellence and advocate for data management best practices for Finance and Risk domains

- Contribute to and support communication of data strategies, standards and initiatives to Finance and Risk partners

- Facilitate building and maintaining a comprehensive inventory of data management practice components for each Finance and Risk domains

 What is the opportunity? 
 As an RBC Ambassador, you create value at the moments that matter most to newcomers and help them achieve their goals by collaborating with your colleagues and partners at RBC. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing partnerships with local community organizations that support newcomers' settlement. This role, which requires mobility and flexibility, is key to organizing and delivering advisory events for community partners. This unique position leverages your expertise in digital advising and your ability to build internal and external Together at RBC partnerships to maximize interactions.
 Specifically, you and your team will address the everyday banking, credit, and investment needs of both clients and non-clients (primarily newcomers), as well as other needs that extend beyond traditional banking services. Whether you're showing newcomers how to use digital banking, assisting with their onboarding as new clients, referring them to a specialist for their more complex transactions, or providing guidance beyond RBC's standard offerings—for example, on adapting to Canadian culture, understanding community needs, or entering the job market—your expertise will contribute to delivering a memorable experience that fosters satisfaction and loyalty.

 You will work from home and will be required to travel within the market.

 What will you do? 

- Create and develop partnerships with newcomer services and settlement agencies to enable RBC to reach as many newcomers as possible in Quebec.

- Applying the Together at RBC principle as an advisor, you possess extensive expertise in providing advice in everyday banking, investments, and credit, leveraging this expertise to offer individuals and businesses a robust, digitally focused experience.

- Focus on educating newcomers, including through demonstrations, and leverage technology to deliver a memorable customer experience, enhance the brand, and build customer loyalty.

- Explore, innovate, and promote excellence in both the customer and partner experience.

- Collaborate with internal (Together at RBC) and external partners to ensure newcomers receive personalized and specialized advice.

- Travel within the region to meet with community partners and clients as needed.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must-have 

- Sound understanding of the Canadian settlement process

- Warm and friendly demeanor, customer-centric approach, and ability to thrive in a fast-paced retail environment

- Above-average knowledge of a wide range of digital devices (smartphones, tablets, laptops, etc.) and the ability to quickly learn new technologies

- High emotional intelligence, excellent situational awareness, problem-solving and interpersonal skills, and the ability to proactively build strong relationships and connections with clients

- Strong communication skills and comfort speaking in public at advisory events

- Strong ability to multitask, initiative, and the ability to work independently in a changing environment

- Mutual fund sales license (e.g., Investment Funds in Canada course or Canadian Securities Course)

- Bilingualism (English and French) required, as you will regularly serve our clients with English and French-speaking needs.

 Nice-to-have 

- Trilingual in English, French, and Spanish

- Proven track record of building and maintaining client relationships in the financial or service industry

- Ability to provide financial advice in English

- The knowledge of a third language is an asset

 What's in it for you? 
We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

- A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation.

- A world-class training program in financial services

- Excellent career development and access to a variety of job opportunities across business and geographies

- Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities

- Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team

 Job Skills 
Adaptability, Advice Based Solutions, Client Centricity, Client Discovery, Communication, Curious Mindset, Data Analysis, Digital Literacy

phenom:RBCAA0088:R-0000190603.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 As a Senior Manager, Treasury Solutions with RBC’s Treasury Solutions Corporate Coverage team, you will be responsible to proactively provide advice and enable clients to leverage RBC’s cash management solutions, taking responsibility for clients’ onboarding, activation, and ongoing adoption of digital solutions. You will manage and grow revenue from a portfolio of complex large commercial/corporate clients by offering a full suite of cash management solutions. You will execute on the client sales plan, delivering a differentiated client experience by offering cash management solutions focused on meeting clients’ business and financial goals to grow relationships, enhance loyalty, and drive innovation with our clients.

 What will you do? 

- Build relationships and manage revenue growth within a portfolio of clients with a focus on recognizing and supporting client needs, enhancing client loyalty, and sharing opportunities for additional RBC offerings across the Bank footprint

- Act as the single point of contact throughout the cash management end-to-end onboarding process, partner with the relationship team and follow up with clients to ensure an exceptional client experience

- Partner with Relationship Managers to develop a coordinated client contact strategy and to complete annual relationship reviews, ensuring future client needs are identified and met

- Provide tailored advice and insights to clients on new or emerging topics that will impact their business

- Lead with a growth mindset, focusing on what’s possible to maximize client acquisition, growth, and an exceptional client experience

- Deliver financial and business “insight” advice through a differentiated value proposition by presenting solutions that clearly articulate the benefits and advantages to the client; help the client to understand alternatives, navigate and implement proposed solutions; and identify opportunities and refer clients to RBC Partners to meet the client’s broader advice needs

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must Have 

- 5+ years of related experience in commercial or corporate banking sales, treasury & cash management products/solutions

- Strong knowledge of cash management/deposit products and emerging industry trends

- Proven client advice/service, sales, and relationship management experience with the ability to match client needs with products/structure solutions

- Demonstrated project management, organizational and time management skills

- Robust written and verbal communication skills

- Proficiency with software applications including MS Office/AI

- Willingness and ability to travel to meet clients in person

 Nice-to-Have 

- Certified Treasury Professional ("CTP") Designation, Master of Business (“MBA”), or similar qualification

 What’s in it for you? 
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

- Ability to make a difference and lasting impact

- Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team

- Opportunities to do challenging work

ashby:rewind:14f7c82a-fb73-4938-9cb9-a50.description:
Rewind is a service that protects the critical data that powers businesses of all sizes. Our focus is on backing up data that lives in the cloud - in apps like Jira, GitHub, Confluence and Shopify. We are backed by Insight Partners, Inovia, Bessemer and Atlassian Ventures and are proud to be recognized as one of Canada's 50 fastest growing technology companies (2023 Deloitte Fast 50 https://www.deloitte.com/ca/en/about/press-room/deloitte-canada-announces-its-annual-technology-fast-50tm-program-winners.html). We invite you to read our startup story https://rewind.io/blog/why-we-started-rewind-backups/ to learn where we came from and where we’re going.

Read about our mission, story and values here https://rewind.com/about-us/.
To find out more about our perks, click here https://rewind.com/careers/#:~:text=Working%20at%20Rewind%20has%20its%20perks.
Some of our Blogs might help you get a better understanding of what we do here. You can find them all here https://rewind.com/blog/.

Thriving at Rewind:

We embrace the fast-paced, ever-changing nature of startup life. If you love working with speed, agility, and creativity, you’ll feel right at home here. Here's what it takes to succeed with us:

 - Team-First Mentality: We put teamwork at the core of everything we do, believing that we are better when we are together. Success is shared, and when the team wins, we all win.

 - Performance-Driven Mindset: We are proactive, goal-oriented, and focused on delivering tangible, high-quality results. We go beyond meeting expectations - we aim to exceed them.

 - Flexible Work-Life Approach: We encourage balance and understand the need to recharge. While we stay agile for urgent needs, we make sure there's time to recover and enjoy life.

 - Customer Centricity: Our commitment to customers shapes everything we do. We listen, build relationships, and innovate - from our dedicated customer support team to our engineers, everyone at our company is focused on solving problems that matter most to our users.

 - Taking Initiative: We value ownership and proactive problem-solving. We encourage team members to think creatively, take ownership, and lead improvements. Your ideas and actions drive our success.

 - We Make Time for Fun: We work hard and make time to enjoy the journey. It’s not just about hitting milestones—it’s about making the experience rewarding along the way.

The Senior Technical Support Engineer (T3) is the highest tier of our support organization, serving as a bridge between customer support and engineering. You will own the most complex, ambiguous technical escalations that our T1 and T2 teams cannot resolve - including issues that previously required involvement from the Engineering Run Team.





THE ROLE

As a Senior Technical Support Engineer, you will serve as the final escalation point within the support organization. You bring a software development background and deep technical instincts to diagnose root causes, reproduce edge cases, write or read code to understand issues at depth, and work directly with the Engineering team to drive resolution. This is not a traditional support role - you will spend a significant portion of your time doing technical investigation work that sits at the boundary of support and engineering.

This role requires participation on a on-call rotation including weekends and holidays.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the most complex technical escalations from T1 and T2, serving as the final line of defense.

 - Investigate and reproduce customer-reported bugs, data inconsistencies, and integration failures across Rewind's supported platforms (Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Shopify, QuickBooks Online, and more)

 - Read and write code (primarily in the context of debugging and scripting) to diagnose issues, test hypotheses, and validate fixes

 - Work directly with Engineering to clearly articulate bugs, provide reproducible test cases, and track fixes through to resolution

 - Manage and resolve issues in customer environments involving API integrations, OAuth configurations, webhook failures, and platform-level permissions

 - Handle data restoration requests and complex recovery scenarios requiring deep knowledge of Rewind's backup architecture

 - Own enterprise customer onboarding when required, including installation, deployment, and education, ensuring the customer is fully set up for success

 - Help build and maintain the internal knowledge base for complex issue patterns, enabling T1/T2 to self-serve future resolutions

 - Participate in on-call rotations for P1 incidents affecting enterprise customers

 - Identify recurring escalation patterns and proactively surface product improvement opportunities to Engineering and Product




WHAT YOU BRING

Required

 - 5+ years of experience in a technical support, solutions engineering, or software development role

 - Computer Science degree or equivalent practical experience (you can read and write code)

 - Proficiency in at least one scripting or programming language (Python, Ruby, JavaScript, or similar)

 - Strong understanding of REST APIs, OAuth, webhooks, and modern SaaS integration patterns

 - Experience with cloud platforms and SaaS ecosystems (Atlassian, GitHub, Shopify, or similar)

 - AWS - CloudWatch for logs, OpenSearch/Kibana for search infrastructure, SQS/SNS for async processing

 - Ability to read logs, inspect API responses, and debug issues at the network and application layers

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication - you can explain a complex technical root cause to a non-technical customer and to an engineer on the same day

 - Comfort working independently in ambiguous, high-stakes situations with limited documentation

Nice to Have

 - Experience with backup, recovery, or data resilience products

 - Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, or Atlassian platform administration

 - Experience with PostgreSQL and DynamoDB

 - Prior experience in a SaaS company at a similar scale (Series B / growth stage)

 - Experience working with enterprise customers and navigating complex account relationships




LOCATION

There is a strong preference for candidates based in Ontario for easier collaboration.



Compensation Philosophy
The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. 

In some cases, we’re open to hiring at a higher level for the right person and are committed to paying competitively and fairly.

If your experience is closer to an earlier career stage, we may still consider your application. In that case, we would evaluate the role at a different level within our levelling framework.

Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at Rewind.



Why join Rewind

At Rewind, you’ll help shape the future of data protection for thousands of businesses. We’re performance-driven, innovative, and not afraid to challenge what’s possible. You’ll join a team that values trust, accountability, and respect for people’s time — and encourages every employee to experiment, think critically, and grow.

We support innovation through experimentation — including smart use of AI tools — and believe the best ideas come from those who aren’t afraid to push boundaries.




How Rewind Will Support You
We know that enjoying the journey is just as important as reaching our goals. We work hard to create a positive, inclusive environment where fun and laughter are part of our everyday routine. We also offer a variety of benefits to support your success both at work and in your personal life which includes but is not limited to: 

 - Flexible work hours

 - Employee stock options

 - Health benefits

 - 3 weeks vacation

 - 7 life leave days

 - 2 Level Up days for professional development

 - 1 volunteer day

 - Summer Fridays and office closed during the holiday break in December

 - Paid parental leave

 - $2000/year wellness/home office allowance

 - $5000/year professional development allowance

Rewind is committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. We value how each new hire is an opportunity for us to bring in a different perspective, and we are always eager to further diversify our company. We strongly encourage candidates of all different backgrounds and identities to apply.



AI Usage

Our recruitment process may include the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools to help manage and review applications efficiently. These tools assist our team, but hiring decisions are ultimately made by human reviewers.

Account Executive, Mid-Market (Bilingual English/French)
About Rippling
Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

 This role is responsible for driving retention and revenue growth within an assigned portfolio of Greater Toronto Area based Enterprise customers (150–1499 employees).

 The Strategic Account Executive partners closely with clients to deliver innovative, outcome-based solutions through strategic planning, executive engagement, and proactive prospecting.

 What you’ll do: 

- Primary focus on new logo acquisition within the GTA mid-market segment (150–1499 employees), proactively identifying, targeting, and closing net-new business opportunities, complemented by managing an existing base of billing business customers (retention, upsell, cross-sell).

- Develop and execute strategic account penetration plans to gain “insider status” and position Rogers as a trusted partner within net-new prospect organizations.

- Collaborate with internal stakeholders to craft tailored, outcome-based value propositions, overcoming barriers to sale and differentiating Rogers in competitive pursuits.

- Lead the development of compelling proposals and business cases, navigating internal stakeholders to advance and close complex opportunities.

- Contribute to a high-performance culture by sharing best practices, prospecting strategies, and wins with the broader Commercial Acquisition team.

- Maintain disciplined pipeline management and forecasting through Salesforce, while completing all training requirements and representing Rogers as a strong brand ambassador.

- Post-secondary degree or equivalent experience with a minimum of 3-5+ years of success in enterprise/strategic sales

- Proven track record of exceeding quota through new business acquisition, with strong funnel management and disciplined pipeline execution

- Deep experience selling into CIOs, IT leaders, and C-suite stakeholders, navigating complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

- Strong industry expertise across telecom and technology solutions (wireless, wireline, IoT, data centre, cloud, managed & professional services, and unified communications)

- Demonstrated ability to build and grow executive-level relationships and position as a trusted advisor solving meaningful business challenges

- Highly developed business acumen, communication, and presentation skills, with confidence engaging senior internal and external audiences

- Proven ability to develop and execute strategic account plans, translating customer needs into differentiated solutions and outcomes

- Collaborative team player with the ability to lead cross-functional virtual teams and navigate internal stakeholders to close complex deals

- Self-starter with a hunter mindset—results-driven, accountable, adaptable, and motivated to win new business in a fast-paced environment

This role balances three core areas: converting assigned inbound and marketing-generated leads, creating opportunities through proactive field activity, and supporting direct sellers as a trusted payments expert on qualified customer opportunities.

 Specialists will manage their own opportunities from discovery through activation, maintain a consistent in-market presence with merchants and local business networks, and collaborate with direct sellers on deals that benefit from deeper payments expertise. On assisted opportunities, the direct seller remains the customer relationship owner while the specialist provides payment discovery, solution guidance and support throughout the sales cycle.

 Convert Inbound Demand 

- Engage assigned digital and marketing-generated opportunities quickly and professionally.

- Conduct discovery to understand the merchant business, current payment environment, operational needs and growth goals.

- Recommend an appropriate Rogers Point of Sale solution and move qualified opportunities through the sales cycle to activation.

- Support direct sellers with discovery, qualification, customer presentations, demonstrations, statement reviews and objection handling while maintaining clearly documented ownership, handoffs and next steps.

- Join qualified customer conversations as the payments expert while reinforcing the direct seller as the relationship owner.

- Help sellers identify RPoS opportunities within new and existing customer conversations.

- Provide clear deal guidance, next steps and ownership at each stage of an assisted opportunity.

 Deliver Payments Expertise

successfactors:jobs.scotiabank.com:60087.description:
Requisition ID: 255618

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 To ensure that our purpose is front and centre in all we do, we have refreshed our name to Financial Planners under the Scotia Financial Planning team (formerly known as “Investment Specialist” under the Mobile Advice Team) within our Global Asset Management Division. 

As a Financial Planner, you will focus on developing and deepening client relationships by providing high quality advice and service within the mass affluent market. As a dedicated entrepreneur, you know how to leverage your external networks and centres of influence and understand that growing a practice is all about building new and long-term relationships. Most importantly, you realize that your clients are your greatest asset, and your priority is providing investment and financial planning advice to help them meet their unique goals.  

You also enjoy the flexibility of being able to meet clients outside of the office, on a schedule that best suits you and them. Finally, you recognize the value of working within a collective Scotiabank framework that benefits both your clients and your practice overall.  

Following a comprehensive financial planning framework, you will be responsible for driving investment sales and new client acquisition, while adhering to Global Sales Principles, compliance and regulatory requirements. You will also establish business development opportunities with prospects and clients within the assigned market area. Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture! 

 Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:  
Promote the development and sustainable growth of proprietary investment business in the assigned market area by: 

- Business Development: Executing on business development plans for prospects and existing clients within the mass affluent market. Identifying additional business development opportunities and facilitating the implementation of an investment solution and/or referral to the appropriate partners.  

- Client-Centric: Providing client-centric investment solutions through a financial planning framework, aligning with Global Sales Principles. Conducting outbound communications and proactive calling to prospects to remain top-of-mind for future business opportunities. Conducting complimentary needs analysis across several financial statements, including competitor statements. 

- Community Involvement: Participating actively in local professional and community events and associations to develop and expand your network. Identifying opportunities to deliver community information sessions and financial seminars to grow prospects. Building and maintaining a market profile in the assigned market area. Networking with investment industry specialists while managing a small budget for independent marketing-based activities.  

 Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We’d love to work with you if you have: 

- 3 years of experience in financial planning and investment sales.  

- Your mutual funds certified professional. You have current accreditation and good standing for MFDA licensing requirements (Investments Funds in Canada or Canadian Securities Course).  

- You have successfully completed a Personal Financial Planning (PFP®) designation and/or a Certified Financial Planner (CFP®) designation.  

- Proven networking, client acquisition and interpersonal skills; experience building and maintaining Centres of Influence (COIs)  

- You’re goal oriented and entrepreneurial. You can work independently as a self-motivated entrepreneur with minimal supervision and as part of a larger team.  

- Extensive knowledge of competitive offerings, market trends, economic conditions, and the regulatory environment.  

- A valid driver's license and access to a vehicle, to meet clients and prospects within the designated district. 

 What’s in it for you?   

- An entrepreneurial culture with the freedom to develop your career.  

- A fast-paced, flexible work environment where you can set your own hours and meet clients when and where it’s convenient. 

- A compensation structure that rewards growing and maintaining your client base. 

- Access to leading-edge resources to support your growth, including dedicated marketing support, powerful mobile technology, leading CRM, portfolio, and financial planning software.  

- The ability to build long-lasting client relationships through exceptional advice and service. 

- A partnership with our branches and access to Scotia Global Asset Management to deliver an excellent client experience.  

- A work culture that promotes diversity, respect, and inclusion.  

 Other Information  
•    Please note that the compensation structure for this role is base plus variable pay. This is a mobile role and will require frequent travel.  

 Another stream to our financial planning advice lays within the Canadian Retail Banking Division. This role is called Financial Advisor, Investment & Retirement (FAIR). If you are interested in learning more about this role, please review the “ Financial Advisor, Investment & Retirement , Branch Network”  posting.

successfactors:jobs.scotiabank.com:60651.description:
Requisition ID: 274892 

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 Purpose 

 Responsible for supporting the development, management and delivery of Private Banking learning programs and changes across all delivery modalities including, but not limited to, virtual classes, face to face classes, eLearning, simulations, videos and podcasts, learning plans and guides, leader guides, and job shadow guides. The Manager will work with internal and external partners and business stakeholders to implement identified changes. This role will also fulfill the program reporting needs and work with the appropriate HR Services group as required. 

 What you will be doing: 

- Responsible for the implementation of content maintenance, the integration of new content, the alignment to new strategies and ongoing learning experience, and delivery modernization 

- Contributes to the design and development and takes a lead role in the quality control of learning programs that support a customer focused culture across the Private Banking network 

- Leads virtual training  sessions and other learning and development sessions as required 

- Impacts the quality and delivery of learning programs through leading regular touchpoints with Private Banking employees to gather feedback and provide direct support and coaching 

- Responsible for engaging with Managers, Senior Managers and Directors to provide professional guidance in supporting training Program progression, identifying opportunities for coaching and development, and addressing areas of concern 

- Takes insights and opportunities from these sessions to address gaps in learning and develop long-term solutions and strategy 

- Supports vendor relationships, including the coordination of content development, reviews and approvals, scheduling virtual and in-person sessions, venue contracts and attendance.   

- Coordinates with the Learning COE and Learning Management System teams on the implementation of complex and large content creation and/or changes to the existing content in accordance with established guidelines and standards 

- Provides ongoing support to the Senior Manager with training content details, reporting on content updates, collaborating with partners in Private Banking, Canadian Banking, RBSC, Contact Centre, product, and technology groups to obtain support and information when required 

- Prepares presentations for Senior Manager, senior audiences and partners when required 
 Leads regional and national calls to educate and improve learning program engagement by connecting the dots across a wide range of audiences to effectively communicate change and influence adoption 

- Develops visuals including learning journey maps, infographics, podcasts, etc. to support learning methodologies and delivery strategies 

- Assesses impacts, dependencies, and trade-offs across all learning programs when managing and making changes to the content library, taking all learning assets and the different modalities into consideration 

- Creates communications when required and evaluation plans for learning programs and assists in the implementation across the network 

- Develops and maintains websites in accordance with the bank standards and guidelines 

- Supports the learning program pages across various sites, including day-to-day maintenance, document upload and working with respective partners  

- Works with the Learning COE and HR Services to set-up and maintain learning assets and to establish cadence of reports and data from Learning Management System 

- Creates and maintains internal learning reports and dashboards  

- Maintains training surveys and shares related insights 

- Actions and responds to requests received via email inboxes 

- Monitors market leading trends and learning best practices to propose enhancements to the learning experience 

- Understands how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions 

- Actively pursues effective and efficient operations of the respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, its Code of Conduct and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-today business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.   

- Champions a high-performance environment and contributes to an inclusive work environment. 

 Do you have the skills to enable you to be successful in this role? We would love to work with you if you have: 

- 3 years Private Banking, Retail or Commercial banking experience and / or Learning & Development, Sales Effectiveness experience 

- University or community college degree preferred 

- Bi-Lingual (English / French is an asset) 

- Knowledge of adult learning principles, and design and development principles  

- Thorough knowledge of Bank products, services, policies, and procedures 

- Credit / Financial analysis experience is an asset 

- Strong project management skills and ability to meet deadlines 

- Strong communication skills, both verbal and written 

- Strong presentation skills required

successfactors:jobs.scotiabank.com:60096.title: Financial Planner, Scotia Financial Planning - Richmond, Vancouver
successfactors:jobs.scotiabank.com:60096.description:
Requisition ID: 255597

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 To ensure that our purpose is front and centre in all we do, we have refreshed our name to Financial Planners under the Scotia Financial Planning team (formerly known as “Investment Specialist” under the Mobile Advice Team) within our Global Asset Management Division. 

As a Financial Planner, you will focus on developing and deepening client relationships by providing high quality advice and service within the mass affluent market. As a dedicated entrepreneur, you know how to leverage your external networks and centres of influence and understand that growing a practice is all about building new and long-term relationships. Most importantly, you realize that your clients are your greatest asset, and your priority is providing investment and financial planning advice to help them meet their unique goals.  

You also enjoy the flexibility of being able to meet clients outside of the office, on a schedule that best suits you and them. Finally, you recognize the value of working within a collective Scotiabank framework that benefits both your clients and your practice overall.  

Following a comprehensive financial planning framework, you will be responsible for driving investment sales and new client acquisition, while adhering to Global Sales Principles, compliance and regulatory requirements. You will also establish business development opportunities with prospects and clients within the assigned market area. Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture! 

 Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:  
Promote the development and sustainable growth of proprietary investment business in the assigned market area by: 

- Business Development: Executing on business development plans for prospects and existing clients within the mass affluent market. Identifying additional business development opportunities and facilitating the implementation of an investment solution and/or referral to the appropriate partners.  

- Client-Centric: Providing client-centric investment solutions through a financial planning framework, aligning with Global Sales Principles. Conducting outbound communications and proactive calling to prospects to remain top-of-mind for future business opportunities. Conducting complimentary needs analysis across several financial statements, including competitor statements. 

- Community Involvement: Participating actively in local professional and community events and associations to develop and expand your network. Identifying opportunities to deliver community information sessions and financial seminars to grow prospects. Building and maintaining a market profile in the assigned market area. Networking with investment industry specialists while managing a small budget for independent marketing-based activities.  

 Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We’d love to work with you if you have: 

- 3 years of experience in financial planning and investment sales.  

- Your mutual funds certified professional. You have current accreditation and good standing for MFDA licensing requirements (Investments Funds in Canada or Canadian Securities Course).  

- You have successfully completed a Personal Financial Planning (PFP®) designation and/or a Certified Financial Planner (CFP®) designation.  

- Proven networking, client acquisition and interpersonal skills; experience building and maintaining Centres of Influence (COIs)  

- You’re goal oriented and entrepreneurial. You can work independently as a self-motivated entrepreneur with minimal supervision and as part of a larger team.  

- Extensive knowledge of competitive offerings, market trends, economic conditions, and the regulatory environment.  

- A valid driver's license and access to a vehicle, to meet clients and prospects within the designated district. 

 What’s in it for you?   

- An entrepreneurial culture with the freedom to develop your career.  

- A fast-paced, flexible work environment where you can set your own hours and meet clients when and where it’s convenient. 

- A compensation structure that rewards growing and maintaining your client base. 

- Access to leading-edge resources to support your growth, including dedicated marketing support, powerful mobile technology, leading CRM, portfolio, and financial planning software.  

- The ability to build long-lasting client relationships through exceptional advice and service. 

- A partnership with our branches and access to Scotia Global Asset Management to deliver an excellent client experience.  

- A work culture that promotes diversity, respect, and inclusion.  

 Other Information  
•    Please note that the compensation structure for this role is base plus variable pay. This is a mobile role and will require frequent travel.  

 Another stream to our financial planning advice lays within the Canadian Retail Banking Division. This role is called Financial Advisor, Investment & Retirement (FAIR). If you are interested in learning more about this role, please review the “ Financial Advisor, Investment & Retirement , Branch Network”  posting.
