Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 Global Transaction Banking 

 Global Transaction Banking (GTB) is the payments and transaction engine of Scotiabank. We support Small Business, Commercial and Corporate clients with effective treasury management solutions coupled with a best-in-class service model, making it easy for clients to do business with us.

As businesses build their digital capabilities and transform their operating models, their payment needs are evolving too. Boasting a unique global footprint, GTB’s comprehensive suite of innovative banking solutions help our business clients generate operational efficiencies, streamline and simplify payments, improve working capital performance, and mitigate financial risk.

At Scotiabank, we embrace your strengths, ideas, and ambitions. GTB is a fast-growing team with a focus on the Americas, particularly Canada, the U.S., Mexico, and we are seeking top tier talent to complement our organization.

Join a purpose-driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

 Purpose 

 The Manager, Merchant Services – Sales Operations contributes to the profitability and revenue growth of the Global Business Markets (GBM) portfolio by supporting the sales team and optimizing the sales process to improve efficiency, productivity, and overall performance.

 The Manager is responsible for activating merchant services sales processes across all business segments (Small Business, Commercial and Corporate) and will work closely with the segment stakeholders and partners on executing the sales processes for new product launches, refresh of existing capabilities and engagement model. As part of the role, the Manager will work on identifying and understanding pain points arising through the merchant sales cycle. Success in this role will be demonstrated by improved satisfaction of the sales teams and through the growth of new opportunities.

 The Manager will work independently, receiving direction from the Senior Manager and will participate in an interdivisional product and sales groups, such as Global transactions Banking, Bank’s Operational organizations (Legal Counsel, Risk and Compliance, AML, Call Centre, Accounting, Systems, Finance, Credit Solutions and Customer Service, etc.). The Manager must also be comfortable in managing a complex array of external vendors and partners.

 Because of the complexities involved in this product line, prior relevant experience in product management, product engagement, or sales enablement would be a highly desirable asset.

 What You’ll Do: 

- Contribute to the business development and financial success of Sales through the development of customized client-facing material. Work with Sales, the Proposal Writing team and partner on ad-hoc requests (e.g., process development and execution, executive support, etc.).

- Collaborate with the Merchant Services Product and Sales Enablement teams on the merchant services sales journey to ensure success of new sales processes and product capabilities are understood and are utilized across key segments and within the distribution network.

- Ensure adherence to the merchant sales governance framework in collaboration with the stakeholders and segment partners. Analyze and evaluate the sales process, identify bottlenecks or inefficiencies, and propose and implement solutions to streamline and improve overall sales operations.

- Support the maintenance of sales process documentation, including sales playbooks, standard operating procedures, and best practices. Ensure the sales team is well-informed and adhering to established processes.

- Support the fostering of an environment in which the internal stakeholders and external partners pursue effective and efficient operations, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations of operational risk, sales conduct, regulatory and compliance risk.

 What You'll Bring: 

- Degree/post graduate degree, preferably in business, marketing, or a related field

- Proven experience in sales operations, enablement, project/portfolio management or similar role

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with internal stakeholders and sales teams

- Strong presentation skills with the ability to articulate results, challenges, recommendations and solutions to various people at different levels across the organization

- Attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

- Knowledge of Global Banking Markets, products, and sales culture

- Good understanding of the Small Business, Commercial and Corporate Bank’s objectives, strategies, and structure is also required

- Familiarity with sales methodologies, processes, and best practices

- 3+ years’ experience with stakeholder and vendor management and relevant experience in the merchant services and/or payment industry

- A great opportunity for a position within GTB, which is a key area of focus for Scotiabank

- A chance to join a vibrant high-performing team that is supportive and accountable

- Working in an inclusive and collaborative environment that encourages creativity, curiosity, and celebrates success

- A rewarding career path with diverse opportunities for professional development

- Internal development to support your growth and enhance your skills

- Career progression opportunities. We hire you for your talent and not just for the job. We want to see you succeed not just in your role but in your career as a whole

- This is a full-time role that offers competitive compensation and benefits package

Requisition ID: 271998 

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 Senior Client Relationship Manager, Agriculture Banking - Canadian Commercial Banking (Brantford / Niagara region) 

 Purpose 

Agricultural banking is looking for a dynamic self-starter who embraces a team environment and shares our passion for helping Canadian businesses in the Agriculture sector achieve their goals to join our team as a Senior Client Relationship Manager.

Our Agricultural banking professionals contribute to the overall success of the National Agriculture Strategy in Canada ensuring specific individual goals, plans, initiatives are executed / delivered in support of the team’s business strategies and objectives.

The Senior Client Relationship Manager “SCRM” is a product generalist who has solid understanding of financial products and services and focuses on the cross sell and retention of existing Agriculture business customers. 

You will be responsible for identifying prospects in target markets, developing proposed sales pipelines, conducting prospect sales calls and qualifying opportunities based on customer information and a high level of due diligence. You will manage a customer portfolio of moderate to higher complexity, with business development activities that targets Agriculture clients with credit authorizations between $5MM to $35MM and annual sales between $25MM to $100MM. The role is specific to the Core segment of Canadian Business Banking.

As the Senior Client Relationship Manager, you are responsible for ensuring effective relationship management and conducts sales planning and fulfills the execution of service for existing customer base. As well you are also responsible for analysis and completion of credit applications with dedicated support from a Credit Solutions Associate.

 Accountabilities: 

 Champions a customer focused culture to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems and knowledge.

 Promotes the development and profitable growth of the Canadian Agriculture Banking portfolio in the assigned market area by:

- Developing and implementing a marketing strategy to maximize business development opportunities for sustainable growth;

- Developing sales plans for prospects and existing customers;

- Identifying prospects/referrals from other internal/external networks;

- Analyzing prospect lists and prioritizing business development opportunities based on market data and customer analytics; Determining pricing for existing customer relationships in addition to proposed financing for any prospects, ensuring a satisfactory level of profitability for one’s overall book of business;

- Partner with internal resources for non-credit related products

- Referring customers and prospects to the appropriate Canadian Business Banking segment and partners as appropriate.

 Pursues a business development program within the assigned market area according to agreed-upon growth objectives by:

- Direct selling of credit and non-credit commercial products to prospects and customers;

- Maintaining an appropriate ongoing sales pipeline and calling program;

- Identifying and facilitating the involvement of key Bank resources and stakeholders to further business interests

- Maintaining effective follow-up with prospects/referrals on any unsuccessful opportunities

- Updating client or contact information accurately and in a timely fashion

 Builds and maintains a market profile in the assigned market area with both internal and external contacts by;

- Planning and completing relationship activities that generate sales opportunities and/or provide value to clients;

- Building and maintaining an awareness of local market and general economic conditions

- Meeting with business leaders and other centres of influence

- Participating in local professional and community events and associations to develop and expand network of contacts

- Liaising and utilizing Bank product specialists to stay abreast of new enhancements, products and services, and to fulfil identified client needs.

 Ensures all aspects of assigned relationships receive ongoing attention, as required to maintain, improve, grow and retain the relationship by:

- Promoting and encouraging a strong relationship with the Client Service Associate (CSAs);

- Using strong knowledge of the Bank’s streamlined products and services including simplified credit application, standardized and simplified products, standardized pricing and underwriting;

- Actively seeking customer feedback on Bank products and services and the delivery of customer service;

- Liaising with the Shared Services Business Service Centre (BSC) for fulfilment (including documentation, liaising with third parties, security registration), compliance monitoring, and all service activities as required;

- Partnering with internal product specialists on the selling of non-credit products and ensuring customer needs are met

- Action suggestions to continually improve customer satisfaction and processes improvements which may be received directly from clients or through client satisfaction vehicles such as the Pulse. 

 Manage an assigned credit portfolio for authorizations between $5MM to $35MM at an acceptable level of risk by:

- Completing credit reviews in a timely and sufficiently detailed fashion

- Authorizing, renewing or declining customer requests within standard Bank policies and authorized limits, forwarding others as per established processes

- Preparing and/or ensuring all documentation is properly prepared

- Ensuring accounts adhere to the conditions of authorization

- Identifying and resolving deviations from the conditions of authorization

- Ensuring early identification of problem loans and ensuring the accuracy of risk ratings through identification of changes in account quality via review of industry/economic trends;

- Making recommendations relative to structure, monitoring and risk rating to Global Risk Management as issues are identified.  This may include exiting a relationships

 Ensures satisfactory onboarding of clients by:

- Completing diligence to ensure through understanding of the Client’s business and expected business activity and that it aligns with the Bank’s risk tolerance

- Ownership of KYC requirements

- Co-ordinating efforts with the CSA to ensure satisfactory completion of the Client Profile Information documentation, satisfactory resolution of inquiries from the Enhanced Due Diligence Unit and obtaining necessary approvals from Leadership as required

- Ensuring all KYC documentation is properly on file.

 Champion sustainment of the Operating Model by:

-  Taking ownership that activities and behaviours align to roles and responsibilities and adherence to guidelines and processes within the Team.

 Champion and support a culture of diversity and other initiatives aligned with the Bank strategy

Understand how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.

Actively pursues effective and efficient operations of his/her respective areas, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational risk, regulatory compliance risk, AML/ATF risk and conduct risk, including but not limited to responsibilities under the Operational Risk Management Framework, Regulatory Compliance Risk Management Framework, AML/ATF Global Handbook and the Guidelines for Business Conduct.

Champions a high performance environment and contributes to an inclusive work environment

 Education: 

- Undergraduate degree in business or economics or work equivalency

- Other training requirements as determined by the Bank from time to time.

 Skills/Work Experience: 

- Previous work experience of at least 2-5 years in Agricultural Banking is preferred

- Proven strong sales and closing skills

- Very strong networking ability

- Very strong negotiation skills

- Very strong communication and interpersonal skills are essential to this position.  The incumbent must be able to effectively articulate their views both within the Bank and externally in the marketplace

- Strong relationship management skills

- Strong Credit skills and strong experience preparing credit applications

- Strong knowledge of Bank’s commercial lending and deposit products and services, and customer profitability model, in order to provide integrated financial solutions

- Ability to conduct due diligence on the strength of customer financials for deals of moderate to higher complexity

- Thorough knowledge of relationship building and teamwork skills

- The incumbent requires a strong knowledge of the commercial banking marketplace in Canada and a detailed knowledge of the assigned market area’s key industries and competitive positioning within the assigned market area. The incumbent understands the Canadian Business Banking objectives, and has a thorough knowledge of segment, strategies and structure, as well as its lending and deposit products and services

- Good knowledge of Onboarding, Know Your Customer, Anti Money Laundering processes

- Good PC skills are necessary, including a working knowledge of MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and other commercial systems and platforms

- Key Competencies include: Customer Focus, Communication, Results Focus, Building Strategic Relationships, Strategic Influencing and Self-Awareness & Personal Development

- Ability to work non-standard hours as required

- Ability to regularly travel within the assigned territory is required - Must have own reliable transportation

successfactors:jobs.scotiabank.com:60403.description:
Requisition ID: 265906 

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 The Senior UI/UX Engineer will design and build an exceptional internal developer experience by executing a consolidated Internal Developer Portal on Backstage. This role blends user experience (UX) leadership with hands-on UI engineering to integrate multiple existing portals and developer tools into a single, consistent "control pane" for engineering teams. By unifying workflows, discovery, and self-service experiences across the software delivery lifecycle, the role will measurably reduce friction for developers, improve onboarding, and accelerate product delivery at scale.

Reporting to the Director & Head, Developer Enablement, the Senior UI/UX Engineer will partner closely with platform engineering, developer productivity, and tool owners to translate developer needs into intuitive journeys, scalable interaction patterns, and high-quality Backstage user interfaces and plugins. The focus is pragmatic and outcome-driven: build a portal that is simple, reliable, and “good enough” to meaningfully improve productivity, while establishing a strong foundation for iterative enhancement and expanded capabilities over time. 

 Is this role right for you? In this role, you will: 

- Lead discovery and UX design for an Internal Developer Portal, translating developer needs into clear user journeys, information architecture, and prioritized experiences.

- Engineer and deliver Backstage frontend capabilities (pages, components, and plugins) using modern web engineering practices (e.g., React, TypeScript), ensuring a consistent and maintainable experience.

- Integrate and consolidate multiple existing portals and developer experiences into a unified Backstage platform, harmonizing navigation, design patterns, and interaction standards.

- Partner with Developer Productivity and Analytics tool owners to surface actionable insights, status, and operational signals within the portal in a way that is intuitive and decision-supportive.

- Establish and evolve a lightweight design system for the portal, including reusable UI components, accessibility-aware patterns, and documented standards that support scale and speed.

- Conduct iterative user validation (e.g., interviews, usability testing, and lightweight analytics) and drive continuous improvements based on evidence and feedback.

- Collaborate with backend/platform engineers to define integration patterns, APIs, and data contracts that support responsive, reliable, and secure user experiences.

- Ensure high-quality delivery through strong engineering discipline: code quality, performance considerations, testing strategy, documentation, and operational readiness.

- Influence the broader Developer Enablement strategy by identifying experience gaps, proposing pragmatic solutions, and helping define a roadmap that improves developer self-service and reduces cognitive load.

- Contribute to a high-performing team culture through mentoring, design and code reviews, and sharing best practices (without direct people management responsibilities).

 Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have: 

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design, or a related discipline (or equivalent practical experience).

- 7+ years of combined experience in UI engineering and UX design for complex web applications, platforms, or internal tooling.

- Demonstrated experience building internal developer platforms/portals, engineering enablement products, or workflow-driven enterprise applications.

- Strong proficiency with modern frontend engineering (React, TypeScript, HTML/CSS), component design, and state management patterns.

- Experience with design systems and scalable UI patterns; familiarity with accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG) and inclusive design.

- Comfort working across ambiguous problem spaces, balancing pragmatic delivery with user-centered design, and influencing stakeholders through clear communication.

- Experience collaborating with platform, DevOps, or SRE teams and integrating with developer tools (CI/CD, observability, service catalogs, documentation).

 What's in it for you? 

- Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.

- Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.  

- Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.

- Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.

successfactors:jobs.scotiabank.com:60388.description:
Requisition ID : 265878 

 At Tangerine, we’re redefining banking. As Canada’s leading digital bank, we thrive on innovation, agility, and bold thinking, tackling every challenge head-on with leading technology and the unstoppable power of collaboration.  

 Our client-obsessed teams deliver flexible, accessible banking solutions, breakthrough products, and award-winning service. Beyond banking, we’re committed to making an impact in the communities we serve and across our organization. We foster a culture built on integrity, inclusion, and fearless ambition – where diverse perspectives are valued, and people are empowered to do their best work.  

 Are you ready to disrupt the status quo? Do you crave challenges that push boundaries? If you’re a high performer looking to accelerate your career and reimagine the banking landscape, this is your moment.  

 Let’s shape the future of banking together!  

 Our design team is growing, and we're looking for an experienced Mobile Product Designer to join our innovative and collaborative team. We live and breathe product design and thrive on creating user experiences that truly stand out. If you have dedicated your craft at turning research into designs that people love, you're the one we want. 

 Is this role right for you? - In this role you will: 

- You possess a deep understanding of mobile native UI patterns, the nuances of user expectations between iOS and Android, and the latest trends in mobile design. 

- You'll take the lead in enhancing our product's usability and accessibility, ensuring topnotch experiences for our users.  

- You will elicit designs based on business requirements and align the creative strategy and client experience across product, design, and development teams. 

- Conducting studies on usability, interaction, visual design, content, and information architecture is your forte. 

- Your design decisions will be driven by principles, customer insights, data, and business acumen. 

- Collaboration is second nature to you, whether it’s working with business stakeholders, fellow designers, or functional teams. 

- You'll play a key role in evolving the Tangerine Design System, championing a mobilefirst design approach while understanding how to scale solutions across channels. 

- You have knowledge of accessibility best practices, ensuring inclusive design solutions for all users. 

- You are skilled at planning design activities, setting expectations for timelines, and balancing creativity with constraints. 

- Your mission is to shape, influence, and nurture Tangerine design community of practice 

 Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? - We'd love to work with you if you have: 

- You bring 5+ years of experience in crafting native mobile applications. 

- Your talent lies in creating intuitive experiences that are both accessible and aesthetically stunning. 

- You’ve not only worked with design systems—you’ve actively contributed to evolving and maturing them. 

- Your portfolio is a treasure trove of wireframes, high-fidelity mockups, and conceptual explorations that lead to final solutions. 

- You are the go-to expert for mobile user interface best practices. 

- Your toolbox includes Figma and Miro, and you excel at creating interactive prototypes, micro-animations, and conducting usability studies to gather user insights. 

- You know the standard UI frameworks and guidelines for iOS and Android inside and out. 

- Quality is your motto; you are a master of annotations and handoffs, and you are meticulous in design QA. 

- Your communication skills are top-notch, enabling you to work smoothly with developers and stakeholders. 

- If you have experience in a financial institution or a related field, that’s an added bonus. 

 What's in it for you? 

- You will be part of a diverse and inclusive team of Client-focused go-getters looking to learn from each other in an environment that celebrates and recognizes success! 

- You’ll get to work closely with our OMNI-Channel Product Design team through design jams, studio visits, and socials. 

- You will have access to thousands of online and in person courses so you can shape your career growth with the support from diverse industry leaders. 

- This role is hybrid, providing flexibility in your work setup. However, you should be able to come to our office at least once a week to maximize collaboration. 

- While we maintain two physical office locations in downtown Toronto and North York, our designers also have the flexibility to work from various Scotia campuses across Canada. 

- We offer competitive rewards, performance bonuses, Share Ownership Program, and Pension Plan Matching. 

- You get health benefits from day one. 

- Work-life balance, team events, and community volunteer opportunities await. 

- You will enjoy workspace flexibility and all the excitement that comes from working at the official Bank of the Toronto Raptors.

successfactors:jobs.scotiabank.com:60148.description:
Requisition ID: 257895

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 As a Financial Planner, you will focus on developing and deepening mass affluent client relationships by providing high quality advice and service. As a dedicated entrepreneur, you know how to build and leverage your external / internal networks and centres of influence and understand that growing a practice is all about building new and long-term relationships.

 External clients  – As a Financial Planner you engage in proactive client outreach to individuals outside the Scotiabank network, showcasing the unique value a Financial Planner brings to their financial journey. Through meaningful conversations and tailored guidance, the goal is to demonstrate how expert financial planning can empower clients to clarify, pursue, and ultimately achieve their financial objectives—no matter where they are starting from.

 Internal clients  – As a Financial Planner, you play a pivotal role in deepening client relationships by identifying and engaging with existing Scotiabank clients who may have limited interaction with the bank. You proactively mine opportunities and cultivate meaningful connections, positioning yourself as a trusted advisor. By building strong internal partnerships across the branch network, you ensure seamless access to the full breadth of Scotiabank’s resources—bringing the best of the bank to every client interaction.

 As a Financial Planner you are:

- Driven by purpose and determination, you understand that your clients are your most valuable asset. Your top priority is delivering personalized investment and financial planning advice that empowers them to achieve their unique financial goals with confidence.

- You also enjoy the flexibility of being able to meet clients outside of the office, on a schedule that best suits you and them.

- You recognize the value of working within a collective Scotiabank framework that benefits both your clients and your practice overall. 

 Following a comprehensive financial planning framework, you will be responsible for the following:

- Driving investment sales and new client acquisition, while adhering to Global Sales Principles, compliance and regulatory requirements.

- Establish business development opportunities with prospects and clients within the assigned market area.

- Join a purpose-driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

 Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:  

 Promote the development and sustainable growth of proprietary investment business in the assigned market area by:

- Business Development: Executing on business development plans for mass affluent prospects and existing clients. Identifying additional business development opportunities and facilitating the implementation of an investment solution and/or referral to the appropriate partners. 

- Client-centricity: Providing client-centric investment solutions through a financial planning framework, aligning with Global Sales Principles. Conducting outbound communications and proactive calling to prospects to remain top-of-mind for future business opportunities. Conducting complimentary needs analysis across several financial statements, including competitor statements.

- Community Involvement: Participating actively in local professional and community events and associations and identifying opportunities to deliver community information sessions and financial seminars to develop and expand your network and develop prospects. Building and maintaining a market profile in the assigned market area. Networking with investment industry specialists while managing a small budget for independent marketing-based activities. 

 Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We’d love to work with you if you have: 

- 3-years of experience in financial planning and investment sales. 

- You’re a mutual fund certified professional with current accreditation and good standing for CIRO licensing requirements (Investments Funds in Canada or Canadian Securities Course). 

- You have successfully completed a Personal Financial Planning (PFP®) designation and/or a Certified Financial Planner (CFP®) designation. 

- Proven networking, client acquisition and interpersonal skills; experience building and maintaining Centres of Influence (COIs). 

- You’re goal-oriented and entrepreneurial. You can work independently as a self-motivated entrepreneur with minimal supervision and as part of a larger team. 

- Extensive knowledge of competitive offerings, market trends, economic conditions, and the regulatory environment. 

- A valid driver's license and access to a vehicle, to meet clients and prospects within the designated district.

 What’s in it for you?  

- An entrepreneurial culture with the freedom to develop your career. 

- A fast-paced, flexible work environment where you can set your own hours and meet clients when and where it’s convenient.

- A compensation structure that rewards growing and maintaining your client base.

- Access to leading-edge resources to support your growth, including dedicated marketing support, powerful mobile technology, leading customer relationship management (CRM), portfolio, and financial planning software. 

- The ability to build long-lasting client relationships through exceptional advice and service.

- A partnership with our retail branches and access to Scotia Global Asset Management to deliver an excellent client experience. 

- A work culture that promotes diversity, respect, and inclusion. 

 Other Information 

 Please note that the compensation structure for this role is base plus variable pay. This is a mobile role and will require frequent travel. 

 Another stream to our financial planning advice lays within the Canadian Retail Banking Division. This role is called Financial Advisor, Investment & Retirement (FAIR). If you are interested in learning more about this role, please review the “Financial Advisor, Investment & Retirement, Branch Network” posting.

Requisition ID: 270329 

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 Join a winning team at Scotiabank! Are you enthusiastic about making an impact for Canadian businesses? In Canadian Commercial Banking, we do not just serve businesses - we serve possibilities. 

 About the Opportunity: 

 As a Client Relationship Manager (CRM) within Canadian Commercial Banking at Scotiabank, you will play a key role in supporting the success of Canadian businesses in the growth segment with annual sales between $5MM and $25MM. You will drive both new business acquisition and portfolio growth, leveraging strong relationship management, financial insight, and collaboration with internal partners to deliver the full capabilities of the Bank. 

 In this role, you are a trusted advisor to your clients, helping them navigate opportunities and solve business challenges, while building a high-performing portfolio and a strong presence in your market. 

 How You Will Make an Impact: 

- Build trusted relationships with Canadian businesses, acting as a key advisor on their growth and financial needs. 

- Drive new business and expand your portfolio through proactive prospecting, networking, and pipeline management. 

- Deliver tailored banking solutions by connecting clients to the full capabilities of Scotiabank. 

- Lead insightful client conversations leveraging financial analysis and market knowledge to uncover opportunities. 

- Partner across the Bank to bring integrated solutions to our clients. 

- Manage and grow a commercial portfolio , balancing relationship development with sound credit and risk practices. 

- Identify emerging clients, portfolio, or operational risks and escalate concerns appropriately to support sound decision-making and strong portfolio health. 

- B ring together the right partners across the Bank to develop coordinated client solutions. 

- Lead and shape deal structuring and credit execution in partnership with credit teams for authorizations between $1MM to $5MM. 

- Contribute to deal structuring and execution in collaboration with credit partners. 

- Build your presence in the local market through community engagement and industry networking. 

 What You will Bring to the Team: 

 Must-have 

- Education : Undergraduate, degree in Business or Economics or work equivalency. 

- Experience : 3+ years within Commercial Banking and business development in the banking/financial industry. 

- Proven ability to drive business development , including prospecting, pipeline management, negotiation, and closing opportunities. 

- An initiative-taking, self-starter approach with strong organization, prioritization, and networking skills in a fast-paced environment. 

- Ability to lead client conversations in a clear and compelling way. 

- Sound credit and risk judgement , with the ability to balance growth and responsible decision-making. 

- Strong financial acumen , with the ability to understand client needs and deliver tailored solutions. 

- Ability to travel within the assigned market, with access to a vehicle. 

 Nice-to-have 

- Establishing a network within the local business and professional community. 

- Strong  knowledge of commercial lending and deposit products , with the ability to deliver integrated financial solutions. 

- Experience  working with small to mid-sized commercial clients in a relationship management or business development capacity. 

- Familiarity with financial analysis and credit structuring for commercial lending opportunities. 

- Understanding of local market dynamics and key industries within your region. 

 What’s in it for You? 

 When you join the bank, you are not just taking a job, you’re becoming part of a culture that values inclusion, accountability, integrity, and client-centricity – that is our ScotiaBond which is the foundation for how we support our people and deliver for our clients . 

As an employee in Canadian Commercial Banking at Scotiabank, you can expect: 

- A competitive Total Rewards package including performance-based bonuses, flexible benefits, and market-leading compensation. 

- Ongoing career development and coaching from experienced leaders, with clear opportunities to grow within Commercial Banking and across Scotiabank. 

- The chance to own and grow a high-impact client portfolio , with real accountability and visibility in your market. 

- A dynamic, collaborative, and high-performing team that values partnership, inclusion, and shared success. 

- Exposure to a broad range of industries, clients, and complex financial solutions, accelerating your learning and expertise. 

 Ready to Apply: 

 If you are ready to take your commercial banking career to the next level and make an impact, start the next chapter of your career story with us and apply today and help shape the future of Canadian business.

successfactors:jobs.scotiabank.com:60548.description:

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture. 

 Start the next chapter of your career with us!

 Make a meaningful difference in the financial lives of clients while building a career with room to grow. Join a collaborative team where you can deepen trusted relationships, expand your network and help clients move toward their goals with confidence.

 One application. Two potential career paths.

 Choose the path that fits your strengths and ambitions:

 Financial Advisor, Investment & Retirement Planning | Retail Banking: 

 Help clients make informed decisions about investments, retirement and everyday banking. You will manage and grow a portfolio of clients, strengthen existing relationships and connect with clients referred by branch partners. This path may be a strong fit if you enjoy working as part of a branch team, developing business and delivering advice that supports clients over time.

 Financial Planner | Scotia Financial Planning, Global Wealth Management: 

 Build and grow a financial planning practice by delivering personalized investment and financial planning advice to mass-affluent clients. You will cultivate long-term relationships, develop internal and external networks and meet clients in ways that support both their needs and your schedule. This path may be a strong fit if you bring an entrepreneurial mindset and enjoy building a practice through trusted advice and relationships.

 What will help you succeed: 

- At least 3 years of experience in financial planning, investment sales or wealth management. 

- Current mutual fund accreditation in good standing and alignment with applicable CIRO licensing requirements, such as Investment Funds in Canada or the Canadian Securities Course. 

- Completion of, or progress toward, the Institute of Financial Planning diploma leading to the F.Pl. designation. 

- A client-first approach, strong relationship-building skills and a genuine interest in helping people achieve their financial goals. 

- Confidence in business development, networking and working toward goals. 

 Language requirement: 

 In addition to French, sufficient knowledge of English is required because the work involves regular interaction and collaboration with groups and individuals based in Toronto, as well as ongoing interaction with English-speaking clients and colleagues locally and elsewhere.

 Ready to take the next step? 

 Apply today to explore where your experience, interests and career goals may align across our Financial Planning opportunities in Quebec.

ashby:semperis:83c28adf-9572-4b2e-a9b4-1.description:
At Semperis, our mission is to be a Force for Good. Starting with being a great place to work. We believe that when people feel valued, supported, and empowered, they do their best work. That’s why we focus on creating an employee experience rooted in purpose, growth, and balance. Semperis has been recognized as one of America’s Fastest-Growing Cybersecurity Companies by the Inc. 5000, a DUNS 100 Top Startup to Work For, and a multi-year Inc. Best Workplace awardee.



Do you live and breathe identity security, least‑privilege, and AI? Do you have a vision for how technology could make it dramatically easier for enterprises to understand “who can do what where” and keep privileges in check across hybrid environments—especially as agentic AI and non‑human identities explode?

Semperis is seeking an experienced Product Manager to lead our Permissions & Delegation Hygiene (Least‑Privilege Enforcement) area. This is a high‑impact domain with fast‑growing customer demand: every organization in the world struggles with over‑permissioned accounts, complex delegations, AI‑driven automation, and hard‑to‑explain access paths. You can be the leader who turns that pain into a flagship, market‑leading product experience, using graph, analytics, and AI‑assisted workflows to help customers get to and stay at least‑privilege.

If you bring real‑world experience in identity security, IAM, or privileged access—and strong instincts for where AI should automate and where humans must stay in the loop—you’ll immediately see the value of this space and know how to steer it.

 You’ll set product vision and strategy for this area, collaborate closely with engineering, design, and go‑to‑market partners, and work directly with customers to deliver solutions that reduce privilege sprawl for both human and machine identities.




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Define and execute the product strategy and roadmap for permissions and delegation hygiene, including how we leverage graph and AI to help customers understand effective access and clean it up safely.

 - Engage deeply with customers and prospects (CISOs, identity architects, AD/Entra/Okta owners, IAM/PAM teams) to understand their workflows around privilege management, service accounts, and AI/automation, and translate them into clear product priorities.

 - Collaborate closely with engineering and design to shape end‑to‑end experiences for understanding effective access, reducing excessive privilege, and supporting review and remediation workflows—with explainable, human‑in‑the‑loop AI assistance where it adds real value.

 - Partner with sales, marketing, and customer success on positioning, messaging, demos, and launches, acting as the subject‑matter expert for this product area.

 - Work with data/AI engineering teams to define and iterate on AI‑powered capabilities (e.g., risk scoring, recommendations, prioritization, copilots, or automation) while maintaining safety, transparency, and customer trust.

 - Conduct ongoing competitive and market analysis in identity security, IAM/IGA, PAM, and AI‑driven identity/agent governance to identify trends and opportunities, and use these insights to inform product decisions.

 - Manage the full product lifecycle—from concept and discovery through launch and post‑launch iteration—using data and customer feedback to guide continuous improvement.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TABLE:

 - Proven ability to deliver effective technology solutions in complex B2B environments.

 - Demonstrated product management (or closely related) experience in software, with substantial time in security, identity, or infrastructure domains.

 - Strong domain experience in at least one of the following:
   
   1- Identity security posture or ITDR.
   
   2- IAM/IGA or directory services (e.g., Active Directory, Entra ID, Okta).
   
   3- Privileged access management, least‑privilege enforcement, or delegation/role management.

 - Familiarity with non‑human identities and AI‑driven workloads (e.g., service principals, managed identities, API keys, agentic AI, automation frameworks) and how their permissions are governed.

 - Solid understanding of concepts like least‑privilege, role‑based access control, and effective rights in large enterprises, including how AI and automation can both reduce and amplify risk.

 - Demonstrated experience working on technically deep products in close partnership with senior engineers and architects, including some hands-on prototyping of workflows or product experiences using generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, or similar); experience collaborating with data/ML/AI teams is a plus.

 - Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills with a data‑driven approach to decision‑making.

 - Outstanding communication and presentation skills; able to convey complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and executive audiences.

What we're looking for:

Semperis is hiring a Sales Compensation Analyst to join our finance team!

Why this role matters

Sales, channel, renewals, BDR, and corporate bonus participants across Semperis count on being paid correctly and on time. As our Senior Sales Compensation Analyst, you'll own the system and the monthly cycle that make that happen. You'll run calculations in Xactly Incent, tie every result back to its source data, and give Finance a close it can trust. The hardest part of the job is judgment: knowing when a variance is a data fix you can make yourself, and when it's a plan question that needs a leader's approval before anything moves.

What you'll own

 - Run the recurring commission and incentive calculation cycle, from source data validation to an approved payment file delivered to Payroll within the monthly close window.

 - Investigate and resolve discrepancies in assignments, splits, credits, quotas, rates, currencies, and adjustments, and document every true up and correction before payment is released.

 - Reconcile Xactly Incent against Salesforce, HR, payroll, and Finance systems each month and quarter, and support close, including commission accruals, in partnership with our Revenue Analyst.

 - Build and maintain audit ready documentation and controls so the commission process is repeatable and any reviewer can follow it.

 - Administer Xactly Incent across all company plans, keeping participant data, access, hierarchies, quotas, rates, and plan assignments current as people join, move, and leave.

 - Lead the annual implementation of every compensation plan in Xactly, working with Revenue Operations and the Global Compensation Director through configuration, testing, and approvals.

 - Own plan letter administration end to end, from preparation and issuance through signature tracking.

 - Turn large datasets into clear reporting on attainment, commissions, and payments, and help managers and employees understand their plans and statements, including findings they may not want to hear.

What success looks like

 - Every cycle closes on time, with an approved payment file and every discrepancy investigated and documented before sign off.

 - Each period ties out across systems, with variances explained and evidence ready for auditors.

 - Every approved plan is configured, tested, and live before the plan year opens, and every participant holds a current signed plan letter.

 - Participants understand their statements, and disputes are resolved with facts rather than escalation.

Who you'll work with

You'll report to our Director of Finance and work closely with the CFO, Revenue Operations leaders and plan owners, and department heads across sales and channel. You'll also partner with HR, Legal, Payroll, Accounting, FP&A, our Xactly technical account manager, and external auditors.

What you'll bring

 - 3-5 years of relevant experience in incentive compensation or commission operations

 - Hands on experience administering Xactly Incent, including plan configuration, participant data, hierarchies, quotas, and rates

 - Strong reconciliation skills, with a track record of tracing variances to root cause across multiple systems

 - Advanced Excel, including formulas, pivot tables, and lookups

 - Experience maintaining documented procedures and audit evidence

 - Clear, steady communication when explaining plan mechanics or delivering unwelcome findings

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Nice to have

 - Experience with Workday and NetSuite

 - Experience supporting global incentive programs across multiple countries or currencies

 - Experience in a public company, high tech or SaaS environment,

 - Familiarity with US GAAP including ASC 606, and background in variable pay payroll, Sales or Revenue Operations, accounting, audit or financial analysis.

At Shakepay, we’re on a mission to usher in the Bitcoin golden age. We’re reimagining financial services to give every Canadian their fair shake.

 Our culture is built around doing work that matters, winning as a team, and celebrating success. If you're the kind of person who values growth, shipping fast, and sharing your ideas openly with a group of like-minded people, come and build with us!

 About Shakepay

 Since 2015, we've been on a mission to help Canadians build long-term wealth through bitcoin. Over the past few years, we've expanded beyond buying and selling bitcoin to offer a growing suite of everyday financial products - including the Shakepay Card, direct deposit, bill payments and Interac e-Transfer - making it easier to earn, save and use bitcoin every day. Today, more than 1.5 million Canadians use Shakepay to grow their bitcoin savings and take control of their financial future as we continue to push the boundaries of what modern financial services can look like.

 We’re regulated as an investment dealer across all Canadian provinces and territories, and backed by renowned venture capitalists with a funding of $44M. We have a passionate, loyal, and growing community, and we’re looking for people who want to help us build something truly special.

 About the team

 The Legal team sits at the center of some of Shakepay’s most important decisions. We partner closely with Product, Compliance, Operations, Finance, People, and leadership to bring new products to market, navigate complex regulatory questions and help the business move quickly with confidence. We believe ownership over hierarchy, practical judgment over perfection, and using technology and AI to rethink how legal work gets done.

 About the role

 As Senior Legal Counsel, you’ll help shape how millions of Canadians interact with money. You’ll work alongside product, compliance and executive leadership to solve novel legal questions at the intersection of crypto, payments and financial regulation. This is a hands-on role for someone who can navigate ambiguity, provide practical recommendations and wants to help build - not just protect - the business.

 What you’ll be doing

- Partner with Product, Compliance and business teams to help design and launch new products, translating complex legal and regulatory requirements into practical solutions.

- Advise on a broad range of legal and regulatory matters across securities, AML/ATF, payments, consumer protection and other areas impacting Shakepay's business.

- Lead regulatory initiatives, including supporting examinations, audits, licensing work, policy development and engagement with regulators.

- Provide practical, business-oriented advice to leaders across the company, helping teams navigate ambiguity and make informed decisions while balancing legal, regulatory and operational considerations.

- Identify opportunities to leverage AI, automation and scalable processes to improve how legal work gets done and enable the business to move faster.

- Support the team on a variety of other legal matters as needed, including commercial agreements, corporate governance, employment and strategic projects.

 Who we’re looking for

- Canadian-qualified lawyer with 5+ years of experience, ideally in fintech, payments, financial services, crypto, or a fast-moving technology company.

- Able to operate independently in a lean team, make decisions with incomplete information, and move work forward without heavy oversight.

- Business-oriented legal judgment: you start from the product or business outcome, then help the team understand risk, options, and a recommended path.

- Comfortable advising product and operational teams directly, including on ambiguous questions where there may not be a perfect answer.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn complex legal issues into clear, practical guidance for non-legal stakeholders.

 Bonus points

- Experience working across both a law firm and an in-house legal team.

- Experience in a startup or scaleup environment where priorities change quickly and legal support needs to be pragmatic.

- Familiarity with Bitcoin, crypto, securities, payments, AML, or regulated financial products in Canada.

- Experience using AI, automation, or lightweight tooling to improve legal work product and team efficiency.

 Why join us?

- Help shape the future of money: Be part of a team that's revolutionizing financial services in Canada, one sat at a time.

- Impact millions: As cryptocurrency continues to gain traction, our potential for growth is massive. You can help us bring Shakepay and Bitcoin to all Canadians.

- Grow your career: We’re growing, and so can you! We have programs in place to encourage continuous learning, growth, and development.

- Ideas, not titles: We want the best ideas to make their way through, no matter where they come from.

 Perks and benefits

- 🤝 Be an owner: Every employee has stock options as part of their total compensation.

- 🥅 Reach your goals: Develop with continuous feedback and quarterly performance and compensation review.

- 🦷 Health & wellness: Access to health and dental coverage, including health and wellness spending accounts.

- 🌎 Remote-friendly: Work from anywhere in Canada, with optional access to our office spaces in Montreal and Toronto.

- 🆙 Level Up: A $2,000 annual budget for courses, certifications, and training to support your career growth.

- 🌴 Time off: 20 days of vacation per year. And if you use all your vacation, we give you a $1,000 bonus.

- 🐣 Parental leave: Enjoy a parental leave top up to 100% of your salary for 18 weeks.

- 🙌 Have fun together: quarterly team-specific or company-wide offsite to connect with each other.

 The base salary range for this position is $200,000 - $240,000 CAD. The base salary may vary based on factors such as years of experience, skills and qualifications. Additionally, employees are eligible for equity, pay increases based on performance, benefits including health and dental care, and paid time off.

 We understand that potential can be just as valuable as experience. If you're eager to learn, grow, and contribute to the mission but worry that you may not have the “right” experience, we still want you to apply. We encourage applications from everyone, regardless of background and life experience. We’re firm believers that a little bit of slope makes up for a lot of y-intercept.

 We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support certain parts of our hiring process. This can include tools that assist with scheduling, application review, candidate communications, and generating interview notes, guides, or summaries so our team can stay focused on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.

 Fluency in English is required due to the percentage of English-speaking customers and the nature of our platform, which is available to all Canadians.

At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Support our team culture by working in the office 4 days a week (Monday - Thursday). This means you’ll have to live within commuting distance of the office you’ll be working in.

Snowflake is seeking motivated people with a passion for technology and the drive to build an incredible career in SaaS sales. The Sales Development team plays a critical role in the growth of our organization. Our team works in collaboration with sales and marketing nurturing leads and setting qualified discovery calls that ultimately lead to new business and new revenue.




IN THIS ROLE YOU GET TO:

 - Build revenue pipeline by setting introductory meetings with target influencers and key decision makers

 - Research and build new and existing accounts through rigorous outbound calling efforts and by creating/executing strategic email and social campaigns

 - Perform analysis of inbound and outbound prospects’ business and engage with these prospects by phone and/or email

 - Apply effective communication skills, collaborating directly with customers, sales and cross functional teams

 - Work in a fast-pace environment, take the initiative to get stuff done, try new things and amplify your successes by sharing your findings with your team


ON DAY ONE WE WILL EXPECT YOU TO HAVE:

 - A passion for technology and software sales, 1-2 years of customer facing experience is preferred

 - Ability to develop strong, long-lasting relationships (both internal and external),

 - A sense of urgency and ability to manage time and prioritize tasks

 - The ability to thrive in a company environment of rapid change; reacting to management initiatives; taking the "customer view"; adopting customer corporate ‘perspective’; accepting change to business/personal situations

 - Resourcefulness and results driven operating style

 - Collaborative and coachable mindset - you should be excited about continuously improving your skills and impact


AND MOST IMPORTANTLY THE ABILITY TO REPRESENT SNOWFLAKE AND THE VALUES WE STAND FOR:

 - Fire in the Belly: The hustle to put in time and energy and to have resilience

 - Win as a Team: Can collaborate in a team environment

 - Get it Done: The ability to meet and exceed metrics and sales quotas

 - Own It: The ability to build our product and company like it’s your own, specifically defining and executing sales plans to meet strategic & financial targets, leveraging industry, partner & Go-to-Market knowledge

 - Integrity, Always: This ability to provide open, honest and respectful feedback creating an inclusive work environment

 - Think Big: Ambition to meet our big goals. Create a strategy to focus on what matters while making a positive impact and lasting difference

 - Be Excellent: Lead by example, doing your best work every day

 - A Desire to Make Each Other Better: Resulting in long standing relationships with internal cross functional partners and the ability to create an inclusive work environment

 - Embrace Each Other’s Differences: A passion for developing a diverse and inclusive environment of sales professionals from all backgrounds

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com

Location: Canada | Eastern or Atlantic Timezone
Department: Revenue Operations
Department Leader: Michael Scott | Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) https://www.linkedin.com/in/michael-s-a9938860/
Type: Permanent | Full-Time
Vacancy Status: This is an active, approved role and we are currently hiring for this position.




ABOUT SOLINK

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 30,000 locations across 32+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!




THE ROLE

The Senior Manager, Marketing Operations is a crucial member of our Revenue Operations (RevOps), Go-to-Market, and Demand Generation teams — responsible for ensuring the smooth operation and scalability of our marketing and lead-generation infrastructure. This person will focus heavily on data integrity, and will work continuously to improve our lead acquisition process to support overall growth. In this role, you’ll play a pivotal part in bridging marketing, sales, and operations to help drive revenue and growth.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Provide regular reporting, analytics, and insights to key business partners across marketing, sales, and leadership — enabling data-driven decisions.

 - Maintain and optimize the foundations of the HubSpot account, ensuring that marketing, sales, and customer data architecture are robust, scalable, and aligned with business needs.

 - Own the strategy and execution of Solink’s campaign architecture and reporting in SalesForce, along with integrations with HubSpot to ensure accuracy

 - Support broader revenue-tech (RevTech) operations — including CRM integration, lead-flow optimization, data hygiene, campaign set-up and tracking, and cross-functional collaboration.

 - Act as a “go-to” resource for a wide range of requests related to revenue-driving activities — from ad-hoc analytics and dashboards to process improvements and technical implementations.

 - Collaborate closely with Demand Gen, Sales Ops, and Go-to-Market teams to ensure lead acquisition and distribution processes are efficient, accurate, and optimized for performance.

 - Identify inefficiencies and areas for improvement across marketing operations, then propose and implement solutions to streamline processes and improve performance.
   
   


WHAT YOU BRING

Must-Have:

 - Strong ability to prioritize tasks and manage time effectively — able to balance multiple responsibilities across reporting, operations, and project execution.

 - Deep understanding of HubSpot and Salesforce— including architecture, CRM setup, workflows, data mapping, and integrations.

 - Strong people and communication skills — capable of managing a team, coordinating across stakeholders, and translating technical/operational issues into clear actions.

 - Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate data into actionable business insights.

 - High proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets (ex: pivot tables, INDEX/MATCH, VLOOKUP, IF statements, filters)

 - A deep understanding of B2B sales, marketing and customer success including process, content and technology; e.g. Marketo, Gong, Hubspot/Salesforce, Outreach/Salesloft, Sales Navigator, Gainsight, etc.

 - Excellent attention to detail, coupled with the ability to see the bigger picture — identify root causes, articulate challenges clearly, and solve problems strategically.

 - Familiarity with CRM systems beyond HubSpot — especially Salesforce — and experience with HubSpot-Salesforce sync is a strong asset.

 - Support M&A due diligence and purchase accounting, if applicable.

 - Provide training and guidance to the broader accounting team on technical topics.

 - Serves as the go-to resource for IFRS interpretation on complex, non-routine transactions for the accounting team and the entire organization

 - Drafts technical accounting memos and position papers with minimal oversight

 - Evaluates new revenue arrangements, leases, or financial instruments for accounting treatment

 - Own Solink’s accounting policy manual

 - Solink accounting policy manual is completed and up to date

 - Clean and efficient annual audit process

 - Solink prepared well in advance of any accounting changes impacting financial reporting

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or related field; CPA or CA required (or in progress).

 - 3-5 years of accounting experience, including public accounting (Big 4 or large regional firm) experience strongly preferred.

 - Deep working knowledge of IFRS, with particular strength in revenue recognition (IFRS 15) and other judgment-heavy areas.

 - Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate research and first-draft memo preparation, with rigorous review and professional judgment applied before finalizing any position.

 - Experience with multi-element or bundled revenue arrangements — hardware/software combined offerings a strong plus.

 - Strong technical writing skills; ability to produce clear, well-supported accounting memos.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-accounting stakeholders (Sales, Legal, Product).

 - Exposure to IFRS reporting.

 - Experience in a hardware-enabled SaaS or similarly complex revenue environment.

 - Experience with multi-entity, multi-currency reporting structures.

This is a quota-carrying, pipeline-generation role responsible for activating Comcast sellers, driving deal registration, running a disciplined co-sell motion with Solink Account Executives and Brand Specialists, and progressing opportunities from initial engagement through pilot and multi-site rollout.

You’ll act as the bridge between Solink and Comcast, building relationships across divisions, regions, and levels of the organization to earn seller mindshare and make Solink easy to sell. You’ll be close to where the selling happens—enabling sellers, coaching live opportunities, coordinating the right Solink resources, and removing friction before it stalls a deal.

Your success will be measured by the partner-sourced pipeline and bookings generated through Comcast, the volume and quality of registered opportunities, and the co-sell revenue you help drive alongside Solink’s sales organization.

 




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Activate Comcast Sellers at Scale: Build seller engagement across Comcast divisions through training, targeted 1:1 enablement, and live opportunity coaching. Help sellers recognize when Solink is a strong fit and confidently introduce the solution to their customers.

 - Drive Partner-Sourced Pipeline & Bookings: Create the cadence, accountability, and joint activity required to consistently generate qualified Comcast-sourced opportunities and convert them into revenue.

 - Own the Deal Registration Motion: Manage deal registration end-to-end, including validating opportunities and site counts, coordinating pricing and approvals, protecting partner opportunities, and removing friction so deals progress efficiently.

 - Run a Disciplined Co-Sell Motion: Partner with Solink Account Executives and Brand Specialists to map Comcast’s install base against target accounts, coordinate joint outreach, clarify ownership throughout the sales process, and keep opportunities moving.

 - Progress Pilots into Rollouts: Coordinate the right resources across Sales Engineering, Customer Success, and other Solink teams to support successful pilots and help Comcast build compelling cases for broader customer expansion.

 - Build Repeatable Brand Plays: Leverage Solink’s approved-vendor relationships and standard pricing within major restaurant brands to develop repeatable franchise plays, penetration strategies, introductions, and joint outreach with Comcast.

 - Deliver World-Class Partner Enablement: Maintain a consistent enablement cadence covering Solink’s platform, vertical positioning, competitive plays, technical fundamentals, sales tools, and escalation paths that keep Comcast sellers confident and unblocked.

 - Forecast, Track & Report Performance: Run structured pipeline reviews with Comcast leadership, maintain accurate CRM and PRM data, and provide clear forecasts and performance updates to Channel and Sales leadership.

 - Deepen Executive Relationships: Lead Quarterly Business Reviews, facilitate executive-sponsor relationships, and drive joint planning that strengthens the partnership and turns strategic alignment into measurable go-to-market execution.

They lead complex initiatives, influence cross-functional outcomes, and use their expertise to raise the effectiveness of those around them.

In this role, you’ll be expected to:

 - Strategically own the Comcast partnership end-to-end, identifying where to focus across divisions, sellers, accounts, and opportunities to maximize partner-sourced pipeline, bookings, and long-term growth.

 - Lead complex co-sell and partner initiatives across Comcast and Solink, proactively anticipating blockers, aligning stakeholders, and providing direction to keep opportunities and joint priorities moving forward.

 - Build trusted relationships from frontline sellers through executive sponsors, influencing Comcast to prioritize Solink and creating strong alignment and accountability around shared goals.

 - Represent the partnership across Solink, bringing forward partner, customer, and market insights to influence Sales, Channel, Marketing, Product, and other cross-functional priorities.

 - Raise the effectiveness of the broader team by sharing channel expertise, coaching others through complex partner opportunities, and continuously improving the frameworks and practices used to execute the Comcast partnership.

 
 

What success looks like:

 - The Comcast partnership consistently delivers against partner-sourced pipeline, bookings, and co-sell revenue goals while building a strong foundation for continued growth.

 - Comcast sellers actively identify, register, and progress Solink opportunities, with successful approaches becoming repeatable across divisions and regions.

 - Complex co-sell opportunities and pilots progress effectively because risks are anticipated, ownership is clear, and the right Comcast and Solink stakeholders are engaged at the right time.

 - Solink has strong relationships across Comcast—from frontline sellers to executive sponsors—and is viewed as a strategic partner rather than simply another product in the portfolio.

 - Joint go-to-market, enablement, and brand plays create measurable results and can be scaled across the Comcast organization rather than relying on one-off execution.

 - Solink leaders and cross-functional teams trust you to represent the Comcast partnership, provide meaningful market insight, and help shape decisions that strengthen the long-term relationship.

 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Experienced Channel Professional: You bring 3–5+ years of experience in channel sales, partner management, or alliances, ideally within physical security, SaaS, networking, or a related technology environment. You’ve carried a number and successfully grown partner-sourced business.

 - Experienced in Large Partner Organizations: You’ve worked within or alongside a telco, ISP, carrier, national integrator, or large MSP and understand how to navigate divisions, regions, and multiple layers of leadership to earn seller attention and engagement.

 - Enablement-Driven Coach: You know how to build training that changes seller behaviour and are comfortable coaching sellers in the moment, including during live customer opportunities.

 - Fluent in Partner Mechanics: Deal registration, co-selling, referral and resale models, MDF and incentives, joint go-to-market planning, and QBRs are familiar territory.

 - Strategic Thinker, Tactical Executor: You can develop a joint partner plan and then execute the hands-on work required to make it successful—from pipeline reviews and deal support to seller activation and follow-through.

 - Comfortable in a Technical Sale: You don’t need to be an engineer, but you can confidently navigate conversations involving cameras, bandwidth, network topology, and integrations—and know when to bring in Sales Engineering.

 - Relationship Builder & Influencer: You can build credibility from frontline sellers through executive sponsors and motivate a large partner organization to prioritize Solink alongside competing solutions.

 - Strong Communicator & Presenter: Whether you’re training a group of sellers, running a QBR, or working through a complex opportunity, you communicate clearly, persuasively, and with the audience in mind.

 - Data-Driven & Process-Oriented: You use CRM and PRM data across pipeline, conversion, forecast, and activity to identify gaps early and determine where action is required.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Solink is looking for a Tax & Treasury Specialist to join our Finance organization. This role starts from a foundation in tax compliance and planning, with the opportunity to grow into treasury responsibilities, including short-term cash forecasting and cash flow management. We're less focused on someone who already has deep treasury experience, and more focused on finding someone with solid core tax fundamentals who is curious, adaptable, and excited to expand into treasury over time.



You'll work closely with the Director of Accounting and cross-functionally with the Accounting, FP&A and Finance Operations teams, as well as our external advisors. Our company reports under IFRS and operates globally, so this role touches multi-jurisdictional tax considerations where you will need to proactively identify tax risks, interpret evolving legislation, and build repeatable processes that minimize risk while supporting business growth.




WHAT YOU’LL DO


TAX COMPLIANCE & PLANNING

 - Prepare and/or support federal, state/provincial, and local tax filings across all legal entities, coordinating with external tax advisors as needed.

 - Support sales/use tax, GST/HST, and VAT compliance across jurisdictions, including monitoring nexus as the business scales — hardware shipments introduce physical nexus considerations beyond typical SaaS.

 - Assist with quarterly and annual tax provision calculations under IFRS, working with the accounting team and external advisors.

 - Use AI tools to accelerate tax law research, first-draft technical memos, and summarize regulatory updates.Research and document tax positions on new products, contract structures, and cross-border transactions between entities.

 - Support tax planning opportunities as they arise (e.g., R&D tax credits, intercompany transfer pricing considerations, jurisdictional structuring).

 - Maintain the tax compliance calendar across all jurisdictions to ensure timely, accurate filings.

 - Help respond to tax notices and support tax audits.

 - Monitor changes in tax law across jurisdictions relevant to the business.


BUSINESS PARTNERSHIP

 - Act as a first point of contact for Sales, Procurement, and Operations on routine tax questions.

 - Review customer and vendor contracts to ensure appropriate tax treatment.

 - Support new market expansion by evaluating tax registration and compliance requirements.

 - Translate complex tax regulations into practical guidance for business stakeholders.


TREASURY & CASH MANAGEMENT

 - Learn and eventually own the short-term (13-week) cash flow forecast, incorporating inputs from AR, AP, payroll, and capital expenditures.

 - Support monitoring of daily cash positions across bank accounts and currencies.

 - Gain exposure to banking relationships, account structures, and treasury tools/platforms.

 - Assist with intercompany funding tracking and foreign currency exposure considerations.

 - Support annual treasury planning and working capital analysis as skills develop.

 - Explore opportunities to use AI tools to speed up variance analysis on the cash forecast (e.g., flagging unusual AR/AP timing) and to automate recurring reconciliation or reporting tasks.




WHAT YOU BRING


MUST-HAVE

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.

 - CPA/CA in progress or completed.

 - 2-4 years of tax compliance experience; multi-jurisdictional exposure a plus but not required.

 - No prior treasury experience required — we're looking for genuine interest in learning cash forecasting and treasury operations.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and picking up new processes; adaptable and curious by nature.

 - Comfortable using AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) to support research, drafting, and analysis — no specific AI experience required, but genuine interest in using these tools to work more efficiently is a plus.

 - Strong Excel skills; exposure to tax software (e.g., Avalara) or ERP systems is a plus.

 - Strong communication skills and comfort working cross-functionally with Accounting, FP&A, and Operations.

 - Detail-oriented and organized, able to manage multiple deadlines.


PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

 - Exposure to IFRS reporting.

 - Experience in a SaaS, hardware, or hybrid hardware/software business.

 - Exposure to multi-entity or multi-currency environments.

 - Experience supporting external audits (financial statement and/or tax).

 - Experience supporting international tax compliance beyond Canada and the United States.

 - Global tax experience, including VAT and other indirect/direct taxes in international jurisdictions such as the EU.
